<a id="grid-L1-r1"></a>

### grid-L1-r1

#### Coverage grid: L1 Access control, round 1

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`. Lens question: who can reach this, and should they? Row ids are
from `inventory.md`. Each cell is **finding** (id below), **holds** (with the reason) or
**n/a** (with the reason).

Evidence key: **R-native** = reproduced by a native test that drives the production
`IcBridge` / `policy` / `mcp` code in a private copy (probe source in the appendix);
**R-live** = reproduced on the local icp-cli network (port 8010) with read-only or no-op
requests (anonymous identity, non-existent hash/principal as arguments); **CP** = the code
path produces it unambiguously. No settings were changed on the live canister.

##### Candidate findings

| Id | Title | Severity | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1-1 | `icp.candid` serves admin overrides (and cached interfaces) without an allowlist check; overrides outlive `remove_allowlist` | Low | R-native |
| L1-2 | Allowlist revocation is not re-checked after the interface-fetch await: a call authorized before `remove_allowlist`/`set_allowlist` narrowing is still sent after it | Medium | CP |
| L1-3 | `set_allowlist` accepts this canister's own principal and `aaaaa-aa` with `"*"`: nested self-runs with fresh budgets, management calls with the canister's authority | Low | R-native (acceptance) + CP (consequence) |
| L1-4 | README says the override is the third interface source; code uses it first, before any fetch (observed under L1; class L16) | Medium | R-native |
| L1-5 | demo_store has no access control: anyone can `cancel_order`/`restock`/`create_order` for any customer, while the README presents them as "blocked" | Low | CP |

Details are in the StructuredOutput of this lens; summary of each:

- **L1-1** `src/bridge.rs:471-480`: `HostBridge::candid` returns `policy::candid_override(&key)`
  and then `cache_get(&key)` before `reserve(&p, None)`, so neither is gated by
  `check_interface_fetch`. `remove_allowlist` (`src/lib.rs:300-304`) evicts the heap caches
  but not `CANDID_OVERRIDES` (D5), and `set_candid_override` accepts any principal (AD7).
  The doc comment at `src/policy.rs:198` says `icp.candid` "may target any allowlisted
  canister". Probe `override_is_served_to_scripts_without_allowlist`: a canister never
  allowlisted, with an override, returns the full override text through `IcBridge::candid`
  and through JS, Python and Rhai scripts, while `icp.call` on it is refused with "not
  allowlisted"; no violation is recorded for the read. Probe `override_survives_remove_allowlist`:
  same after the `remove_allowlist` sequence. Variant (CP): a fetch in flight when
  `remove_allowlist` runs re-inserts `DID_CACHE` after its await (`src/bridge.rs:497-499`),
  so the removed canister's interface is served by `icp.candid` for up to 1 h.
- **L1-2** `src/bridge.rs:510-528`: `call` runs `reserve(&p, Some(method))`, then
  `self.service(&p).await`, which on a cache miss calls `candid` -> `fetch_did`, two
  `bounded_wait` awaits (up to ~300 s each). Other messages (e.g. a controller's
  `remove_allowlist`) execute during those awaits. After them the call is encoded and sent
  with no second policy check. Same inside `fetch_did` (`src/bridge.rs:424-436`): the
  fallback `__get_candid_interface_tmp_hack` is sent to `p` after the
  `canister_metadata` await without re-checking `p`. A run's bearer token is checked once
  per HTTP request (`src/mcp.rs:375`), so `revoke_api_token_hash` does not stop a run in
  flight either (up to `max_calls_per_script` more messages, possibly much later with
  unbounded waits).
- **L1-3** `src/lib.rs:295-298`, `src/policy.rs:155-157`: no validation of the principal.
  Probe `any_principal_can_be_allowlisted_including_management_and_self_like_ids`: with
  `"*"`, `check_call` admits `aaaaa-aa.update_settings`, `aaaaa-aa.delete_canister`, and
  `<self>.http_request_update`. Consequences by code path: a self-call to
  `http_request_update` carrying the caller's token passes `mcp::authenticate` (inter-canister
  calls skip `inspect_message`, `src/lib.rs:270-272`) and starts a nested run with its own
  `IcBridge` (fresh 25-call cap, fresh instruction budget in a new call context, its own
  `run_id`, not linked to the outer run), bounded only by the 8 run slots for depth;
  sequential fan-out is up to 25 per level. Admin endpoints stay closed: the canister is
  not its own controller (R-live: controllers = one user principal), so the guard refuses.
  The README warns about none of this.
- **L1-4** `README.md:493-496` vs `src/bridge.rs:207-212, 439-443, 475-477`. Probe
  `override_is_used_before_any_fetch_even_when_allowlisted`: an allowlisted canister with
  an override returns the override without attempting a send (a send would hit the ic0
  stub and panic natively).
- **L1-5** `demo_store/src/lib.rs:277-337` has no caller check and no `inspect_message`;
  `create_order` takes `customer` as an argument. `README.md:168-171` and
  `scripts/demo-setup.sh:3` say `cancel_order` and `restock` "stay blocked"; that holds only
  through `icp_code_mode`.

##### Not tested, and why

- L1-2 and the L1-3 consequences need `remove_allowlist`/`set_allowlist` on a live
  network during an in-flight fetch, or allowlisting the canister itself; both change
  settings, which this phase may not do. A Live-phase test: allowlist demo_store with
  `create_order`, start a script that calls it with a cold interface cache, call
  `remove_allowlist` while the fetch is pending, then check demo_store's order count and
  the audit `methods`.
- `IcBridge` paths that send messages cannot run natively (ic0 stubs panic, register #58);
  only the no-send paths and the policy decision before the send were exercised.
- Calls to `http_request_update` and admin methods from another canister (A8) were not
  made: no caller canister is deployed and creating one changes the network.
- `set_limits` and `set_candid_override` were not probed live as non-controllers: no
  argument is a guaranteed no-op if the guard were broken.
- `canister_metadata` returning private metadata when this canister is a controller of the
  target was not examined (needs a controlled target).

##### Appendix: probe source (private copy, `src/l1_audit_tests.rs`, added as `#[cfg(test)] mod`)

Run: `cargo test --lib l1_audit` with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` shared; 7 passed. The shared target
directory is reused by other agents with the same package hash, so the test binary was
copied out right after building before it was run.

```rust
const X: &str = "ryjl3-tyaaa-aaaaa-aaaba-cai"; // never allowlisted in these tests
const DID: &str = "service : { secret_admin_only : (text) -> (); icrc1_balance_of : (record { owner : principal }) -> (nat) query }";
fn bridge() -> IcBridge { IcBridge::new("c".into(), "javascript", "s".into()) }

#[test]
fn override_is_served_to_scripts_without_allowlist() {
    let p = Principal::from_text(X).unwrap();
    policy::set_candid_override(p, Some(DID.into()));
    assert!(policy::list_allowed().is_empty());
    let b = bridge();
    assert_eq!(block_on(b.candid(X)), Ok(DID.to_string()));
    assert_eq!(block_on(b.candid(&X.to_uppercase())), Ok(DID.to_string()));
    let e = block_on(b.call(X, "icrc1_balance_of", Value::Null)).unwrap_err();
    assert!(e.contains("not allowlisted"), "{e}");
    assert_eq!(b.violations.borrow().len(), 1); // the call only; the read records nothing
    // JS `return await icp.candid(X)`, Python `icp.candid(X)`, Rhai `icp::candid(X)` through
    // `Fwd(IcBridge)` (IcBridge with principal() stubbed): all return DID.
}

#[test]
fn override_survives_remove_allowlist() {
    let p = Principal::from_text(X).unwrap();
    policy::set_allowed(p, vec!["icrc1_balance_of".into()]);
    policy::set_candid_override(p, Some(DID.into()));
    evict_interface(&p);               // what remove_allowlist does
    assert!(policy::remove_allowed(p));
    assert_eq!(block_on(bridge().candid(X)), Ok(DID.to_string()));
}

#[test]
fn override_is_used_before_any_fetch_even_when_allowlisted() {
    let p = Principal::from_text(X).unwrap();
    policy::set_allowed(p, vec!["*".into()]);
    policy::set_candid_override(p, Some(DID.into()));
    assert_eq!(block_on(bridge().candid(X)), Ok(DID.to_string())); // no send attempted
}

#[test]
fn bridge_canonicalises_before_allowlist_on_call_path() {
    // uppercase id passes the allowlist and panics in ic0 `cost_call` (the send);
    // "ICRC1_BALANCE_OF" -> not allowlisted; " id", id without dashes, "id-", "aaaaa-aa-"
    // -> "invalid canister id".
}

#[test]
fn any_principal_can_be_allowlisted_including_management_and_self_like_ids() {
    // set_allowed(aaaaa-aa, ["*"]): check_call ok for update_settings, delete_canister;
    // set_allowed(other, ["*"]): check_call ok for http_request_update, set_allowlist.
}
```

#### Grid: L1 (access control), round 2: identifiers compared in the caller's spelling

Scope: register class #1 swept beyond principals. Question per row: is any spelling accepted
on one route (query `http_request` E4, update `http_request_update` E5, `inspect_message` E3)
and refused or read differently on another?

Live probes ran against the local icp-cli network (port 8010, gateway
`icp_code_mode.local.localhost`), read-only except one trivial Rhai script (`40+2`, one
`Ok` audit entry, 0 calls) and two direct `http_request_update` ingress calls with a `ping`
body (one returned 200, one trapped on decode; neither changes state). No setting was
changed, nothing was deployed. Token read from `.env` (MCP_TOKEN line) and never printed.

Gateway forwards the raw path unchanged (no decoding, no `//` or dot-segment folding). Live, POST without token: `/mcp`, `/mcp/`, `/mcp//`, `/mcp?a=1` -> 401; `/MCP`, `/Mcp`, `//mcp`, `/./mcp`, `/x/../mcp`, `/%6Dcp`, `/%6dcp`, `/mcp%2F`, `/mcp;x`, `/mcp%3Fa`, `/mcp%20` -> 404. <a id="grid-L1-r4"></a>

### grid-L1-r4

#### Coverage grid: L1 Access control, round 4: durable authority through allowlisted methods

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`. Question: can one audited call hand an outside principal standing
authority over what this canister's principal holds, so that later effects escape the call
cap, the policy check, the audit log, token revocation and `remove_allowlist`?

Evidence key: **R-native** = probe in a private copy (`src/l1r4_probe.rs`, 4 tests, all pass,
source in the appendix); **R-live-ro** = read-only queries on the local network (port 8010),
nothing changed; **CP** = the code path produces it unambiguously.

##### Candidate findings

| Id | Title | Severity | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1-r4-1 | The allowlist and the README treat authority-granting methods like any other; `vec {"*"}` is offered with no caveat. One `icrc2_approve` (or ICRC-37 approval, neuron hotkey, controller change) gives an outside principal standing authority that is exercised outside every guardrail and survives `revoke_api_token_hash` and `remove_allowlist` | High | R-native (policy and encoding), R-live-ro (ledger supports ICRC-2), CP (consequence) |
| L1-r4-2 | Audit entries record `canister.method` only, never the arguments, so the log cannot tell who was approved, who was paid or how much | Medium | R-live-ro (real `icrc1_transfer` entry), R-native (field list) |
| L1-r4-3 | An empty method list is an undocumented third state: the canister is listed by search, its interface is fetched (messages sent to `aaaaa-aa` and to the target) and returned by `icp.candid`, while every call is refused | Low | R-native |
| L1-r4-4 | Interface fetch asks for `candid:service` without a visibility check: if this canister controls the target, `canister_metadata` can return the private section, which is then cached and handed to every token holder; the code comment and README say "public" | Low | CP (platform behaviour for private sections not reproduced) |

###### L1-r4-1

- `src/policy.rs:178` admits any method when the list contains `"*"`; there is no notion of a
  method that delegates authority. `README.md:159` "Use `vec {"*"}` to allow every method of a
  canister", directly after the ICP ledger example, with no caveat. `README.md:460-462`
  advises revoking tokens "when in doubt", which does not undo an approval.
- R-native `l1r4_wildcard_admits_authority_granting_methods`: with `["*"]` on the ledger id,
  `check_call` admits `icrc2_approve`, `icrc37_approve_tokens`, `icrc37_approve_collection`,
  `manage_neuron`, `add_controller`, `set_admin`, and a method a future upgrade of the target
  might add. After `remove_allowed`, `icrc2_approve` is refused: the canister then has no path
  at all to zero an allowance it granted (only re-allowlisting plus a token-holder script can).
- R-native `l1r4_approve_encodes_unbounded_non_expiring_allowance_to_any_spender`: the Candid
  bridge encodes `icrc2_approve { spender = 2vxsx-fae; amount = 2^128-1; expires_at = null }`
  intact (decoded bytes show both). One cap slot, one audit entry `ledger.icrc2_approve`.
- R-live-ro: the local ledger `ryjl3-...` reports ICRC-2 in `icrc1_supported_standards`;
  `icrc2_allowance(4caro-hl777-77775-aaaba-cai -> 2vxsx-fae)` = 0 (no approval exists today);
  the live allowlist holds the five read methods only. No `icrc2_*` entry in 9,799 audit
  entries scanned.
- Consequence (CP, ICRC-2 standard semantics): the spender calls `icrc2_transfer_from` on the
  ledger directly. That message never passes through this canister: no call cap, no
  instruction budget, no allowlist, no audit entry, and neither `revoke_api_token_hash`
  (stops new requests only) nor `remove_allowlist` (stops this canister's own calls only)
  affects it. Same shape: ICRC-37 approvals, NNS/SNS `manage_neuron` (hotkeys, follow,
  disburse to another account), any `add_controller`/`set_owner` method; `aaaaa-aa.update_settings`
  is the already-reported L1-3 variant.
- Refutation tried: register #49 (one shared identity, accepted, Low) says tokens act as one
  principal; it does not say that a grant outlives the token or escapes caps and audit. The
  ledger's own block log does record the approve and every `transfer_from` (mitigates
  detection for ledgers, not for neurons or arbitrary targets); it does not stop the drain.
- Fix: document that allowlisting a delegating method gives token holders the power to
  create authority that outlives them; exclude a known list of delegating methods from `"*"`
  (must be named explicitly) or refuse `"*"` on canisters whose interface declares them;
  give controllers a way to undo grants (e.g. a controller-only passthrough) after revocation.

###### L1-r4-2

- `src/policy.rs:76-98` (`AuditEntry`): fields `id, timestamp_ns, caller, language,
  script_sha256, canisters, calls, instructions, status, violations, error, run_id, methods`
  (R-native `l1r4_audit_entry_carries_no_call_arguments`). Label built at
  `src/bridge.rs:388` as `format!("{}.{method}", p.to_text())`. The script text is not stored,
  only its hash.
- R-live-ro: entry id 1160 (`Ok`, python, methods `ryjl3-....icrc1_balance_of`,
  `ryjl3-....icrc1_transfer`) has no recipient, amount or memo; nothing in the canister can
  recover them.
- Fix: for calls (not fetches), store a bounded copy or a digest of the encoded arguments, or
  the decoded record of a known value/authority method (spender, to, amount, expires_at).

###### L1-r4-3

- `src/policy.rs:200-201`: `check_interface_fetch` only tests `contains_key`. R-native
  `l1r4_empty_method_list_still_admits_messages_to_the_target`: `set_allowed(p, [])` ->
  fetch `Ok`, any call refused, `search::scope` lists `p` with `[]`. `README.md:365` documents
  only `["method" | "*"]`; nothing says an empty list still permits messages to the target.

###### L1-r4-4

- `src/bridge.rs:424-432` sends `canister_metadata { name = "candid:service" }`; the platform
  type (`ic-management-canister-types-0.10.0/src/lib.rs:604-606`) addresses both
  `icp:public` and `icp:private` sections. The comment (`src/bridge.rs:421`) and
  `README.md:494` say "the public `candid:service` section". The result goes to `DID_CACHE`
  and out through `icp.candid` (`src/bridge.rs:478-479`) and search to every token holder.
  Live: this canister controls neither target (both controlled by one user principal), so
  the private case cannot arise there today.

##### Grid

| Row | Cell |
|---|---|
| VF4 assets held by this principal | **finding** L1-r4-1: value can move after the token and the allowlist entry are gone, through authority granted in one audited call; L1-r4-2: the audit does not say where value went |
| D2 allowlist | **finding** L1-r4-1 (no delegating-method notion, wildcard covers future methods), L1-r4-3 (empty list semantics). Keying and canonical form hold (round 1, 2) |
| AD2 `set_allowlist` | **finding** L1-r4-1 / L1-r4-3: accepts `"*"` on any canister without warning and `[]` as a silent fetch-only state. Unvalidated principal itself: already reported (L1-3), not repeated |
| E6 `set_allowlist` | **holds** for who may call it (controller guard, R-live round 1). What it grants: L1-r4-1 |
| E9 / AD5 `add_api_token_hash` | **holds**: guard, 64-hex validation (`src/policy.rs:208-214`); a new token gets exactly the shared principal's current allowlist, nothing more. Label length is L3/L14, not L1 |
| E10 `revoke_api_token_hash` | **finding** (part of L1-r4-1): revocation stops new requests (holds, round 1) but not authority already delegated to outside principals. In-flight runs: already reported (L1-2), not repeated |
| AD6 token revocation | same as E10 |
| A7 management canister | **finding** L1-r4-4 (fetch can read private metadata when this canister is a controller). Script calls to `aaaaa-aa`: already reported (L1-3) |
| CL6 "deny by default; checked before any message is sent" | **holds** literally for messages this canister sends (R-native round 1, `reserve` before every send); the guarantee does not extend to effects of delegated authority, which the README never says (L1-r4-1). Empty-list nuance: L1-r4-3 |
| CL1 "every run is audited" | **holds** literally (each message of each run gets an entry). Misleading for delegated effects (not runs, not audited) and for arguments (L1-r4-2) |
| README:159 `vec {"*"}` | **finding** L1-r4-1 (no caveat; on a ledger it includes `icrc2_approve` and `icrc1_transfer`) |
| README:460-462 revocation advice | **finding** (part of L1-r4-1): "revoked ... when in doubt" implies revocation contains a leaked token; it does not undo its approvals |

##### Phase 4 techniques applied

- Boundary: approve with `amount = 2^128-1`, `expires_at = null` encodes intact (no limit on
  the size of a grant; one cap slot regardless of amount).
- Differential: `check_call` vs `check_interface_fetch` on an empty list (fetch allowed, call
  refused).
- Live: read-only only (this task is not the Live phase).

##### Not tested, and why

- The end-to-end grant: allowlist `icrc2_approve` on the local ledger, fund the canister,
  approve an outside identity from a script, revoke the token and `remove_allowlist`, then
  `icrc2_transfer_from` as that identity and diff the audit log. It changes settings and
  ledger state, which only the Live phase may do. Restore: allowlist back to the five read
  methods, allowance set to 0, balance returned.
- Private `candid:service` via `canister_metadata`: needs this canister as controller of a
  target built with `icp:private candid:service`; that changes canister settings.
- ICRC-37, NNS governance, SNS: none deployed on the local network.

### grid-L2-r1

#### Coverage grid: L2 Atomicity and commit points, round 1

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`. Lens question: if execution stops here, what has already been
committed and what is lost?

Dynamic work was done on a **private, disposable local network** (icp-cli 1.7.0, gateway port
8047, own state directory in the scratchpad, stopped and deleted afterwards) running the exact
deployed artifacts copied from the shared network's state (`icp_code_mode` sha256
`ad3ee221…2411`, `demo_store` `5ed9b423…a029`), with a freshly generated test token. The shared
network on port 8010 was not touched. Fault injection used: a reply-callback trap at the 40B
instruction limit (catastrophic regex backtracking, register #23), the "insufficient liquid
cycles" on-the-spot refusal (freezing threshold raised), and attempts to make stable-memory
growth fail (see L2-5).

Candidate ids (L2-n) refer to the findings returned with this grid.

| Row | Verdict | Reason / evidence |
|---|---|---|
| K1 first-pending commit (`IcBridge::sent` / `record_message`) | holds | ic-cdk 0.20.3 `CallFuture::poll` returns `Pending` only after `call_perform` returned 0, and `Ready(Err)` on `call_perform` failure or on the liquid-cycles pre-check (`call.rs:899-935`); `record_message` runs inside that first poll, in the same execution as `call_perform`. Reproduced: with liquid cycles below the call's reservation the call failed with "insufficient liquid cycles balance" and the run's entries showed `calls = 0`, no `Started`. A normal call wrote `Started` with `calls = 1` |
| K1 (record content) | finding L2-1 | For an interface fetch the record names `aaaaa-aa.canister_metadata` and `canisters = ["aaaaa-aa"]`; the canister whose interface was read appears nowhere. Contradicts `.did`/`policy.rs` "`canister.<candid interface>` for an interface fetch". Reproduced |
| K2 JS awaits (`join_all` per round) | holds / finding L2-2 | Commit per round holds (all K1 entries of a round commit with their sends). But requests still queued in `State.pending` when the script's promise settles are dropped without being sent, error or warning (`js.rs:377-383`); run reports `Ok`. Reproduced (L2-2) |
| K3 Python awaits | holds / finding L2-2 | Same as K2 for `rebased(host)`/`rebased(join_all)`; `icp.call_async` requests left in `queued` at `RunProgress::Complete` are dropped (`python.rs:241, 249`). Reproduced (L2-2) |
| K4 Rhai replay awaits | holds | One request per replay, awaited before the next replay; answers kept per run. Differential: an unused `icp::call_canister` statement *is* executed (order created), unlike K2/K3 |
| K5 `run_search` awaits / two sequential awaits in `fetch_did` | holds (with L2-1) | Each fetch message is recorded at its own first poll; a refused-on-the-spot `canister_metadata` falls through to the hack call with no entry for the first. Label issue as L2-1 |
| K6 closing entry + reply | holds | `finish()` and `http_update` re-measure keep the reply under 1.9 MB (register #2/#4). If the execution traps after the closing entry, the entry and `finished = true` roll back together and K7 writes `Trapped` (code path; reproduced for the trap-in-callback case) |

But the `Trapped` entry under-reports `instructions` (L2-3) and drops the "…and N more" violation count (L2-4). If the cleanup itself traps, the slot and the pending id leak (L2-5, code path) |
| K8 trap before first send | holds (accepted, register #11) | Whole request rolled back; no entry; documented in README "Not in the log at all" |
| K9 policy refusal before any send | holds (with #11 caveat) | Refusals are recorded only in the closing entry; if that execution traps, nothing is recorded (register #11, accepted, documented). After a send, refusals made in the final (trapped) execution are lost from `Trapped` (documented: "violations recorded up to the last message"); reproduced (`late_bad` absent) |
| K10 admin updates | not applicable | Single execution, no await, no outbound effect: all or nothing |

Not reproduced: needs a target that stays busy across an upgrade |

| O3 stable audit writes | holds | Every append is in the same execution as the effect it describes (K1) or the closing step (K6/K7); `append_audit` assigns `id = len` and appends in one borrow |
| D4 `AUDIT` StableLog | holds (with F4) | Index and data writes happen in one execution, so a trap cannot leave a half-written entry. Growth failure traps (F4, see L2-5) |
| E5a `run_script` closing entry | holds | Exactly one closing entry per run that reaches the end; written before `finish()`; `run_id` links (reproduced) |

<a id="grid-L2-r2"></a>

### grid-L2-r2

#### Coverage grid: L2 Atomicity and commit points, round 2 (cleanup-callback limits)

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`. Question for this round: can an ordinary token holder make the
cleanup callback trap, so that a run gets no closing entry and leaks its run slot and pending
id? Round 1 found one trigger only (stable-memory growth failure, L2-5, Low).

Evidence key: **R** reproduced, **C** code path, **L** read-only on the shared network (port
8010).

Where it ran:
- **Private network.** icp-cli 1.7.0, a separate project in the scratchpad, gateway port 8047,
  its own state. It ran the exact deployed artifacts from `.icp/cache/artifacts`
  (`icp_code_mode` sha256 `ad3ee221…2411`, `demo_store` `5ed9b423…a029`) with a freshly
  generated token. It was stopped and deleted afterwards.
- **Shared network (8010).** Read-only use: `get_audit_logs`, `get_policy`, `icp canister logs`,
  and management `canister_info` through the network's proxy canister.

Nothing was compiled.

##### Platform facts used

- **Cleanup instruction budget.** The replica (`rs/execution_environment/src/execution/response.rs`)
  holds back 5% of the message limit for cleanup. The response callback runs under a limit
  reduced by that reserve. Cleanup gets whatever the callback left unused, plus the reserve. So
  after a callback that hit the instruction limit, cleanup has about 2B instructions (5% of 40B).
- **Wasm memory limit.** Per the DFINITY PSA on the Wasm memory limit, `wasm_memory_limit` is
  enforced only in update, init and post_upgrade. It is not enforced in response callbacks, so
  in a callback or in cleanup the only memory ceiling is the 4 GiB wasm32 address space.
- **Drop order** (ic-cdk 0.20.3, `call.rs:1006-1038`; executor `machinery.rs:146-189`). Cleanup
  first makes two small allocations: the `"cleanup"` reject string and
  `Vec::with_capacity(tasks)`. It then drops the whole task. Inside `run_script` the awaited
  `LanguageRouter::execute` future is the innermost live value, so it is dropped first. That
  future holds the Boa Context and State, the Monty snapshot and heap, the Rhai Engine, AST and
  `answers`, and the in-flight `join_all`. Next `IcBridge::drop` runs (`PENDING_RUNS` removal,
  then the `Trapped` append), and `RunSlot` drops last. The R evidence below confirms this order:
  the Monty heap teardown shows up in the `Trapped` entry's instruction count.

##### Cells

| Row | Verdict | Reason / evidence |
|---|---|---|
| E5d / K7: cleanup instruction cost, Python | holds | **R.** Script: build 500,000 heap objects (at the 64 MiB limit), `icp.call` (commit), then `3 ** 7000000` in the callback. The callback trapped with "instructions for single message execution". The cleanup still wrote `Trapped` (id 33, `calls = 1`); `active_runs = 0` and `pending_run_ids = []` afterwards. `Trapped.instructions − Started.instructions` was 96.8M: everything committed after `Started` plus the Monty heap drop, about 190 instructions per object. The cap on the heap is 64 MiB counted, plus the L8-2 reply allowance. Each reply is held to `DECODING_QUOTA`: a 5,000-item `list_orders` reply decoded and 10,000 items failed (R). With 25 replies of at most a few MiB each, the heap stays near or below 1M objects, so teardown is about 0.2B. That is roughly 10x under the 2B reserve. Monty frees iteratively (`Heap::dec_ref` work stack, flat `StableHeap::drop`), so there is no recursion and no stack risk |
| E5d / K7: cleanup instruction cost, JS | holds | **R.** Script: hold 400k objects, `icp.call`, then a burn loop inside a function (L6-1) that trapped at the instruction limit. `Trapped` was written (id 39), with only 0.81M between `Started` and `Trapped`. Boa GC objects are only unrooted on drop (`boa_gc` `Gc::drop` finalizes the handle; `Context::drop` decrements a counter), so heap size does not affect cleanup cost. The objects are freed by the next JS run's `force_collect` |
| E5d / K7: cleanup instruction cost, Rhai | holds | **C.** Across an await Rhai keeps only the Engine, the AST and `answers` (JSON replies plus request args). It keeps no script-built Dynamics, because each replay finishes `eval_ast` before the await (`rhai_rt.rs:188-218`). AST nesting is capped by `set_max_expr_depths(64, 32)`. Request args are capped at depth 128 by `to_json_value`. Replies are capped by `DECODING_QUOTA` (5k-item ceiling, R) and `MAX_DEPTH`. At most 25 answers, so teardown is far below 2B and serde_json's recursive drop stays shallow. Not reproduced: Rhai has no in-callback 40B trap under default limits (`on_progress` stops cleanly; L14-2 needs `max_instructions ≥ 40e9`) |
| E5d / K7: cleanup memory | holds (code path, ceiling not reproduced) | **C.** Before any drop, cleanup allocates only two tiny blocks. In every run, the execution that commits before a suspension sends a message, and `record_message` there appends an audit entry and frees its Candid buffer and string clones before the commit. So free chunks larger than those two blocks exist at every commit point. Every engine also frees memory before the `Trapped` append runs: JS frees Boa's 1,024-slot VM stack (`Stack::new(1024)`, 16 KiB contiguous), Python the Monty heap, Rhai the Engine and AST. The append needs under about 1 KiB. Not reproduced at the 4 GiB ceiling (see Not tested) |
| E5d / K7: panic during cleanup drops | holds | **C.** No RefCell or Mutex guard is held across an await in `IcBridge`, `js.rs` (comment at `:382`), `python.rs` or `rhai_rt.rs`. Monty's `dec_ref` asserts `readers == 0`, which holds at a suspension. **R:** the Monty and Boa teardowns completed in cleanup |
| E5d / K7: drop order engine → `IcBridge` → `RunSlot` | holds | **C** (Rust drop order of an async fn's live locals; the awaited temporary goes first). **R:** the 96.8M Python delta against 0.81M for JS. All engine teardown happens before the closing record and before the slot and pending id are released. That is a variant of L2-5 (fallible work before the release), bounded today as measured above |
| E5d / K7: other trap triggers in callback | holds | **R.** Boa `String.prototype.repeat` with a count of 2e8 panics with "capacity overflow" (candidate L2r2-1). After a send, cleanup wrote `Trapped` (id 44), the slot came back, and the pending list was empty. **R:** the instruction-limit trap (Python bigint `**`, JS loop) also left `Trapped` |
| V1 `ACTIVE_RUNS` | holds | **R.** 0 after every trapped run on the private network (4 `Trapped` runs). **L:** 0 on 8010, which has had no icp_code_mode code change since 09:32:24 and 4 `Trapped` runs since then, so no cleanup failure has leaked a slot there |
| V3 `PENDING_RUNS` | holds | **R** and **L**: empty, under the same conditions as V1 |
| CL18 "exactly one closing entry" | holds (single tool call; SW7-1 known for batches) | **R.** Private log: 15 runs with `Started`, each with exactly one closing entry. **L.** 8010: entries 680-899 (current module) have no orphan |
| CL20 "pending or unknown … A trap is recorded as `Trapped`" | holds; the six live orphans explained | **L.** See "Six live orphan runs" below. Every orphan was written by a code version that had no `Trapped` cleanup (register #9 era), not by the audited module |
| K11 upgrade while runs are suspended | not applicable to the six orphans | **L.** No orphan was still waiting at the upgrade that followed it: `demo_store` (their only target) kept answering other runs inside each window. See below |

| W11 Rhai `answers` retention | holds for cleanup | Bounded as above. Memory retention is L3's question |
| V6 Monty memory atomics in cleanup | holds | The frees during cleanup go through `sub()`, and this cleanup is kept, so the counter matches the freed heap. Baseline is re-set per run (`python.rs:229`) |

Rust panics do (`Panicked at …` plus `[TRAP]`, including in a callback whose cleanup succeeded). **L:** the 8010 log has 17 records (05:01-05:05 and 10:34-10:35), nothing for its 4 `Trapped` runs, and nothing between 05:05 and 10:34 |

##### Six live orphan runs (465, 469, 470, 471, 488, 654)

Upgrade times come from management `canister_info` (read through the 8010 proxy canister).
Commit times come from `git log`.

| Run | Started (UTC) | Module (deployed at) | Next upgrade | Messages | Closing entry existed in that version? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 465 | 08:53:21 | `bc5a98…` (08:53:07, commit f5305be "run_id") | 09:04:30 | 1 to demo_store (old schema: `calls = 0`, no `methods`) | No. `Drop for IcBridge` did not exist |
| 469, 470 | 08:58:40, 08:58:53 | `bc5a98…` | 09:04:30 | demo_store; same script `91c57ccc` twice | No |
| 471 | 09:04:46 | `a7d5cf…` (09:04:30, d508ece) | 09:22:21 | 5 (list_orders, fetch, 3× create_order) | No |
| 488 | 09:22:47 | `21872f…` (09:22:21, 5d856e3) | 09:23:58 | 2 (sales_summary, fetch); script `e5fdbc9c` | No |
| 654 | 09:27:22 | `f32a00…` (09:27:17, 13abe24) | 09:32:24 | 1 (sales_summary); same script `e5fdbc9c` | No. `Drop` only removed the pending id; no `Trapped` |

`Trapped` closing entries arrived with cdfa3d9, deployed as `ad3ee221` at 09:32:24. Since then
there have been 220 entries (680-899), 4 `Trapped` runs and no orphan.

Cause, with the evidence:
1. **Not cut off by an upgrade.** Every orphan targeted only `demo_store`, a synchronous
   canister that replies within a round. Other runs to `demo_store` finished inside the same
   windows (467 eight seconds after 465; 491 eight seconds after 488; 679 after 654). The gaps
   to the next upgrade (71 s to 17.5 min) are far longer than any round trip. `demo_store` had
   no code change inside any window.
2. **Deterministic.** The same script was orphaned twice in a row (469/470 `91c57ccc`), and
   across two module versions (488/654 `e5fdbc9c`). A run cut short by an upgrade would not
   repeat like that; a script that traps after its first reply would.
3. **Instruction-limit trap, most likely.** The 8010 canister log has no record between 05:05
   and 10:34. The log is not full (17 records, indices 0-16, none evicted) and records persist
   across upgrades. Wasm traps and panics are logged, also in callbacks (R); instruction-limit
   traps in callbacks are not (R).

So each orphan was a response-callback trap, most likely at the instruction limit (register
#23 / L6-1 class), under a version without the `Trapped` cleanup (register #9, fixed in
cdfa3d9). None is evidence of a failed cleanup in the audited code.

##### Not tested

- **Cleanup out of memory at the 4 GiB ceiling.** Making it fail would need the committed heap
  to have under about 64 bytes free with no reusable small chunk, so that ic-cdk's two
  pre-drop allocations fail before anything is freed. Reaching that takes about 4 GiB of JS
  allocations spread over several concurrent runs (about 24 instructions per byte, within the
  20B per-run budget), followed by byte-level calibration across many probes. Not attempted:
  each probe costs minutes and GBs of replica state. The code-path argument in the
  cleanup-memory row says the window does not open, because the committing execution frees
  its `record_message` temporaries. Unverified.
- **Exact cleanup budget on this PocketIC version.** Read from the replica source on master;
  the measured teardowns (≤ 0.1B) are far below any plausible reserve.
- **Rhai in-callback 40B trap.** Not reachable with default limits.

<a id="grid-L2-r3"></a>

### grid-L2-r3

#### Coverage grid: L2 Atomicity and commit points, round 3 (target-side reconciliation)

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`. Question for this round: does the audit log match what the
targets actually received, run by run? The claim under test (README.md:394-396, CL17) is
"the log never shows a message that was not sent, and never misses one that was". Until
now it had been checked one finding at a time and by code path. No automated test drives the
production bridge (register #58). This round builds the missing harness by hand and runs it.

Evidence key: **R** reproduced on the private network below, **C** code path.

##### Method

**Network.** I used a private, disposable icp-cli 1.7.0 network: its own project in the session
scratchpad, gateway port 8061, its own state. It ran the deployed `icp_code_mode` artifact
copied from `.icp/cache/artifacts` (sha256 `ad3ee221…2411`) with a freshly generated test
token. When the test finished, the network was stopped and its state, the token and the
wasm files were deleted. I sent nothing to the shared network on port 8010, which is still
running. That network was not used because this round needs upgrades and `set_limits`
changes. A different port avoids any collision.

**Recording target.** `rec_target` is a throw-away Rust canister (ic-cdk 0.20.3) and is not
part of the repo. Every message it receives is appended to a heap log with: sequence number,
`msg_caller`, method, sha256 of the raw Candid argument, the decoded tag, and `time()`. It
has these methods:
- `ping(text)`: replies.
- `nope(text)`: records, then sends an explicit reject. The record is kept.
- `hold(text)`: records, then loops on self-calls until `set_hold(false)`. Used for slow
  targets, timeouts and upgrades.
- `secret(text)`: never allowlisted. It is a canary for sends that bypass policy.
- `__get_candid_interface_tmp_hack`: exported as an update, so interface fetches that reach
  the target are logged too.

The wasm has no `candid:service` metadata. Every fetch therefore sends two messages:
`aaaaa-aa.canister_metadata`, which fails, and then the fallback to the target. Only
`ping`, `nope` and `hold` were allowlisted.

**Scripts.** A generator writes random scripts in all three languages. Every call site carries
a unique literal tag `<run>.<n>`, so each target-side message maps to exactly one run. The
step kinds are:
- sequential calls;
- `Promise.all` / `asyncio.gather` batches mixing allowed, rejected and policy-refused calls;
- un-awaited calls;
- caught and uncaught rejects;
- caught and uncaught policy refusals;
- `icp.candid`;
- bursts of 20-30 calls past the 25-call cap;
- traps at random positions.

The traps are a catastrophic regex in JS (register #23), `3 ** 7000000` in Python, and
`index_of` over a 1 MiB string in Rhai. The Rhai trap needs `max_instructions = 50e9`
(L14-2). That value was set only for the Rhai trap phases and then put back.

**Reconciler** (scratchpad `recon.py`, `extra.py`). For every `run_id` it checks:
- the first message entry is `Started`, and the message entries carry `calls` = 1..n;
- there is exactly one closing entry;
- the closing `methods` equals the per-message entries in order;
- the closing `calls` equals their number;
- the closing `canisters` equals the canisters named in `methods`;
- the closing status matches what the client saw: `Ok`/`PolicyViolation` for a success,
  `Error`/`PolicyViolation` for an error, `Trapped` for a gateway reject;
- the sequence of messages to the target in the audit equals the sequence the target logged
  with that run's tags. Order counts.

Globally it checks:
- fetch messages counted in the audit equal fetch messages received by the target;
- no tagged target message lacks an audit run;
- no `secret` arrived;
- every argument hash equals the Candid encoding of its tag;
- the only caller is `icp_code_mode`;
- each message entry's timestamp is ≤ the target's receive time, which is ≤ the closing
  entry's timestamp.

##### What ran (all reconciled together at the end)

| Phase | Content |
|---|---|
| A (seeds 1, 4) | 88 random scripts, 8 at a time, interface cached |
| B (seeds 2, 3) | 14 rounds of 6-10 concurrent scripts and searches. The interface cache was evicted before each round (`remove_allowlist` + `set_allowlist`), so concurrent runs and searches raced on fetches |
| C | 10 concurrent scripts (JS/Python/Rhai) held on `hold` (8 slots), plus 3 searches while held, then release |
| D | `call_timeout_seconds` 5 and 0 with `hold` in all three languages, timed-out calls caught and followed by more calls |
| E1 | `icp deploy icm` (upgrade) while 2 Python, 2 Rhai and 1 JS run waited on `hold`. Released during `Stopping` |
| E5 | Same, but never released, with `call_timeout_seconds = 240`: the deadline expired during `Stopping` |
| E4 | Same as E5, but the canister ran short of liquid cycles mid-run (unplanned on-the-spot refusals) |
| F, R (seeds 7, 11) | Trap phases with `max_instructions = 50e9`: 36 random scripts, then 20 scripts with the trap forced after 1-6 sends (12 Rhai) |
| G | One HTTP batch: an uncached search followed by a Python script that traps before any send |
| I | Fault-injection build (see the K7 row): a trap inside the cleanup callback, one run per language |

The final reconciliation covered 271 audit runs. Phase R ran after the client-request
counts and the argument checks, so its numbers below are reported separately:
- Client requests, all phases except R: 282 (86 Python, 80 Rhai, 78 JS, 38 searches).
- Phase R: 20 more scripts.
- Messages to the target: 868 tagged script messages and 212 interface fetches.
- `Trapped` closings: 41 (17 JS, 13 Rhai, 10 Python, 1 search).

**Result.** Zero differences between the target log and the audit fields `methods` and
`calls`, and zero differences in closing status, in every phase. Argument hashes, callers and
timestamp order were checked over the first 1,035 receipts (before phase R): every hash
matched, the only caller was `icp_code_mode`, and all 823 order checks passed. The only reconciler flags are the three runs of
phase I: no closing entry, which is the documented "unknown" case (already reported as
L2-5). Two known findings were reproduced, not only shown by code path: SW7-1 (phase G) and
L2-5 (phase I).

| CL17 "never shows a message that was not sent, and never misses one that was" | holds | **R.** Every tagged message the target received has exactly one `Started`/`Call` entry in the right run and position. Every such entry addressed to the target has a matching receipt. The same holds under concurrency (8 slots full), un-awaited calls, `Promise.all`/`gather` batches, cap bursts, caught and uncaught rejects, call timeouts, upgrades, and traps in all three languages. Policy-refused calls (`secret`, calls over the cap) never reached the target and have no entry. On-the-spot refusals for insufficient liquid cycles (E4) also have no entry. Messages sent in an execution that later trapped were neither delivered nor logged. Rhai replays never re-sent an answered request (no duplicate tags) |

##### Not tested

- **Upgrade without a stop.** Both icp-cli upgrade paths stop first (L13-r2). A raw chunked

  documented outcome ("unknown": `Started`/`Call` with no closing entry) is unverified.
- **A message accepted but never delivered** (a bounded-wait call that times out before
  delivery). A local network delivers within a round, so every timed-out call here had already
  been received. The README covers this as "outcome unknown".
- **A target that traps.** The recorder cannot log a message whose execution it rolls back.
  The caller-side behaviour is the same as for `nope` (a reject after an accepted send).
- **The original direction of SW7-1** (the script completes and a later search in the same
  execution traps). It would need the script's last execution calibrated to within the
  search's cost of 40B. The reverse direction (G) shows the same root cause.
- **Cleanup trap from a real trigger** (stable-memory growth failure, F4). It was injected
  with a modified build instead. See L2-r1/L2-r2 for why the real trigger was not reachable.
- **Mainnet timing** (cross-subnet delays, queue-full refusals). This was local PocketIC
  only.

##### How it was tested

- Private copy of the tree (no `target/`), shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. Native probes as
  `#[cfg(test)]` tests built with `cargo test --release` (profile `opt-level="z"`, LTO), each
  heavy case run on a thread with an 8 MiB stack; instruction counts are macOS
  `/usr/bin/time -l` "instructions retired" for the whole test process (native aarch64, a
  proxy for wasm instructions, not an on-chain count).
- A small wasm probe crate (`cdylib` depending on `icp_code_mode`, same `.cargo/config.toml`
  rustflags including `-zstack-size=8388608`, same release profile) run in Node with stubbed
  `ic0` imports and a large V8/OS stack, so a trap is the 8 MiB shadow stack running out
  ("memory access out of bounds"). This matters because candid's recursion guard is a
  no-op on wasm (`candid-0.10.40/src/utils.rs:12-32`) and native-only tests cannot see it.
- No live canister was touched.

### grid-L3-r2

#### Coverage grid: L3 Resource bounds, round 2 (Boa global Symbol registry)

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`. Row ids refer to `inventory.md`. Cells: **finding** (candidate id
below), **holds** (why), **n/a** (why). Candidate L3r2-1 is described in the lens's returned
findings.

##### How it was tested

- **Code path.** `boa_engine-0.22.0/src/builtins/symbol/mod.rs:41-80`: `static
  GLOBAL_SYMBOL_REGISTRY: LazyLock<GlobalSymbolRegistry>` holds two `FxDashMap`s
  (`keys: Box<[u16]> -> JsSymbol`, `symbols: JsSymbol -> Box<[u16]>`); `JsSymbol::new`
  (`src/symbol.rs:175-186`) stores a third `Box<[u16]>` copy of the description in an `Arc`
  owned by the map. No code removes entries. `Symbol.for` (`mod.rs:320-336`) is the only
  writer. `src/runtimes/js.rs:308-315` deletes `Math.random`, `Atomics`,
  `SharedArrayBuffer`, `WeakRef`, `FinalizationRegistry`, not `Symbol.for`;
  `boa_gc::force_collect` (`js.rs:361`) only sweeps the thread-local GC heap, and the registry
  is outside it (`JsSymbol` is `unsafe_empty_trace`, `Arc`-counted).
- **Other engine statics checked (V10).** Boa: `CANNOT_BLOCK_COUNTER`,
  `ASYNC_EVAL_QUEUE_INDEX`, `CODEBLOCK_ID_COUNTER`, `SYMBOL_HASH_COUNT` are counters;
  `RecursionLimiter::SEEN` is a Debug-fmt scratch map that empties itself; boa_string
  `RAW_STATICS_CACHE` is a fixed table; `futex::CRITICAL_SECTION` is unreachable (Atomics
  deleted). Rhai 1.27.0: only fixed tables and two `OnceCell` hash seeds. Monty: fixed
  LazyLocks (per task brief). `GLOBAL_SYMBOL_REGISTRY` is the only growable engine static.
- **Native test** (private copy, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/audit-target`,
  `cargo test --lib audit_l3_symbol -- --nocapture --test-threads=1`, debug profile). The
  test turns on the project's own counting allocator for its thread
  (`counting_alloc::COUNT_THIS_THREAD`) and reads `monty_types::LIVE_MEMORY` before and after
  each `js()` run (`MockBridge`). Keys are a 131,072-char string built by doubling
  (`let S='k'; for(j<17) S+=S`) plus a suffix; `'k'.repeat(1e5)` cannot be used because
  `String.prototype.repeat` charges the frame's 1M loop counter (LIM24).

  | Run | Script (200 iterations unless noted) | Live heap retained after the run |
  |---|---|---|
  | A | `Symbol.for(S+i)` | +150.03 MiB (total 150.08) |
  | B | `Symbol.for(S+'b'+i)` | +150.03 MiB (total 300.10) |
  | A again | same keys as A | +0.00 MiB |
  | C control | `Symbol(S+i)` (not registered) | +0.00 MiB |
  | D control | `a.push(S+i)` (200 strings in an array) | +0.00 MiB |
  | E | `Symbol.for(S+'e'+i); throw new Error('x')` (run ends with an error) | +150.03 MiB (total 450.13) |
  | F | 100,000 x `Symbol.for('s'+i)` (short keys) | +13.39 MiB (total 463.52) |

  150.03 MiB = 200 x 131,072 x 6 bytes: three UTF-16 copies per key. Short keys cost about
  140 bytes each. The controls show that `force_collect` reclaims everything else a run
  allocates, so the growth is the registry alone.
- **Live test** (local network, port 8010, `icp_code_mode`, module hash `0xad3e...2411`),
  token from the `MCP_TOKEN` line of `.env`, never printed. Instruction counts from the
  closing audit entries, matched by `script_sha256`:

  | Audit id | Script (20 iterations, 131,072-char keys) | Instructions |
  |---|---|---|
  | 911 / 917 | baseline: build `S`, `return` | 19,875,185 / 19,926,026 |
  | 912 / 915 | `Symbol(S+'L3r2a'+i)` | 322,072,784 / 326,806,093 |
  | 913 | `Symbol.for(S+'L3r2a'+i)`, first time (inserts) | 678,637,783 |
  | 914 | same script and keys in a new request (lookups only) | 479,803,848 |

  If each run had a fresh registry, 913 and 914 would cost the same. The second run is ~199M
  instructions (29%) cheaper, so the 20 keys from run 913 were still registered in a separate
  later request on the deployed canister. Cost of a retained byte: about
  (678.6M - 19.9M) / (20 x 786,432 B) = 42 instructions. Under the default `max_instructions`
  of 20e9 one run that ends cleanly keeps about 20e9 / 42 = 476 MB (about 454 MiB). With the
  default 3 GiB `wasm_memory_limit` (LIM29), about 7 such runs fill an empty heap. This was not
  driven to the limit.
- **memory_size is not a usable signal here.** `icp canister status` showed 1,246,514,630
  before and 3,259,715,014 after the window, but other agents' runs (for example audit ids
  916 and 918, 2.07e9 and 5.15e9 instructions, not this lens's scripts) ran in the same
  window, and Wasm memory never shrinks. This lens's runs keep about 15.7 MiB (20 keys x
  786 KB). **No upgrade was done** (only the Live phase may upgrade). Those 15.7 MiB stay
  allocated until the next upgrade. The canister answered a baseline run normally afterwards.
- **Cross-run observability (I6/I20).** Native: run 1 `Symbol.for('probe')` then run 2
  `[Symbol.keyFor(Symbol.for('probe')), Symbol.keyFor(Symbol('probe')),
  Symbol.for('probe')===Symbol.for('probe'), Object.getOwnPropertySymbols({[Symbol.for('zz')]:1,
  [Symbol.for('probe')]:2}).map(String)]` returns `["probe", null, true, ["Symbol(zz)",
  "Symbol(probe)"]]`. These are the same as with a fresh registry. No symbol value outlives a
  run, so identity cannot be compared across runs. Property order is insertion order, not
  the global hash order. A script has no clock or instruction counter. The only signal is
  cost: a lookup is cheaper than an insert. The caller can see that only in audit entries
  (controllers) or in the number in a budget-exceeded error, after the run.

##### Grid

| Row | Cell | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| V10 engine statics | **finding L3r2-1** | `GLOBAL_SYMBOL_REGISTRY` is a process-global, insert-only map that a script fills through `Symbol.for`. Measured: +150 MiB kept per run, the same after a run that throws, and still present in a later request on the live canister. Every other Boa, Rhai and Monty static is a counter or a fixed table (see above) |
| V8 Boa GC heap | holds (for retention) | Controls C and D keep 0.00 MiB after the run: `force_collect` reclaims the run's GC heap, strings and unregistered symbols. Charging one run for another's GC work is the separate L8-1. The registry is outside the GC heap, so nothing in V8 frees it |
| LIM29 3 GiB Wasm memory | **finding L3r2-1** | Round 1 graded this row "holds/accepted" because each JS run frees what it allocates (#24). That is false for the registry. The limit is cumulative across runs, and about 7 clean runs at the default budget reach it (extrapolated from the measured 42 instructions per byte). Nothing in the app tracks or caps it |
| F13 out of memory | **finding L3r2-1** | Round 1 graded this row "accepted (#24)". #24 covers one run's trap, which rolls back that message. Here the memory is committed by runs that succeed, so after the limit is reached the out-of-memory trap is persistent, not per-run. Not reproduced to the trap: that would make the shared dev canister unusable until an upgrade, and upgrades belong to the Live phase |
| LIM24 JS loop/recursion limits | holds | `String.prototype.repeat` charges the frame's loop counter (`'k'.repeat(1e5)` x ~10 calls hits it). Building by doubling uses 17 iterations. The limit bounds iterations, not memory, as documented. Neither path is a new bypass |
| LIM26 Python 64 MiB / LIM27 Rhai sizes | n/a | No process-global engine registry in Monty or Rhai (V10 check). Their per-run memory is bounded and freed |
| W8 JS unbounded work | **finding L3r2-1** (memory dimension) | The cost per run is bounded by `max_instructions`. The memory a run keeps after it ends is not bounded |
| E5 `http_request_update` | **finding L3r2-1** (reach) | Any token holder: `execute_icp_script` with `language: "javascript"`. No allowlist entry and no outbound call are needed, so no policy check or call cap applies |
| E4 `http_request` query | n/a for writing (a query's heap changes are discarded) | Whether queries trap once the registry fills the heap is unverified: the limit is not driven, and the platform's enforcement of `wasm_memory_limit` for queries was not checked |
| AD4 `set_limits.max_instructions` | holds | A larger budget raises the memory one run can keep (42 instructions per byte), but the total across runs is unbounded at any setting. The budget does not affect this finding |

| I10 Honest interface; README.md:451-453 ("a script that hoards memory ends in a trap ... The cap of 8 concurrent scripts limits how far this can spread"); README.md:70 ("fresh VM per call") | **finding L3r2-1** (claim part) | The README treats JS memory as per-run. Registry memory accumulates across sequential runs, so the 8-run cap does not limit it, and the engine is not fully fresh per call. ### grid-L3-r3

#### Coverage grid: L3 Resource bounds, round 3 (Monty native operations whose cost grows with input)

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`. Row ids refer to `inventory.md`. Cells: **finding** (candidate id
below), **holds** (why), **n/a** (why). Candidates L3r3-1 and L3r3-2 are described in the lens's
returned findings. Known and not repeated: bigint `**` (`long_int.rs:1054-1069, 1166`),
`py_repr`/repr of big ints in `to_json`, `eval`/`exec` compiling runtime-built source.

##### How it was tested

- **Where.** The project's local icp-cli network (port 8010), canister `icp_code_mode`, module
  `224cfa7a...` (built from the committed tree, see `grid-L13-r2.md`). Limits at their defaults
  throughout (`max_instructions` 20e9; confirmed by `while True: pass` ending at
  `20000533166 > 20000000000`). No setting was changed; nothing was deployed.
- **How measured.** Each probe is one `execute_icp_script` (`language: python`) with a unique
  trailing comment. Its audit entry is found by `script_sha256` (other agents were writing
  entries at the same time) and its `instructions` field read with `get_audit_logs`. The cost of
  an operation is the run's total minus a setup-only run. Helper:
  `$SCRATCH/l3r3/probe.sh` (token read from `.env`, never printed).
- **Interruptibility test ("PRE").** Setup, then `for i in range(23500000): pass` (815
  instructions per iteration; the loop alone ends at 19.16e9), then the operation. A polled
  operation stops just past the budget (`> 20000000000` by under 0.1e9). An unpolled one runs to
  completion and the post-run check reports budget + its whole cost.
- **Trap test.** An operation that costs more than about 20e9 after the PRE loop, or more than
  40e9 on its own, ends in HTTP 503 `Canister exceeded the limit of 40000000000 instructions for
  single message execution`. No audit entry is written (nothing was sent; register #11).

##### Per-operation results (wasm, live)

Largest input that fits the 64 MiB limit unless a smaller one already traps.

| `math.gcd(a, b)` | 2^16 / 2^17 bits | 4.65e9 / 18.4e9 (quadratic) | no | 2^18-bit operands (32 KiB each): **trap** (L3r3-1) |
| `math.lcm` | (calls `gcd`, `math.rs:1104-1105`) | same as gcd | no | same (code path) |
| `math.isqrt(a)` | 2^20 bits | 14.8e9 | no | 2^21 bits (256 KiB): **trap** (L3r3-1) |
| `a * b` (random) | 2^20 / 2^22 bits | 0.91e9 / 20.6e9 | no (PRE overshoot = full cost) | 2^23 bits (1 MiB): **trap** (L3r3-1) |
| `a // b`, `a % b` (random) | 2^20//2^19 / 2^22//2^21 bits | 2.26e9 / 18.4e9 | no | 2^23//2^22 bits (1 MiB by 512 KiB): **trap** (L3r3-1) |
| `pow(a, b, m)` | m 2^20 / 2^21 bits, e=3 | 9.3e9 / 25.7e9 | per exponent bit only | m 2^22 bits (512 KiB): **trap**; one squaring+reduction is unpolled (L3r3-1) |
| `decimal` sqrt | `getcontext().prec` 1e5 / 3e6, `Decimal(2).sqrt()` | 0.65e9 overshoot / - | between iterations only | prec 3e6, no input data at all: **trap** (L3r3-1) |

| `int(s, 16)` | 30M hex digits | 10.6e9 | no (PRE 29.97e9) | overshoot (L3r3-2) |

**Is the 64 MiB limit applied before one large allocation?** Yes, for every single large
allocation tried: `'a'.ljust(3e9)`, `'1'.zfill(3e9)`, `b'a'.ljust(3e9)`, `bytes(3e9)`,
`random.randbytes(3e9)`, `random.getrandbits(2.4e10)`, `int(Decimal('1e1000000000'))`,
`f"{'a':>3000000000}"` all raise `MemoryError: memory limit exceeded: ~3000032849 bytes >
67108864 bytes` (or a size error) within 0.7e6-1.1e6 instructions; `[0]*3e9` raises a bare
`MemoryError`; `'\t'.expandtabs(3e9)` raises OverflowError. No wasm out-of-memory trap.
(`bytearray` and `int.to_bytes` do not exist in Monty.) Per-item growth inside one native call is
checked periodically, so memory can exceed 64 MiB by up to ~1.5x before the error (`split`:
99 MB, `list(s)`: 80 MB, NFKC: 82 MB).

### grid-L3-r4

#### Coverage grid: L3 Resource bounds, round 4 — hash-collision quadratic work

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`. Lens L3: engine and host hash tables use public or unkeyed hashes, so
an attacker who chooses keys can force O(n^2) probing. Rows from `inventory.md`. Cells:
**finding** (candidate id below), **holds** (why), **n/a** (why).

Candidates returned by this round: **L3r4-1** (host-side converters, no budget applies),
**L3r4-2** (VM-side set/dict ops, one unpolled native op crosses 40e9 within the policy budget),
**L3r4-3** (root cause: no hash table in either engine has a secret seed — the "random" seed is
the fixed splitmix stream). Already filed and not repeated: bigint `**` and the native-op traps
of grid-L3-r3 (L3r3-1, L3r3-2); host converter cost per node (SW2-1-1).

##### The hash functions (all public or unkeyed — confirmed from source)

| Table | Hash | Keyed? | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Python `dict`/`set` (`PyHashTable`, hashbrown `HashTable<usize>`) | per-value `py_hash` | — | `monty-1.6.0/src/types/hash_table.rs:118-127` |
| Python `int` key hash | `HashValue::new(i.cast_unsigned())`; `new` only bit-inverts, `raw()` returns `i` | hash == the int itself | `monty-1.6.0/src/value.rs:1189-1190`, `src/hash.rs:70-84` |
| Python `str`/`bytes` key hash | `DefaultHasher::new()` = SipHash-1-3 with key **(0,0)** | unkeyed (fixed zero key) | `monty-1.6.0/src/hash.rs:160-186` |
| Boa object property table | `rustc_hash::FxHashMap` (FxHash) | unkeyed, trivially invertible | `boa_engine-0.22.0/src/object/shape/property_table.rs:5,11,19` |
| Boa `Map.groupBy`/`Object.groupBy` | `BuildHasherDefault<FxHasher>` | unkeyed | `boa_engine-0.22.0/src/builtins/map/mod.rs:707-735` |
| Boa `Map`/`Set` (`OrderedMap`, IndexMap) | std `RandomState` (SipHash) | seed from `getrandom` | `boa_engine-0.22.0/src/builtins/map/ordered_map.rs:5,39` |
| Boa shared-shape transitions | IndexMap with `RandomState` | seed from `getrandom` | `boa_engine-0.22.0/src/object/shape/shared_shape/mod.rs:365-369` |
| ahash tables (monty `AHashSet`, rhai) | ahash | seed from `getrandom` | `monty-1.6.0/src/types/hash_table.rs:31` |

The one seed source, `getrandom`, is the fixed deterministic splitmix64 stream
(`src/lib.rs:433-449`), seeded from the compile-time constant `0x9E3779B97F4A7C15` and never
reseeded. Its own comment says "fine for hash seeding." It is **not** fine against a chosen-key
adversary: the seed is public and constant, so an attacker computes the same SipHash/ahash the
canister will use and precomputes multi-collisions offline. FxHash and SipHash(0,0) have no seed
at all. **No hash table in engine or host has a secret seed (L3r4-3).** The grids were searched
for "collision"/"HashDoS": only the token-prefix cell existed; this is new.

##### How the collision bites

- **hashbrown `HashTable`** (Python dict/set) indexes into the control array by `hash & bucket_mask`
  and matches the top 7 bits as the control byte. For keys `i<<32` (i = 0,1,2,...) the raw hash is
  `i<<32`: the low 32 bits are all zero, so `hash & bucket_mask == 0` for every key (bucket_mask is
  far below 2^32). All N keys begin probing at bucket 0; insertion is O(n) per key, O(n^2) total.
  The control-byte (h2) differs, so lookups of *absent* keys stay cheap, but building the table, a
  set/dict intersection, union, `==`, `issuperset`, `symmetric_difference` and `dict.update` each
  re-probe the colliding region. Str keys reach the same state by SipHash(0,0) low-bit collisions.
- **FxHash** (Boa properties) is `state = (state ^ byte) * K`; a chosen key sets any target hash,
  so an attacker fixes `hash & mask` and the top bits alike — strictly easier than hashbrown.

##### Grid

| Row | Cell | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| U6 Script source (program) | **finding L3r4-2** | A token holder writes a script that builds a colliding `set`/`dict` and runs one set/dict operation over it. Construction via `set(range(0,N<<32,1<<32))` is polled (interrupted at the native-VM wall budget), but a single collection operation — `keys()&set`, `set==set`, `issuperset`, `symmetric_difference`, `dict.update(colliding_dict)` — runs to completion inside one native op with no budget poll. Native (R, private copy, release): N=20,000 colliding ints, `d={k:1 for k in s}; len(d.keys()&s)` ran 3.22 s against the 2 s native budget, ~1.2 s unpolled inside one op, vs 0.001 s for `set(range(N))`; 580x. On chain the same unpolled op reaches the 40e9 per-message limit within the default 20e9 policy budget → trap (same class as L3r3-1, F14). JS object-property and `Object.fromEntries`/`new Map`/`new Set` with FxHash-colliding keys are the Boa equivalent. |
| U8 Candid reply bytes from targets | **finding L3r4-1** | The decoded reply of a hostile allowlisted target is turned into engine values host-side: `python::from_json` (`src/runtimes/python.rs:104-115`) builds `MontyObject::dict` keyed by SipHash(0,0); `JsValue::from_json` (`src/runtimes/js.rs:403`) builds a JS object keyed by FxHash. Field names come from the target-authored `.did` (up to `MAX_DID_BYTES` = 512 KiB, `src/bridge.rs:186`): `idl_to_json` inserts each record field under `label_name` (`src/candid_bridge.rs:345-349`). A target whose return record has thousands of field names chosen to collide forces O(n^2) insertion. | B9 Python MontyObject<->JSON | **finding L3r4-1, L3r4-2** | JSON->MontyObject `from_json` dict keyed by SipHash(0,0) (host-side, L3r4-1); script-side `dict`/`set`/`json.loads` of a colliding object (L3r4-2). |
| V7 getrandom splitmix `STATE` (shared seed) | **finding L3r4-3** | This is the single seed for every ostensibly-randomised table (Boa Map/Set RandomState, Boa shape transitions, ahash). It is a fixed compile-time-seeded splitmix64 stream, so the seed is public and constant across replicas and runs. HashDoS mitigation that relies on an unpredictable seed is defeated. (The determinism itself is required for replica agreement, so the fix is not "make it random" but "key the untrusted-input tables with a value that is secret to the attacker, or bound the work" — see fixes.) |
| LIM2 `max_instructions` (default 20e9, settable u64) | **finding L3r4-1 (does not bound host path); L3r4-2** | For L3r4-2 the budget is the trap trigger: one unpolled colliding op added to a nearly-spent budget crosses 40e9 (as in L3r3-2). For L3r4-1 the budget is irrelevant — the host converter is not polled, so raising or lowering `max_instructions` neither prevents nor is honoured by the trap. A high `max_instructions` additionally lets a VM-side colliding op (L3r4-2) run further before the final post-run check, so it traps at 40e9 rather than ending with a clean `policy:` error. |

Same mechanism as L3r3-1; the collision just makes a cheap-looking op O(n^2). Trap = HTTP 503, no audit entry (nothing sent after the trap; register #11). |

### grid-L3-r5

#### Coverage grid: L3 Resource bounds, round 5 — Rhai replay cache, replay cost, ahash

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`. The Rhai-specific pass that L3-r4 and sweep-r2-5 left open. Rows from
`inventory.md`: W11, V10, LIM27, F13, B10 (plus the rows these measurements bound: LIM12,
LIM20, LIM29, V7). Cells: **finding**, **holds** (why), **n/a** (why). Evidence: R = reproduced
(native test, wasm32 harness or the port-8010 dev canister), C = code path.

Result: **no new finding**. W11 is bounded, and the bound is the instruction budget, not
Rhai's size limits. That bound was measured on chain. The earlier W11 "holds" figures (L4-r1:
about 85 MiB per run and 0.7 GiB for 8 runs) underestimated the per-run reply retention. They
did not change the verdict.

##### Method

- Private copy, shared build dir. In the copy only, a `PEAK` counter was added to the existing
  test allocator (`lib.rs` `counting_alloc`), and probe tests were appended to
  `rhai_rt.rs` (`w11_probe`). Replies were real Candid bytes decoded by
  `Service::decode_reply` with the real `DECODING_QUOTA`.
- wasm32 sizes: a probe cdylib (`icp_code_mode` with feature `rhai`, plus a counting global
  allocator) was built for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` and run in Node with `ic0` stubbed.
  `rhai_rt::run` was driven by 1 or 8 interleaved bridges.
- On chain (dev canister, port 8010, test token from `.env`): five `execute_icp_script` Rhai
  calls (K = 0, 1, 4, 8, 16, described below), each with one real `get_product` call to
  `demo_store`. Instructions were read from the newest audit entry. No setting was changed and
  nothing was deployed or upgraded. Side effect: the canister's `memory_size` high-water rose
  from 107,212,395 to 219,278,955 B. Wasm memory does not shrink, so this stays until the next
  upgrade.

##### Measurements

###### Largest reply per shape under the effective quota (native 64-bit, `decode_reply`)

| Reply type | Max accepted | Wire | Held as `Value` | Peak during decode |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | 399,998 chars | 400,008 B | 0.38 MiB | 0.76 MiB |
| `vec text` (200 B each) | 1,960 | 395,931 B | 0.44 MiB | 0.92 MiB |
| `vec null` | 99,999 | 12 B | 4.0 MiB | 13.0 MiB |
| `vec record {}` | 49,999 | 14 B | 2.0 MiB | 6.5 MiB |
| `vec record { a : null }` | 26,666 | 16 B | **17.1 MiB** (672 B/element: a BTreeMap leaf per 1-entry map) | 27.0 MiB |
| `vec record { "<L bytes>" : null }` | refused once L x n is above about 400,000 (L=1,000: n=100 ok, 1,000 refused) | 18 B | — | — |

The quota charges label bytes for every record (x50 untyped), so long field names from a
hostile `.did` do **not** amplify the held `Value`. My hypothesis that per-record key copies
could reach GBs is refuted (R).

Largest reply that Rhai also accepts (the array has 10,000 or fewer elements and the maps have
10,000 or fewer entries): `record { r : vec record { a : null }; t : text }` with 9,998 records
and a 250,007 B text. It is 250,031 B on the wire, holds **6.77 MiB native / 4.5 MiB wasm32**,
and peaks at 10.95 MiB during decode. A larger reply (26,000 records) ends the run uncatchably
on the next replay. `try` does not catch "Size of array/BLOB too large", and only 1 call was
made (R). So it is never retained next to later answers. This confirms L3-r1.

###### Retention in `answers` (25 call replies of the shape above plus 39 `icp::candid` texts of 512 KiB)

| Runs | `max_calls` | Script keeps answers | Native 64-bit peak | wasm32 peak above base / held at each await / `memory_size` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 25 (default) | no | 194.6 MiB | 136.4 / **105.0** / 161 MiB |
| 1 | 25 | yes | 330.9 MiB | 240.2 / 105.0 / 268 MiB |
| 8 | 25 | no | 1,480.7 MiB | 1,034.8 / 870.4 / 1,134 MiB |
| 8 | 25 | yes | 1,617.0 MiB | **1,138.7** / 870.4 / 1,240 MiB |
| 1 | 64 | no | 431.7 MiB | 287.2 / 275.3 / 321 MiB |
| 8 | 64 (operator-set) | no | 3,335.0 MiB | **2,214.4** / 2,202.5 / 2,380 MiB |

The native numbers are within 2x of the 3 GiB limit, so the limit question went on chain (next
table). Between replays only `answers` survives an await. Script-built Dynamics are dropped
when each `eval_ast` ends, which confirms L2-r2.

###### Retention without large replies: requests refused before any message

`IcBridge::call` refuses a method longer than 256 B (`bridge.rs:511`), and `candid` refuses a
bad canister id. Both refusals come before `reserve`, so they take no cap slot, send no message
and have no await. The `Request` is still kept in `answers`: canister text up to 1 MiB, method
text up to 1 MiB, and args up to the `ValueBudget` (4 MiB of text; Rhai does not count map
keys, see SW2-5b). One request kept 5.7 MiB (R native: k=63 gave 360.7 MiB per run, and 8 runs
x k=30 gave 1,375 MiB). Every later replay rebuilds, converts and compares each kept request.

On chain, the script was K refused requests of 5.5 MiB each (seven 512 KiB map keys, plus 1 MiB
canister text and 1 MiB method text) and then one real call:

| K | Result | Instructions (audit) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Ok | 242,586,541 |
| 1 | Ok | 730,782,383 |
| 4 | Ok | 3,143,285,012 |
| 8 | Ok | 8,662,753,177 |
| 16 | `policy: instruction budget exceeded (20053393702 > 20000000000)`, `PolicyViolation`, before the real call | 20,053,393,702 |

Fit: about 0.29B instructions per replay plus about 0.167B per kept request per replay, which
is about 29 instructions per retained byte per replay. The most one run can retain is
sqrt(2 x budget x S / c), about **90 MB** at the default 20B (K of about 13). The 40e9
per-message limit caps it at about 126 MB, because all these replays run in the first message.
For 8 runs that is about 0.7 to 1.0 GB, which is under 3 GiB by a factor of 3 or more. The
overshoot past the budget was 53M instructions, so the budget is polled at fine granularity.

###### Replay cost (item 2)

Native: one op that converts one cached 9,998-record answer (`to_dynamic` plus Rhai's size
check) takes 2.5 ms. Comparing a cached 4 MiB-args `Request` takes 0.33 ms (clone included).
A whole run with 25 large replies and 39 interface texts (65 replays) takes 4.3 s. All of this
happens inside native calls that run one Rhai operation at a time. `on_progress` checks the
deadline before the next operation, so the unpolled work per operation is one answer conversion
or one request comparison, which `DECODING_QUOTA` and `ValueBudget` bound. On chain, the K=16
run stopped cleanly at the budget (R). The quadratic replay cost is the register-accepted
ponytail (`rhai_rt.rs:195-196`). It is spent inside the budget, not between operations.

###### Rhai and ahash (item 3)

- Rhai uses ahash only through `func::hashing::get_hasher()` (`rhai-1.27.0/src/func/hashing.rs:57-63`).
  With no `RHAI_HASHING_SEED` that is `AHasher::default()`, the fixed keys from
  `get_fixed_seeds()[0]`. The build enables `ahash/runtime-rng` (rhai default) and
  `compile-time-rng`, and outside ahash's own tests the `runtime-rng` branch wins: 64 bytes
  drawn once from `getrandom`, which on wasm is the public splitmix stream (`lib.rs:433-449`,
  known L3r4-3). The keys are public up to the stream offset at first use.
- The hashes are u64 keys into `StraightHashMap` (std hashbrown with identity hashing): the
  function-resolution cache (`eval/cache.rs:27`, per evaluation, one lookup per call operation,
  polled), the strings interner (`types/interner.rs`, at most 256 entries of at most 32 B), the
  module and AST function index (at most 256 script functions), switch-case tables
  (`ast/stmt.rs:198`, filled at compile time), and closure and variable hashes.
- Forced collisions (R, native, keys read in-process): 9,000 switch-case string literals whose
  hashes share their low 15 bits (found in 48 s, 2.99e8 tries) compile in 744 ms. 9,000 random
  literals compile in 564 ms, with 37% more source text in the colliding case. Evaluation took
  12 µs. So there is no measurable quadratic blow-up: the probing is O(n/group) with u64 key
  comparisons, n is bounded by `MAX_CODE_BYTES`, and compile cost is already the known SW3-2-2.
- A full 64-bit collision (a 2^32 birthday search offline) would let two literals or two script
  functions share one hash, so a script would take the wrong switch arm or call the wrong
  function **in its own script**. `eval` is dispatched by name (`func/call.rs:614`) and disabled
  by symbol. Host functions are separate qualified hashes that the script can call anyway.
  Nothing crosses a run or the host boundary.
- `rhai::Map` is `BTreeMap<Identifier, Dynamic>` (`rhai-1.27.0/src/lib.rs:328`), so maps are
  immune to hash collisions. The JSON side is immune too: `serde_json::Map` is a BTreeMap,
  because `preserve_order` is not enabled (checked with `cargo tree -e features`).

##### Grid

| Row | Cell | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| W11 Rhai `answers` / replays | **holds** (R) | Each kept answer is limited by `DECODING_QUOTA` and by Rhai's element limits (an oversized answer ends the run uncatchably). Kept requests are limited by `ValueBudget` plus 1 MiB per string. Together they are bounded by `MAX_REQUESTS` and above all by the instruction budget, because every kept byte is re-processed on every later replay (about 29 instructions per byte per replay, on chain). Worst case measured: replies 105 MiB per run held across awaits (wasm32, default) and 1.14 GiB peak for 8 runs. Refused requests: about 90 MB per run within the default budget. Both are 2.5x or more under 3 GiB, and 2,380 MiB `memory_size` even at `max_calls` 64. The earlier W11 figures (L4-r1: 52 MiB, about 85 MiB per run, 0.7 GiB for 8) were low but led to the same verdict. |
| W11 vs "heap past `wasm_memory_limit` after an await" (L8-6) | **holds** (R) | `answers.push` runs in a response callback, where the limit is not enforced. But W11 alone reaches at most about 1.1 GiB (default) or 2.4 GiB (`max_calls` 64, 8 runs). Neither crosses 3 GiB. Reaching L8-6 through Rhai needs the in-engine route (SW2-5b, known). |
| V10 engine-internal statics (Rhai) | **holds** (C) | Rhai statics are constant tables plus three write-once cells (`HASHING_SEED`, `INDEXER_HASHES`, `DUMMY_RESOLVER`). ahash's `SEEDS` `OnceBox` is filled once per instance. Nothing grows across runs. The engine, its `StandardPackage` and its caches are rebuilt for each run in `build_engine`. |
| V7 shared seed stream (Rhai's use) | known (L3r4-3); **holds** for Rhai's harm | Rhai's ahash keys are public, as above. The only effects are a measured, insignificant collision cost and same-script mis-dispatch. Maps are BTreeMaps. |
| LIM27 Rhai limits | **holds** (R) | `MAX_REQUESTS` 64 is reachable without spending cap slots (interface texts and refused requests), and each answer costs a full replay. 1M operations per replay are polled, and the budget stops the run cleanly (K=16 on chain). The array limit refuses oversized replies uncatchably (R). Map keys are not counted (known SW2-5b). The 1 MiB string limit does not apply to error values thrown by host requests: a 3 MiB mock error reached `catch (e)` with `e.len() == 3145728` (R, native). But no on-chain error source above 1 MiB was found (the largest is the L9-6 interface parse error, at most about 512 KiB), so this is not a finding. |
| LIM12 8 runs | **holds** (R) | 8 runs interleaved at awaits were measured. Totals as in W11. |
| LIM20 `DECODING_QUOTA` | holds as the per-answer bound (R). Its size (x50) is known L9-4 | The largest held `Value` from one reply is 17.1 MiB native (`vec record { a : null }`, 16 B on the wire). Label bytes are charged (R). |
| LIM29 3 GiB | **holds** for W11 (R) | See W11. |
| F13 out of memory (Rhai) | known (SW2-5b) for in-engine memory; **holds** for `answers` (R) | The replay cache alone does not reach the limit, as measured above. |
| B10 Rhai JSON <-> Dynamic | **holds** (R) | `to_dynamic` runs once per cached answer per replay, inside one operation (2.5 ms native for the largest answer Rhai accepts). The size check runs after conversion, but the input is quota-bounded. `to_json_value` is bounded by `ValueBudget`, and the comparison is bounded by the same. Map keys and `FnPtr` are known (SW2-5b). |

##### Not tested

- On-chain retention of large **replies** (the 9,998-record shape) needs a target canister
  that returns it. Deploying one is outside this phase. The on-chain instruction cost was
  measured only for the refused-request route. The reply route's cost per replay was not
  measured on chain, so its own budget ceiling is unknown. The memory figures above assume
  the runs finish within budget.
- 8 concurrent runs on chain were not attempted. Driving `memory_size` toward 3 GiB is
  destructive. Only the native figures and the wasm32 harness were used.
- IC charges for `memory.copy` versus a byte loop were not separated. The cost of about 29
  instructions per byte is measured end to end.
- Whether the platform caps reject-message size, which would bound the error-string route
  under LIM27, was not checked.
