### grid-L4-r1

#### Coverage grid: L4 Multiplication, round 1

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`. Lens question: what happens when this is done N times at once, or
N times in one request? Rows are from `inventory.md`; `file:line` is commit `295d64b`.

Evidence keys: **R** reproduced (native test in a private copy, or a request to the local
network on port 8010; nothing was deployed or reconfigured), **C** the code path produces it
unambiguously. Candidate findings are numbered L4-1 ... L4-5 (see the end of this file).

##### Cells

| Row | Verdict | Reason / evidence |
|---|---|---|
| LIM1 `max_calls_per_script` | **finding L4-1, L4-2** | The cap counts slots, not messages: one interface-fetch slot (`IcBridge::candid`, `src/bridge.rs:486`) can send two messages (`fetch_did`, `src/bridge.rs:424-437`: `canister_metadata`, then `__get_candid_interface_tmp_hack`), so a run can send up to 2x the cap (C). Slots are also spent on duplicate fetches of the same interface inside one batch (L4-1, R). Boundary: `authorize` refuses at `calls_made >= max` (25 allowed, 26th refused; `policy::execution_caps`), holds. Cap 1: any call to an uncached canister needs 2 slots (call + fetch) and is refused when cold, accepted when warm (C, documented by CL7 "every interface fetch that misses the cache", folded into L4-1) |
| LIM8 `MAX_BATCH` 50 | holds | Checked right after parsing in both paths (`src/mcp.rs:295`); bounds messages per request, so per-message work (search render, tools/list) is multiplied by at most 50. Guard `mcp::replies_always_fit`. Query-path consequence of 50 searches: see LIM9 |
| LIM9 `MAX_SEARCHES` 5 | **finding L4-3** | Enforced only in `http_update` (`src/mcp.rs:395`). `http_query` answers up to 50 cached searches (R: 6 and 50 answered). The same 6-search batch gets 6 answers when every interface is cached and 5 answers + `-32600` when one needs a fetch (whole batch upgraded) or when `certified_reads` is on (R). A batch whose cold search is 6th or later is upgraded on every attempt and never fetches it (C) |
| LIM10 one script per request | holds | `ran_script` flag (`src/mcp.rs:392`), set even when the script is refused as busy. Guard `mcp::one_tool_call_per_request`. Register #26 re-checked: each `IcBridge` takes its own `base_instructions` (`src/bridge.rs:318`), so tools in one request no longer share a counter |
| LIM12 `MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS` 8 | **finding L4-4 (searches excluded), L4-5 (slot held across unbounded wait)** | Scripts: capped and returned on drop (guard `lib::run_slots_are_capped_and_returned`), holds. Searches take no slot (`run_search`, `src/lib.rs:121`) but suspend across interface fetches holding the request body, the parsed batch and their args (C). A slot is held for the whole run, including an `unbounded_wait` call (default `call_timeout_seconds = null`), so 8 runs waiting on a target that does not reply refuse every other script (C; needs a non-replying allowlisted target, register #55) |
| LIM25 JS rounds/pending/jobs | holds | 64 rounds x 64 pending = 4,096 requests max; requests beyond the call cap are refused before any await (`reserve`), cost one policy check each, and add at most 16 violations + a counter (`deny`, `src/bridge.rs:356-366`). Budget checked after every round (`src/runtimes/js.rs:376`) and every 256 jobs. `icp.candid` of a cached interface takes no slot, so a run can copy the interface text up to 4,096 times into JS; that is memory the script controls, i.e. register #24 (JS has no memory cap, accepted), not a new multiplication |
| LIM27 Rhai `MAX_REQUESTS` 64, 1M ops per replay | holds | Each request costs one replay; replays of cached answers do not resend (`request`, `src/runtimes/rhai_rt.rs:64-83`). Replay work is O(n^2) in requests but every Rhai operation checks the policy budget (`on_progress`), so the run stops at `max_instructions`. Register #13 re-checked: `answers.len() >= MAX_REQUESTS` holds |
| E5a `execute_icp_script` | holds (multiplication); see L4-1 | Per request: 1 script, own call cap, own budget measured from its own start. Batching inside the script multiplies interface fetches (L4-1) |
| E5b `search_icp_canisters` | **finding L4-3, L4-4**; budget holds | Per request up to 5 searches, each with its own 25-slot cap and full instruction budget. Searches in one request run sequentially, so search 2..5 see the cache filled or `DID_FAILED` set by search 1 and do not refetch the same canister (C). Each search can fetch a different set of up to 25 canisters, so one request can fetch up to 125 interfaces (up to 250 messages), but each canister is fetched at most once per TTL in steady state: bounded by allowlist size, holds. Budget sharing in one execution: render of a ~1.9 MB, ~950k-keyword query over demo_store's interface takes 223 ms natively (R, release build), far from the 20e9 headroom between the default budget and the 40e9 message limit, holds at the default budget |

A reply over Rhai's limits ends the run uncatchably on the next replay (`Size of array/BLOB too large`, 1 call made), so it is never retained alongside others. 64 retained interface texts of <= 512 KiB add <= 32 MiB. Until an update-path search or script uses the override, every query-path search re-parses each override in scope (up to 512 KiB), up to 50 times per batch. | CL9 "five searches per HTTP request (further ones get -32600)" | **finding L4-3** | Not true in the query path (50) |
| CL15 "One entry per outbound message ... `calls` counts messages sent" | holds; consequence of L4-2 | `calls` can exceed `max_calls_per_script` (up to 2x) |
| CL36 "Searches are cheap and size-capped, so they are exempt" | holds for cost (see E5b); see L4-4 for concurrency |

| Register #27 search keeps fetching after the cap | holds | `halted` stops further fetches after any `policy:` refusal (`src/lib.rs:132-144`); guard manual |

| Register #29 unlimited concurrent scripts | holds for scripts (guard exists); searches excluded: L4-4 | |
| Retries / replays of a whole request | not applicable (no promise made) | The HTTP gateway turns a client retry into a new ingress message, so a retried `tools/call` re-runs the script and repeats any update calls (e.g. `create_order`). Nothing dedups by JSON-RPC id; the tool is not annotated idempotent (MCP default `idempotentHint: false`), so no claim is broken |

##### Candidate findings

- **L4-1** Concurrent requests for one uncached interface each send their own fetch (no in-flight dedup). Within one JS `Promise.all` / Python `gather`, N calls to a cold canister take N call slots + N fetch slots and send N identical fetches; a batch of 13 calls succeeds when the interface is cached and fails with a policy violation when it is not. Across concurrent requests (scripts or searches), every in-flight request repeats the fetch messages and their audit entries until the first reply fills the cache.
- **L4-2** One call-cap slot can send two messages (fetch fallback), so a run can send up to 2x `max_calls_per_script` messages and its audit `calls` can exceed the configured cap.
- **L4-3** `MAX_SEARCHES` is enforced only in the update path: the same batch of searches gets all answers from the query and 5 answers + errors once upgraded (one cold interface, or `certified_reads`); a cold search at position 6+ is never fetched.
- **L4-4** Searches take no run slot, so concurrent searches suspended on interface fetches are not bounded by `MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS` and are invisible in `active_runs` (they do appear in `pending_run_ids`).
- **L4-5** A run slot is held across an unbounded-wait call; 8 runs waiting on a target that never replies make every later script "busy" until those calls return (symptom of register #44's root cause, new consequence).

### grid-L4-r4

#### Coverage grid: L4 Multiplication, round 4 (canister callers: the ingress size bound x5)

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`. Lens question: what happens when this is done N times at once, or N
times in one request? This round asks it of the request size itself. The inventory bounds U1-U5,
W1 and W3 by the 2 MiB ingress limit. A same-subnet canister that holds a token is not bound by
that limit: it is bound by the inter-canister payload limit. `file:line` refers to commit `295d64b`.

Evidence keys: **R** reproduced on the project's local icp-cli network (port 8010), **C** the code
path produces it unambiguously.

##### Setup (Live phase)

- Fixture: a purpose-built caller canister (not in the repository; `ic-cdk 0.20.3`, `candid
  0.10.40`, built in a private temp dir with the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`). Its `send(prefix,
  filler, n, suffix, method, token)` method builds the HTTP body inside the canister as `prefix +
  filler*n + suffix`, calls `http_request_update` (or `http_request`) with `Call::unbounded_wait`,
  and returns the status, the first and last bytes of the reply, any reject, and its own cycle
  spend. `blast(n, ...)` / `blast_oneway(n, ...)` send n small calls concurrently. The test token
  went in through an `--args-file` init argument written from `.env` by a script and deleted right
  after install. It was never printed or passed on a command line.
- Targets:
  - the live `icp_code_mode` (`4caro-...`, module `224cfa7a...`, built from HEAD, see
    grid-L13-r2) for the size and search tests. Caller `4zfnl-5t777-77775-aaadq-cai`.
  - a **throwaway copy** of the audited module (`.icp/cache/artifacts/icp_code_mode`, sha256
    `ad3ee221...`, same commit) installed in detached canister `5uljf-s3777-77775-aaaea-cai`,
    with the same token hash and the same 13-method allowlist (ledger 5 + demo_store 8),
    default limits. Caller `5tkpr-7d777-77775-aaaeq-cai`. Used for the memory tests, so the
    shared canister's heap high-water mark would not be pushed toward 3 GiB, and for the cost
    tests, so other agents' traffic would not add noise.
- No setting of `icp_code_mode` was changed, and it was not deployed. Limits read back
  afterwards were the defaults (25 calls, 20e9 instructions, no timeout, no certified reads).
  All three fixture canisters were deleted (cycles recovered). Side effects on the live canister:
  memory size went from 380,391,208 B to 481,120,040 B (heap high-water mark from the 10.48 MB
  search below; it stays until the next upgrade), about 0.2T test cycles spent, and audit entries
  9911-9913, 9976-9978 plus a few in between that are mine (the PolicyViolation search and script
  runs below).

##### Candidate findings

###### L4r4-1 Canister callers send 10 MiB bodies; one search at the default allowlist traps at 40e9 and leaves no record (Medium, R)

- Lens L4 (and L3/L5). Invariants I4 (bounded cost), I5 (clean failure), I3 (a run that ended
  over budget has no entry).
- Where: `src/mcp.rs:374-412` (`http_update`: no body-size limit, runs every item in one
  execution), `src/search.rs:80-82` (`keywords`: unbounded count), `src/search.rs:116-121`
  (every keyword checked against every allowed method), `src/lib.rs:150-154` (budget compared
  only after `render` returns).
- Repro (R, live `icp_code_mode`, default limits and allowlist): from a same-subnet canister
  holding the token, call `http_request_update` with body
  `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"search_icp_canisters","arguments":{"query":"-> -> ... (3,000,000 times)"}}}`
  (9,000,112 B). Reply: reject `IC0522 ... exceeded the limit of 40000000000 instructions`.
  Target paid 40.01B cycles, the caller 10.03B, and the audit length was unchanged. At
  2,000,000 keywords (6 MB) the same request returns `policy: instruction budget exceeded
  (26704841870 > 20000000000)` and writes a `PolicyViolation` entry.
- Batch variant (R, B2, known root SW3-5-2): `[Python while-loop script, search "-> " x 1.6M]`
  (4.8 MB) traps. The script, which spent its 20e9 and would have closed `PolicyViolation`
  (B0), leaves no entry. The same pair at ingress size (B1, 2.07 MB) completes and is audited.
- Why it is new: SW3-5-2 and L5-4 judged reachability against "the HTTP body caps the keywords
  at about 1M" and estimated that about 85 allowed methods were needed. A canister caller gets
  5x the bytes, and `"-> "` costs about 13,350 instructions per keyword over 13 methods (vs
  about 5,000 for `"( "`). So a single search traps at the demo's 13 methods with no
  configuration change.
- Refutation tried: `"( "` at the maximum size stays at 26.6e9 (K3, no trap); the query route
  stops at 5e9 (Q2); `MAX_SEARCHES` does not help because one search suffices; the caller pays
  about 1,233 cycles/byte, so the cost amplification (4x-7.5x) is lower than an ingress token
  holder gets for free. The finding is the unrecorded trap at default settings, not the cost.
- Fix: bound the work before doing it. Cap keyword count and length in `parse_tool_call` or
  `keywords`, check the instruction counter inside the `render` loop, and enforce one per-request
  budget across all items (the SW3-5-2 fix). Also cap the body size in `http_update` (for
  example 2 MiB, matching ingress), so canister callers get no larger inputs than gateway callers.
- Pattern for the sweep: *a bound taken from one entry path's transport limit (ingress 2 MiB)
  and assumed for every caller of the same method*.

###### L4r4-2 The request parser keeps three full copies of untrusted `params` as `serde_json` trees: about 1,300 bytes of heap per 5 body bytes, 2.70 GB high-water from one request (Medium, R)

- Lens L4/L3 (L18 cost). Invariant I4 (no caller can make the canister hold unbounded memory).
- Where: `src/mcp.rs:293-304` (`parse_body` builds the whole `Value` tree), `src/mcp.rs:255`
  (`classify`: `msg.get("params").cloned()`), `src/mcp.rs:212` (`parse_tool_call`:
  `params.get("arguments").cloned()`). The tree is a `BTreeMap` per object (no
  `preserve_order`), so a one-key object costs a full leaf node.
- Repro (R, throwaway copy of the audited module, empty-ish heap of 73 MB):
  `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"execute_icp_script","arguments":{"code":"return 1","pad":[ ... ]}}}`
  - `pad` = `{"":0}` x 299,000 (2.09 MB, fits ingress): memory size 73 MB -> 478 MB, result `1`;
  - `pad` = `{"":0}` x 1,497,000 (10.48 MB, canister caller): -> 2.08 GB;
  - `pad` = 17,400 single-key objects nested 120 deep (10.47 MB): -> 2.70 GB, result `1`.
  The wasm heap never shrinks, so idle burn stays at 69.9B cycles/day until an upgrade. The
  copy at 73 MB burned about 1.9B/day (estimated from the live 481 MB at 13.2B/day). The
  caller paid 11.06B once.
- Not shown: a trap. The densest shape found peaks at about 2.7 GB on a fresh heap. Together
  with suspended runs holding memory (JS is uncapped, register #24) the request would trap
  instead. A trap rolls the growth back, so the lasting effect is the cost, and only a request
  that succeeds leaves the high-water mark behind.
- Relation to known findings: the "high-water never shrinks" cost is L18-8/L8-6, and those
  triggers are script heaps. This trigger runs before any script, budget or language. It needs
  only a valid token, and it works through ingress too (+404 MB at 2.09 MB). A canister caller
  makes it 5x larger.
- Fix: refuse bodies over a fixed size before parsing (`http_update` and `http_query`). Read
  `params`/`arguments` by reference (`get`/`as_str`) instead of cloning. Reject unknown
  `arguments` fields (this also closes the known "unknown fields accepted" finding at
  `src/mcp.rs:202-228`).
- Pattern for the sweep: *untrusted input copied in full where only a few scalar fields are
  read*. Other candidates to check: `classify` `id` clone (bounded by echo/`finish`), JS
  `args_json` + parsed `Value` + `enc.bytes` held across awaits (sweep-r3-2 "not tested").

##### Not tested, and why

- **Cross-subnet canister callers** (2 MiB inter-canister limit): the local network has one
  subnet. Mainnet behaviour, including whether the 10 MiB same-subnet limit applies to an
  application subnet's own canisters, is unverified (register #57).
- **Mainnet cost ratios**: cycles here are the local network's prices (about 1.06
  cycles/instruction observed). The ratios in VF3 hold only if mainnet charges caller and callee
  the same way.
- **A parse-path trap** (body peak over 3 GiB): not reached at 10 MiB on an empty heap. It was
  not combined with 8 suspended JS runs holding memory, because doing that on the shared canister
  would block other agents (another lens already saw the 3 GiB limit block every update). On the
  copy it would only add a trap, with no lasting effect beyond L4r4-2.
- **5 searches x 2 MiB each in one batch**: the fixture's `filler` primitive repeats one unit,
  and an ingress argument to the fixture is capped at 4 MiB by the local gateway, so a batch of
  five big searches could not be expressed. A single search already traps (K5), so this adds
  nothing.
- **Rhai/JS budget-burning script + search**: only Python was used for B0-B2. The Python run
  stopped cleanly at its 20e9 budget, and the trap comes from the sum, so the language does not
  matter.
- The live canister's high-water mark grew by about 101 MB from K3 (keyword strings). This was
  not reversed: shrinking it takes an upgrade, which is outside this lens's remit.

##### Candidates

- **L5-1** (Medium, R): authenticated update requests that run no tool cost the canister up to ~4B cycles each (1.9 MB body) and write no audit entry; a search in the update path up to 8.7B. README:411 says only two kinds of request write no entries.
- **L5-2** (Medium, C): a search touching an allowlisted canister whose interface fetch failed in the last 5 minutes is always upgraded to a paid update and writes no audit entry; the tool description tells the AI model searches are free and use no consensus round.
- **L5-3** (Low, R): any canister, without a token, makes icp_code_mode pay 5.2M-7.1M cycles per call to `http_request_update`, admin methods or `http_request`; the README and code comment say tokenless update calls are refused before the canister is charged / callers pay for themselves.
- **L5-4** (Medium, R): search rendering cost grows with keyword count x allowed methods and is checked against `max_instructions` only afterwards; 925k keywords over 13 methods = ~12B instructions, 8.69B cycles, reported as success, no audit entry.
- **L5-5** (Medium, R native + C): demo_store accepts zero-quantity lines from anyone, so one ~2 MB `create_order` stores ~170k lines; two such orders make `list_orders(null)` a 4.08 MB reply (over the IC reply limit), and repeated orders exhaust its heap; demo_store pays for every call.
- **L5-6** (Low, R native): demo_store oversells: duplicate lines in one order pass the availability check against the same stock; `reserved` wraps with `restock(p, u32::MAX)`.

##### Not tested

- Cycles reserved for in-flight calls (response prepayment) held by 8 scripts x 64 pending unbounded-wait calls against a target that never replies: needs a misbehaving target canister (register #55); not deployed in this phase.
- Cost to a purpose-built attacking canister per call (only the generic proxy's cost was measured, 13.3M per call), so the amplification factor of L5-3 is not established.
- Mainnet fee schedule and gateway behaviour (register #57); local fees match a 13-node subnet only by observation.
- The search 40B-trap extrapolation in L5-4 (needs an allowlist of about 45+ methods, i.e. a settings change reserved for the Live phase).
- Duplicate-line oversell and the 170k-line order were reproduced natively only (demo_store live data is shared with other agents and was left untouched).

### grid-L5-r2

#### Coverage grid: L5 Cost and payment, round 2 (value-moving flows, live)

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`. Lens question: who pays, and can someone else make them pay? This
round covers the one flow round 1 left as "needs a controller": a value-moving method
(`icrc1_transfer`, legacy `transfer`) on the local ICP ledger `ryjl3-tyaaa-aaaaa-aaaba-cai`,
driven end to end through the MCP gateway.

Evidence keys: **R** = reproduced live on the project's local icp-cli network (port 8010,
`icp_code_mode` = `4caro-hl777-77775-aaaba-cai`, module hash `ad3ee221...` = the audited
build, not redeployed by this lens); **C** = code path.

##### Setup and restoration (Live phase)

- Test funds: 300M test ICP sent from the local `anonymous` identity to the canister's
  default ledger account (blocks 496, 498). Destinations were subaccounts `..01`-`..0c` of
  `anonymous`.
- Allowlist: `icrc1_transfer` added to the ledger entry at 11:06 UTC (later `transfer` as
  well, for the memo test); restored afterwards to the original five read methods (see "Restoration" at the end).
- `set_limits` was changed once to `max_instructions = 25_000_000` for one run (SW3-2 test)
  and immediately set back to the defaults (25 calls, 20_000_000_000, no timeout, no
  certified reads); `get_policy` confirmed the restore.
- Interface cache was evicted with `remove_allowlist` + `set_allowlist` to get cold-cache runs.
- The test token was read from `.env` by a helper script and never printed.
- Interference seen: between 11:08 and 11:09 UTC every update call to `icp_code_mode`
  failed with "Canister exceeded its current Wasm memory limit of 3221225472 bytes" (memory
  size 3.42 GB; a `Trapped` search run against another lens's fault-injection canister
  `4qggx-...` precedes it). Someone else reinstalled the same module (memory back to 95 MB,
  stable state kept). Later all 8 run slots were held by another lens's `hang` runs, which
  blocked scripts ("busy") for minutes. Neither is a finding of this lens; both are noted
  for L3/L18/L4-5.

| Audit of value moves (D4, CL15, README "How to read the audit log") | **finding** L5r2-3 | An entry records only `canister.method`; no argument hash, amount, recipient or reply. M9: a transfer and its refused duplicate both close `Ok` with identical entries. M5/M7: the run that moved 1 ICP closes `Error` "script exceeded 64 host round-trips"; README:404-406 defines `Error` as "the script failed" and README:397-398 says "Whether the target executed it is in the script's result or error", but here the ledger's reply (block 501/502) reached the canister and was discarded, so neither the client, the result, nor the audit has it. M11: closes `PolicyViolation`, which README:406 describes as "A call was refused by policy, or the instruction budget ran out", while the call was not refused |
| I2 policy precedes effect | violated (R, M11) | Budget checked before the await only (SW3-2). Allowlist re-check after the await: C (L1-2), not reproduced live |
| I3 records match reality | violated (R, M5, M7, M9, M11) | See L5r2-3 |
| I8 fidelity | violated (R, M1, M4) | See L5r2-4 |

##### Candidates

- **L5r2-1** (Critical per the plan's rule "grade by the worst outcome demonstrated": loss of
  value; narrow trigger; root cause SW5-1, this is its value consequence and a regrade
  request). A transfer that is the last request of a JS run reaching round 64 (or a Python
  run reaching suspension 256) is executed, its reply is discarded, and the client is told
  the script failed; a retry of the same `tools/call` executes it again. R: M5+M6 moved
  2 ICP for two `isError:true` replies; M7 for Python. Ledger dedup does not help unless the
  script hard-codes `created_at_time` (M8-M10). Fix: the SW5-1 fix (re-check the promise /
  `progress` after the loop or count before dispatch, as Rhai does); plus, for any run that
  sent messages, never report a bare failure: include the sent-message list and say the
  effects may have happened.
- **L5r2-2** (High: value moved while the run is reported as a policy refusal; root cause
  SW3-2, value consequence). With a cold interface cache the instruction budget is checked
  before the fetch and not again before the send: M11 moved 1 ICP at 32.8M instructions
  with a 25M budget and reported `policy: instruction budget exceeded`. At the default 20B
  budget the overshoot window is the fetch + parse + encode (about 14M instructions for the
  ledger interface), i.e. only scripts that spent ~19.98B first. Fix: re-check budget and
  allowlist in `call` right before `self.sent` (also closes L1-2).
- **L5r2-3** (Medium: an operator is misled). The audit log cannot show whether or how much
  value moved: no args/amount/recipient/reply in entries; a ledger-refused duplicate and a
  real transfer both close `Ok` (M9); runs that moved value close `Error` (M5, M7) or
  `PolicyViolation` (M11), contrary to README:397-398, 404-406. Fix: record a hash of the
  encoded args and the reply status (or the first bytes of the reply) on the message entry
  when the reply arrives, and give the closing entry a status that distinguishes "script
  failed after N messages were sent" from "nothing was sent".
- **L5r2-4** (High per the scale "return wrong data as if it were right", for identifiers;
  root cause L7-3, value consequence and a regrade request). R: M1 moved 9_007_199_254_740_992
  for a script that wrote 9007199254740993, reported `Ok`. The amount error is at most one
  ulp; M4 shows the identifier case: a legacy `transfer` with memo 12345678901234567 was
  recorded in block 515 with memo 12345678901234568, reported `Ok`. Fix: refuse JS/Python numbers
  that are not safe integers where a `nat`/`int` is expected ("pass it as a string"), as the
  output side already does.

##### Restoration

- 11:17 UTC: the canister's remaining test ICP (2_978_400_735_587_022 e8s) returned to the
  `anonymous` default account by a script (block 516); the canister's ledger balance is 0.
  Test ICP sent to `anonymous` subaccounts `..01`-`..0c` stays with `anonymous`.
- Ledger allowlist entry set back to the original five methods (`icrc1_balance_of`,
  `icrc1_symbol`, `icrc1_decimals`, `icrc1_metadata`, `icrc1_total_supply`); `get_policy`
  diffed against the snapshot taken before: identical except two allowlist entries added by
  another lens (`4qggx-...`, `4xhad-...`). Limits at defaults. Network left running.

##### Not tested

- L1-2 race live: the window is one round (~0.12 s locally); four timed attempts missed it.
  A deterministic test needs a hook to hold the fetch reply (e.g. a target whose
  `canister_metadata` is slow, or a PocketIC test that controls rounds).
- Gateway-initiated retries: whether the HTTP gateway (local or boundary node) re-submits a
  timed-out `http_request_update` was not observed; only client retries (M6) were. A script
  waiting on a slow target past the gateway timeout would make the client see a failure
  while the run continues: not tested (needs a slow target and the gateway's timeout).
- 18-decimal ICRC tokens (ckETH-like), where every amount above ~0.009 token exceeds 2^53:
  no such ledger on the local network, and installing one means downloading a ledger Wasm.
- Rhai transfer at request 64: not run live (slots held by other runs); native result cited.
- ICRC-2 `icrc2_approve`/`icrc2_transfer_from` (allowance amounts and expiry are nat/nat64):
  not allowlisted or tested; same converter, same expectation as M1.

### grid-L6-r1

#### Coverage grid, lens L6 (Consistency across variants), round 1

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`. Row ids from `inventory.md`. Cells: **finding** (id below), **holds**
(why), **n/a** (why). Evidence: *live* = request to the project's local network on port 8010
(read-only or ordinary token-holder requests; no deploy, no settings changed); *native* =
differential test in a private copy (`cargo test --lib`, shared target dir); *code* = code path.

##### Candidate findings

| Id | Sev | Title | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| L6-1 | High | JS enforces the instruction budget only between host round-trips; ordinary synchronous JS (loops inside called functions) runs to the IC's 40B trap. Python and Rhai stop in-engine | live + native |
| L6-2 | High | Python's VM budget is not checked inside a single native operation (bigint `**`, `str()` of a large list); one expression runs past the budget to the 40B trap | live + native |
| L6-3 | Medium | JS counts value text in UTF-16 code units, Python/Rhai in UTF-8 bytes: JS lets 3x the documented 4 MiB of text leave a script | native |
| L6-4 | Medium | Python `print` bypasses the shared log and value paths: it raises `MemoryError` at the 64 KiB cap (JS/Rhai truncate and succeed), and printed values are formatted without the value limits | live + native |
| L6-5 | Medium | Rhai rejects replies JS and Python accept (arrays/maps over 10,000 entries, strings over 1 MiB) after the call has executed | native |
| L6-6 | Medium | Per-language builds still advertise all three languages and default to `javascript` in `tools/list`; a Rhai-only worker fails every call that omits `language` | native |
| L6-7 | Low | Query-path search ignores the failed-fetch cache the update path honours, so every search touching a failing interface is upgraded to a paid update call | code |
| L6-8 | Low | `MAX_SEARCHES` (5 per HTTP request) is enforced on the update path only; the query path answers 8 of 8, the update path 5 of 8 for the same batch | native |
| L6-9 | Low | A value the host cannot represent is dropped (JS), stringified as `Repr('<function f at 0xc>')` (Python) or refused (Rhai) | native |
| L6-10 | Low | Depth limit off by one between runtimes: 129 nested empty lists pass in Python and Rhai, fail in JS | native |

<a id="grid-L7-r3"></a>

### grid-L7-r3

#### Grid: L7 Data fidelity, round 3 (stale or overridden interface vs. Candid opt-subtyping)

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`. Reviewer: L7 lens agent, round 3. Question: can a value the target
actually sent (or the script actually passed) reach the other side as `null` or missing while
the run is audited `Ok`, and does the script get any signal?

Method: private copy of the tree (no `target/`, no `design/`, no `.env`), shared
`CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, probe module `src/audit_l7r3.rs` in the copy only (not committed),
`cargo test --lib audit_l7r3 -- --nocapture`. Each probe encodes a value under the target's
NEW type with candid (`IDLArgs::to_bytes_with_types`), checks the new type decodes it back
exactly, then decodes the same bytes with the app's `Service::decode_reply` under the OLD
(cached or override) type. Evidence: **R** = reproduced natively, **C** = code path
unambiguous. Candidate finding: **L7r3-1**.

Probe results (all R, native):

| Probe | Target's new type vs. app's cached type | Reply the target sent | What the app returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | `info : opt record { amount : nat }` -> `amount : text` | `{"id":1,"info":{"amount":"12 ICP"}}` | `Ok({"id":1,"info":null})` |
| P1c control | same change, not under `opt` | same | `Err("candid decoding failed ...")` |
| P2 | `get_customer : (nat64) -> (opt Customer)`, `Tier` gains `Platinum` | customer 7, tier `Platinum` | `Ok(null)` (customer "does not exist") |
| P2 | same, tier `Gold` | customer 7, tier `Gold` | correct object (loss is value-dependent) |
| P2c control | `list : () -> (vec Customer)` | `[customer 7, Platinum]` | `Err(...)` |
| P2b | `status : opt variant { Pending; Done }` gains `Refunded : nat` | `{"id":3,"status":{"Refunded":500}}` | `Ok({"id":3,"status":null})` |
| P2v | `vec opt variant { A; B }` gains `C` | `[A, C, B]` | `Ok([A, null, B])` (element-wise) |
| P3 | `opt record { a }` gains required `b : text` | `{"a":1,"b":"new"}` | `Ok({"a":1})`, `b` dropped |
| P3r | cached type requires `b`, target dropped it | `{"a":1}` | `Ok(null)`, `a` lost too |
| P3n | `meta : opt record { owner; memo : nat64 }` -> `memo : text` | `{"id":9,"meta":{...}}` | `Ok({"id":9,"meta":null})`, `owner` lost too |
| P4 | lying interface: `(record {id;name})` declared as `(opt record {id;name})` | `{"id":1,"name":"x"}` | correct object |
| P4 | lying interface: declared `(opt record { id : text })` | same | `Ok(null)` |
| P4 | lying interface: declared `(opt nat)` | same | `Ok(null)` |
| P4c control | honest wrong type, no `opt` wrap | same | `Err(...)` |
| P5 | `() -> (nat)` cached, target returns `(nat, text)` | `[5,"lost"]` | `Ok(5)`, second value dropped |
| P5b | `(nat, opt text)` cached, target returns `(nat, nat)` | `[5,6]` | `Ok([5,null])` |
| P6 | P2 through a full run, JS / Python / Rhai, bridge = P2 trip | - | all three `Ok("no such customer")`, logs `[]` |
| P7 | outbound: cached arg `memo : opt nat64`, target now `memo : opt blob` | script passes `memo: 42` | target decodes `memo = null` and would execute the update |

| Row | Cell | Reason / evidence |
|---|---|---|
| U8 Candid reply bytes from targets | **finding** L7r3-1 | `decode_reply` (`src/candid_bridge.rs:96-110`) decodes typed against `func.rets` from whatever interface `service()` returned, with skipping on and no check that the wire types match the expected types. Candid's rule (`candid-0.10.40/src/de.rs:1156-1174`, `recoverable_visit_some` :801-842) turns any value under `opt` that does not fit the expected type into `None`; extra fields and extra return values are skipped. Result: real reply data becomes `null` or disappears, returned as `Ok` (R, P1-P5). Outside `opt` the same mismatch is a loud error (R, P1c, P2c, P4c), so the loss is exactly where the README says `null` means "absent" ("Opt is a value or `null`", README.md:356) |
| B6 Candid -> JSON (`idl_to_json`) | **finding** L7r3-1 (via U8) | `idl_to_json` maps `IDLValue::None` to `null` (`src/candid_bridge.rs:331`), identical to a real `null`; the coercion has already happened in candid and leaves no marker, so nothing downstream can tell "absent" from "did not fit" (R, P6: script result and logs identical to a genuine missing customer). Distinct from #42 (`opt opt`) and from L7-r1's L7-14 |
| B7 `.did` -> TypeEnv | holds (parse), feeds L7r3-1 | Parsing is correct and errors loudly on invalid text. Reversing round 1's dismissal: the stale type is produced by the app's own cache (V2) and override precedence (V5/D5), and the app chose typed decoding with no wire-type check; candid provides `subtype_with_config(OptReport::Error, ..)` (`types/subtype.rs:76-86`) that the app does not use. So the loss is app behaviour, not only spec behaviour |
| B5 JSON -> Candid (outbound, same stale type) | **finding** L7r3-1 (outbound symptom) | Arguments are encoded under the cached type (`src/bridge.rs:516-517`). If the target changed the type inside an `opt` field, the target's own decoder turns the script's value into `null` and the method executes (R, P7: `memo: 42` arrives as `memo = null`). The app cannot see this after the fact; only a fresh interface prevents it |
| V2 `DID_CACHE`, TTL 1 h | **finding** L7r3-1 (stale-type source) | `cache_get` (`src/bridge.rs:284-289`) checks only age; nothing ties the entry to the target's module (no module hash, no re-fetch on decode failure or on suspicion). A target upgraded inside the hour is called and decoded with its old interface for the rest of the hour (C). The `.did` comment and README:441-443 present the TTL as the freshness mechanism |
| LIM18 `DID_CACHE_TTL_NS` | **finding** L7r3-1 | Same as V2: the 1 h bound is the window of silent loss, not a correctness bound (C) |
| D5 `CANDID_OVERRIDES` / V5 `OVERRIDES` | **finding** L7r3-1 (amplifier; precedence itself already reported) | An override shadows the target's real interface indefinitely (`override_service`, `src/bridge.rs:216-227`, used first at :439-443; already reported, not repeated). New here: a wrong override whose returns are wrapped in `opt` converts every reply mismatch into `null` instead of an error (R, P4), and a stale override has the P1-P3 effect with no TTL at all (C). No validation of an override against the target's own interface exists (`src/lib.rs:324-333` only parses) |
| A6 Allowlisted target | **finding** L7r3-1 (trigger) | Trigger is an ordinary target upgrade that adds a variant tag or changes a field inside `opt`: routine Candid evolution (adding a variant case to an output type is common), no hostile target needed |
| CL22 "cached for one hour, then fetched again, so a target's interface change is picked up" | **finding** L7r3-1 (claim incomplete) | True as stated, but the README and tool descriptions never say that within the hour, or forever under an override, reply values under `opt` that no longer fit become `null` and new fields/return values are dropped. The code comment at `candid_bridge.rs:99` ("Skipping covers reply fields newer than our copy") shows the skip was intended; the opt-to-null effect is not mentioned anywhere |
| I8 Fidelity invariant | **violated** by L7r3-1 | Data is silently dropped or reinterpreted as `null` while reported as success, in all three runtimes (R, P6), and in the outbound direction (R, P7) |
| O1 inter-canister call | **finding** L7r3-1 (P7) | The effect is sent with a field the script set but the target received as `null`; the audit log records `Call`/`Ok` (C: `record_message` logs the send, closing entry from the script's `Ok`) |
| E5 tools/call (script) and audit `Ok` | **finding** L7r3-1 | The run returns `Ok` and the closing entry is `Ok`; no log line, warning or field marks the coercion (R natively for the result; audit status by code path `src/lib.rs:236-260`) |
| E4 search | not applicable to the loss | Search shows signatures only, no reply values. It does show the stale signature for up to 1 h (C), which is the same source, not a separate loss |

##### Candidate finding L7r3-1

- **Title:** A stale or overridden interface makes Candid's opt rule turn real reply data into
  `null` (and drop new fields and return values), and the run is audited `Ok` with no signal.
- **Severity proposed:** High (returns wrong data as if it were right: an existing customer is
  reported as absent, P2/P6). A verifier may argue Medium because the window is 1 h for the
  cache; the override path has no window.
- **Evidence:** reproduced natively (P1-P7 above). Live repetition not done (see below).
- **Root cause:** the app decodes with a cached type whose freshness is judged only by age and
  never checks the reply's wire types against it; candid's `opt` rule hides the mismatch.
- **Fix (proposed, not applied):** before or after typed decoding, check each reply type
  against `func.rets` with `subtype_with_config(OptReport::Error, ..)` (or decode untyped and
  compare); on a mismatch, evict the cache entry, re-fetch once and retry the decode, and if it
  still fails (or an override is in force) return an error naming the field. Key `DID_CACHE`
  to the target's module hash (`canister_info` is callable by any canister) so an upgraded
  target invalidates the entry before the next call, which also covers the outbound (P7)
  direction. Document the behaviour next to CL22.
- **Regression test:** P1, P2, P3r, P4 and P7 as unit tests on `Service` (encode under new,
  decode under old must be an error or a re-fetch, never `null`).

##### Not tested

- **Live repetition (upgrade demo_store within the cache hour):** not run. This task is
  Phases 3-4, and the run's rules allow deploys, upgrades and wasm builds only in the Live
  phase; the shared local network is also in use by other agents, so swapping demo_store's
  interface mid-run could corrupt their results. The mechanism is the same native code
  (`decode_reply`, `idl_to_json`); the 1 h window is from code (`cache_get`). A Live-phase
  repro: allowlist demo_store, call `get_customer` once (fills the cache), upgrade demo_store
  with `Tier` gaining `Platinum` and one customer set to it, call `get_customer` for that
  customer within the hour: expected `null`, status `Ok`; then restore demo_store.
- Behaviour of candid's `OptReport::Warning` path at runtime (no logger is wired in the app).
- Whether `canister_metadata` / `canister_info` are available on the local replica for the
  module-hash fix (not needed to establish the finding).

### grid-L8-r1

#### Coverage grid: L8 Concurrency and shared state, round 1

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`. Lens question: what if two of these interleave? Row ids from
`inventory.md`. Evidence: **R** = reproduced (native test in a private copy, or the local
network on port 8010), **C** = code path (unambiguous reading). Candidate findings are
numbered L8-1 to L8-5 (details in the lens report returned to the workflow).

Private copy: `/private/tmp/claude-501/audit-L8` (tests added there only, deleted at the end);
live requests: ordinary `execute_icp_script` calls with the test token, plus controller
`get_audit_logs` / `get_policy` / `canister status` queries. No settings were changed.

##### Volatile shared state

| Row | Cell | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| V1 `ACTIVE_RUNS` | holds | Incremented in `RunSlot::take` and decremented in `Drop`, both in single executions; a trap before the first await rolls back the increment with the heap, a trap after an await runs `Drop` in ic-cdk's cleanup (`cancel_all_tasks_attached_to_method`, ic-cdk-executor 2.0.0 `machinery.rs:168`). Only leak path: the cleanup callback itself trapping (e.g. F4 stable memory full during the `Trapped` append), which would also leave the id in `PENDING_RUNS`; not reproducible without exhausting stable memory (not tested). `tests::run_slots_are_capped_and_returned` passes. Searches take no slot (LIM12 note): a multiplication question, left to L4. |
| V2 `DID_CACHE` | **finding L8-3, L8-5** | Insert after the fetch await is unconditional, so a `remove_allowlist` that evicts during an in-flight fetch is undone (L8-3). Concurrent misses for the same canister in one `join_all` round each reserve a cap slot and send their own fetch (L8-5). Cross-run reuse of a fetched interface is intended; a successful entry always wins over a stale failure because `cache_get` is consulted before `failed_get` in `candid()` and `service()` (C). |
| V3 `PENDING_RUNS` | holds | Inserted in the execution that sends the first message (`record_message`), removed in `IcBridge::drop` on every exit path, including cleanup after a trap (C). Searches add their ids too, which matches the doc text "runs that have sent messages". Same cleanup-trap caveat as V1. |
| V4 `DID_FAILED` | holds (by design) | One run's failed fetch is served to every run for 5 min (LIM18). Ordering with a concurrent success is safe (see V2). No way found for a token holder to force a failure of a healthy target (queue-full needs >500 in-flight messages; 8 runs x 25 = 200): not tested further. |
| V5 `OVERRIDES` | holds | Re-validated against the stored text on every lookup (`override_service`), no await inside; inserts from the query path are discarded with the query (C). Override set mid-fetch takes precedence over the later cache insert (C). |
| V6 `LIVE_MEMORY`/`BASELINE_MEMORY` | **finding L8-2** | Register #43's fix holds for other runs' allocations (test `memory_limit_survives_interleaved_runs` passes), but `rebased` also excludes this run's own reply, which is allocated inside the window and freed after conversion: every reply's size comes off the run's count. Reproduced natively: 200 MiB of `icp.candid`/`icp.call` replies held with the 64 MiB limit, while 200 MiB built in the VM gives `MemoryError`. |
| V7 getrandom `STATE` | holds | Shared stream, but nothing a script can observe reads it: Monty's `random` uses `RandomStart::Seed` (not getrandom), Monty str hashing uses a fixed-key `DefaultHasher`, Boa has no `Math.random`, Rhai maps are B-trees. Live: Python class repr/`id`/`hash` and set iteration order identical across runs interleaved with other users' traffic (R). Monty `create_uuid` draws from it for instances crossing the boundary, never shown in results. |
| V8 Boa GC heap | **finding L8-1** | One thread-local heap for every JS run; each collection (automatic and the `force_collect` at the end of every run) marks all live objects of all suspended JS runs and sweeps garbage left by cancelled ones. Reproduced live: `return 1` cost 701,875,371 instructions (audit id 727) when it interleaved with another run holding 600k objects, vs 19.0M normally. The GC threshold is also process-global and only ever raised. |
| V9 ic-cdk executor | holds | Each run's future is its own task; cleanup cancels only the trapped method's tasks (C). |
| V10 engine statics | not tested | Boa interner/shapes, Rhai and Monty internal statics not inspected beyond V7/V8. |
| V11 demo_store `STORE` | not applicable | Shared by design (demo), every update is one execution with no await. |

##### Commit points

| Row | Cell | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| K1 first-pending hook | holds | Hook runs in the execution that hands over the message; `record_message` borrows are temporaries, no shared state read before and used after (C). |
| K2 JS `join_all` round | **finding L8-3, L8-5** | Per-call `reserve` (allowlist, method, cap, budget) runs before `service().await`; when the interface is not cached the message is sent in a later execution without a re-check (L8-3). Duplicate fetches per round (L8-5). No `State`/`GcRefCell` borrow is held across the await (C). |
| K3 Python awaits | **finding L8-2, L8-3** | `rebased` window (L8-2); same bridge TOCTOU (L8-3). |
| K4 Rhai replay await | finding L8-3 (shared bridge path) | Mutex not held across the await (C); `answers` per run. |
| K5 `run_search` awaits | **finding L8-3** | `list_allowed()` captured before the loop: methods rendered are the pre-change list; a mid-search removal makes `check_interface_fetch` refuse, and the `halted` heuristic then skips every remaining canister. |
| K6 closing entry | finding L8-4 | Final budget check reads `policy::limits()` again while the engines enforced the deadline captured at bridge creation. |
| K7 cleanup | holds (untested) | Writes `Trapped`, removes `PENDING_RUNS`, returns the slot; heap borrow flags are rolled back to the last commit, where no borrows are held across awaits (C). |
| K8, K9, K10, K12 | not applicable | Single executions, nothing suspended. |
| K11 upgrade in flight | not applicable to L8 | Heap reset is documented; stopping with unbounded waits is L9 (#44). |

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`. Focus: one JS run (no memory cap, register #24) commits a large

path. Candidate findings L8-6 (and the trap attribution) are detailed in the lens report.

No private build was needed (no code compiled). Live work used the shared test token and
demo_store only; one reset upgrade used the already-deployed module copied from the local
replica state (no rebuild). Limits were never changed (an identical `set_limits` was sent

network at the same time: 8 run slots were held by their `hang` runs 11:11-11:17Z, and they
upgraded the canister at about 11:19Z (module `224cfa7a…`) and again before 11:21:55Z.
**Outage caused by this lens:** 11:08:36Z-11:09:25Z every update call on `icp_code_mode` was
refused (any 503 another lens saw in that window comes from this test).

|---|---|---|
| I6 Isolation | **finding L8-6** | One run's heap decides whether every other caller's update can run at all (R above). VM-state isolation still holds (round 1). |

<a id="grid-L8-r3"></a>

### grid-L8-r3

#### Coverage grid: L8 Concurrency and shared state, round 3 (DID_FAILED poisoning)

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`. Question: can a token holder make `DID_FAILED` hold a failure for a
healthy target, so every caller is refused for 5 minutes? Row ids from `inventory.md`.
Evidence: **C** = code path (unambiguous reading). Nothing was reproduced in this round. No
private build was made, and no request was sent to the local network. Flooding the shared
instance with more than 500 concurrent searches, or pinning calls until its liquid cycles run
out, is a destructive load test. Under the run rules that belongs to the Live phase, not to this
lens. Candidate finding: **L8-7**.

##### How the code behaves (C)

- `IcBridge::candid` (`src/bridge.rs:471-507`) caches **every** `Err` from `fetch_did`, size
  check or parse in `DID_FAILED` under the target's canonical id. The entry lasts 5 minutes,
  is shared by all callers, and is not tied to the run or caller that caused it. Only policy
  refusals from `reserve` are kept out of the cache, because they return earlier through `?`.
- `fetch_did` (`src/bridge.rs:423-437`) falls back to `__get_candid_interface_tmp_hack` on any
  error from `canister_metadata`, including a send refusal. It returns the fallback's error.
- In ic-cdk 0.20.3 (`call.rs:612-660`), two kinds of error are clean and not the callee's
  fault. One is a synchronous refusal: `CallPerformFailed` (output queue full, or the
  canister cannot pay for the send or the response reservation) or
  `InsufficientLiquidCycleBalance`. The other is a `SysTransient` or `SysUnknown` reject, such
  as a bounded-wait timeout or a dropped best-effort response. ic-cdk marks the
  `SysTransient`/`SysUnknown` rejects as immediately retryable. `candid()` treats them all like
  a permanent "this target has no interface" and caches them.
- The two causes behave differently on the fallback:
  - A cycles shortfall refuses both sends: metadata to `aaaaa-aa`, then the fallback to the
    target.
  - A full queue to `aaaaa-aa` refuses only the first. The fallback then goes to the target's
    own queue. demo_store exports `__get_candid_interface_tmp_hack` (`demo_store/src/lib.rs:342`),
    so it would still succeed there.
  - On a healthy target without `tmp_hack` (many Rust canisters), the fallback's "method not
    found" is cached. In that case, failing only the metadata step is enough.
- The cache is not single-flight. Concurrent misses from separate ingress messages each send
  their own fetch, and the last one to finish decides what is stored. A fresh `DID_CACHE`
  entry still wins over a later failure, because `cache_get` is read before `failed_get`.
- Recovery: a controller's `set_candid_override` is read before both caches, so it bypasses
  the lockout. Callers have no way to clear the entry.

##### Cells

| Row | Cell | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| V4 `DID_FAILED` | **finding L8-7** (cache semantics, C); poisoning by a token holder **unverified** | Transient and self-caused send failures are cached as if they were a property of the target, for every caller (see above). Whether a token holder can cause one on demand was not tested (see "Not tested"). This revises the round-1 V4 cell, whose bound of 8x25 did not count searches. |
| V2 `DID_CACHE` | holds for this lens; expiry symptom already reported | A fresh entry wins over a concurrent failure (C). After the 1 h TTL, a failed refresh makes the held copy unusable and the target is refused for 5 minutes. That is the reported finding at `src/bridge.rs:284-289, 439-449, 471-507`. L8-7 widens the set of failures that trigger it to transient ones. |
| E5b `run_search` | **finding L8-7** (carrier) | Searches take no run slot (LIM12) and fetch through the same `candid()`. Within one HTTP request, searches run one after another (`src/mcp.rs:400-402` awaits each `exec`), so one request has at most 1 fetch in flight. More than 500 sends in flight therefore need more than 500 concurrent ingress messages. That is plausible because searches are not slot-capped and fetches are not single-flight, but it was not measured. |
| O2 interface fetch | **finding L8-7** | 2-step fallback that keeps only the last error. With a cycles shortfall both steps fail synchronously, in the same execution, and the failure is cached (C). |
| LIM9 `MAX_SEARCHES` | holds | It bounds the searches per request, and they run sequentially. It does not bound concurrency across requests. That gap is LIM12's and is already reported (search not slot-capped). |
| LIM12 `MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS` | not new | The search exclusion is already reported. Here it is only what makes the ingress-flood vector plausible. |
| LIM18 TTLs | **finding L8-7** (symptom) | The 5-minute TTL is applied to transient errors that are retryable right away. Any caller who arrives in that window is refused, even if the very next fetch would have succeeded. |
| A6 allowlisted target | holds (not caller-controlled) | The pinning vector needs an allowlisted target that never replies to an unbounded call. demo_store answers every method at once and exports `tmp_hack`. A token holder cannot add targets. In production, a slow or stopping target is in the hands of a third party, not the token holder. |

##### Not tested

- **The ingress flood.** More than 500 concurrent searches against an uncached target would
  need a load test on the shared instance, which belongs to the Live phase. Whether the queue
  to `aaaaa-aa` actually fills was also not checked: management messages may be inducted
  every round, so it might never reach 500.
- **Cycle exhaustion by pinned unbounded calls.** The per-call reservation (the task's figure
  of 42.8B) was not measured. No silent allowlisted target exists on the demo deployment.
- **The production bridge off-chain.** It cannot run there (register #58), so no native test
  drives `candid()` with an injected `CallPerformFailed` or `SysTransient`. Harness needed: a
  trait seam over `Call` in `IcBridge`, so that fault injection can return each `CallFailed`
  variant, and then a check of what lands in `DID_FAILED`.

### grid-L8-r5

#### Coverage grid: L8 Concurrency and shared state, round 5 (DID_FAILED poisoning, live)

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`. Question: can an ordinary token holder make a healthy target's
interface fetch fail, so that `DID_FAILED` refuses that target to every caller for 5 minutes?
Round 3 (L8-7) described the cache semantics from the code only. This round ran it live.
Row ids are from `inventory.md`. Evidence: **R** = reproduced on the local network (port 8010),
**C** = the code path produces it unambiguously.

##### Setup

- The canister found running was **not** the audited code. Module `0x89b4c117…` had been
  installed at 16:07Z by someone else, and its interface has fields that are not in the tree
  (`Limits.tool_calls_per_minute`, `PolicyView.candid_overrides`). I built HEAD `295d64b` in a
  private copy (`/private/tmp/claude-501/audit-L8r5`, shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, `ic-wasm`
  metadata + shrink as in `icp.yaml`). That gave module `0x224cfa7a…ec769`, the same hash
  L18-r3 saw deployed. I installed it with `icp canister install --mode upgrade --args '(null)' --yes`.
  `--yes` was needed because of the Candid-breaking `get_policy` change. demo_store
  (`0xae53d21b…`) was left as deployed. It has public `candid:service` metadata and
  exports `tmp_hack`.
- Client: MCP JSON-RPC over the gateway (`Host: icp_code_mode.local.localhost:8010`). The
  token came from the `MCP_TOKEN` line of `.env` and was never printed. Scripts are in
  `scratchpad/l8r5/`.
- Eviction: `remove_allowlist` + `set_allowlist` on demo_store with its original 8 methods.
  This clears `DID_CACHE`, `DID_FAILED` and `OVERRIDES` for it.
- Liquid shortfall: the L18-r3 margin method. `freezing_threshold` was set to
  `(balance - margin) / idle_burn_per_second`, and a shell `trap` restored `2_592_000`
  within seconds. The idle-burn figure moved during the round, because another agent grew
  memory to 1.5 GB. So the margins below are targets, not measured liquid. The available
  figures in the rejection texts are measured.
- Final state, checked: threshold `2_592_000`; limits 25 / 20_000_000_000 / null / null (never
  changed); demo_store allowlist entry restored with the same 8 methods; demo_store Running;
  `pending_run_ids = vec {}`; `active_runs = 0`; demo_store interface fetchable (a search
  returned OK at 16:38:52Z). Another agent added `73qqu-…` to the allowlist during the round.
  I did not touch it. The network was left running, and `icp_code_mode` now runs `0x224cfa7a…`.

##### Experiments

| # | Input | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | Evict, then 200 concurrent `search_icp_canisters {canister_id: demo_store}` | All 200 returned the interface. 25 fetch runs (audit `Started`/`Ok` pairs), started in 2 blocks (13 + 12). At most 25 fetches were open at once. No error, no `CallPerformFailed`, no `SysTransient`. 8.5 s total (R) |
| A2 | Evict, then 600 concurrent searches | Same: 600 OK, 25 fetches, 2 blocks, at most 25 open, no error (R). The first `canister_metadata` reply lands one block later and fills `DID_CACHE`, and every later search is served from it. On this replica, ingress induction (about 13 per block) caps fetches in flight far below the 500-message queue |
| B1 | Evict, `icp canister stop demo_store`, search, script call, `start` | The search fetched the interface **successfully** while the target was stopped: `canister_metadata` is answered by the management canister and never reaches the target. The script call was refused with `5 - Canister … is stopped`. That is a call error, not a fetch error, so it was not cached. After `start`, calls worked at once (R). Stopping a target that has public metadata does not poison the cache |
| C1 | Evict; margin 80B; one search; restore at once; then a search and a script every ~30 s | Search during the shortfall: `could not fetch candid for 4fbx2-… (insufficient liquid cycles balance, available: 39988878635, required: 42102449000); a controller can register it with set_candid_override`. After the restore (balance 13.56T), every search **and** every script (`icp.call(demo,'get_product',1)` -> `Error: could not fetch candid … insufficient liquid cycles …`) was refused with the same stale text, from 16:25:10Z through 16:29:59Z. First success at 16:31:39Z. The failing search wrote **no audit entry**: both sends were refused, so `calls = 0` and there were no violations (R). Margin 60B: the update could not start (HTTP 503), and nothing was cached (R) |
| C2 | Evict; margin ~900B target; **one ordinary token-holder script**: `Promise.allSettled([24 x icp.call(ledger,'icrc1_symbol',[]), icp.candid(demo)])`; restore; victim search every 45 s | The script returned HTTP 200 in 19.4 s. 6 ledger calls were sent, then 18 were refused with `insufficient liquid cycles balance, available: 30…`, and the `icp.candid(demo)` fetch was refused the same way and cached. Victim searches after the restore (balance 13.42T) were refused with `could not fetch candid for 4fbx2-… (insufficient liquid cycles balance, available: 30246110773, required: 42102449000)` from 16:33:35Z to 16:38:07Z. OK at 16:38:52Z. The attacker's audit entries are 10507 `Started` … 10513 `Ok`, `calls = 6`: nothing in the log shows that 18 sends and the fetch were refused or that a failure was cached (R) |
| C3 | Margin ~6T target; 8 scripts x 25 ledger calls, plus 6 searches 50 ms later | Every call and every search OK. The scripts finished over 0.8-5.8 s, so their calls did not overlap enough. Inconclusive (R) |
| C4 | Evict; margin ~3T target; 8 concurrent scripts, each `24 x ledger call + icp.candid(demo)` | Liquid ran out across scripts. One script got **0** calls through, others got 1 and 16. Three fetches returned the cached `available: 8024119516` failure. The other 5 scripts' fetches succeeded. A fetch already in flight that finished later cleared `DID_FAILED` and filled `DID_CACHE` (`src/bridge.rs:497-500`), so the victim search after the restore was OK. Aggregation across concurrent runs is real, but a lasting poisoning needs no successful fetch to finish after the failure (R) |

| Row | Cell | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| V4 `DID_FAILED` | **finding L8-r5-1** (R) | A fetch refused because **this canister** is short of liquid cycles is stored as the target's failure. It is served to every caller, in searches and scripts, for 5 minutes after the balance has recovered (C1, C2). The text it serves is stale and misleading: "insufficient liquid cycles balance, available: 30246110773" while the balance was 13.4T. This revises round 1 (holds) and confirms round 3's L8-7, with a trigger an ordinary token holder controls (C2). The opposite race (a late success clears the failure) was also observed (C4) |
| O2 interface fetch | **finding L8-r5-1** (R) | With a liquid shortfall, both steps (`canister_metadata` to `aaaaa-aa`, then `tmp_hack` to the target) are refused synchronously in one execution, and the second error is cached (`src/bridge.rs:424-437, 502-505`). A refused fetch writes no `Started` entry (correct: nothing was sent). A stopped target does not fail the fetch when it has public metadata (B1). Without metadata, the fallback's `is stopped` reject would be cached: C only, not reproduced, because no target without metadata is deployed |
| E5b `run_search` | **finding L8-r5-1** (R, carrier); ingress-flood vector **refuted on this replica** (R) | 800 concurrent fetching searches never had more than 25 fetches open, and none failed (A1, A2). The first reply fills the cache within one block, so the >500-in-flight vector from round 3 does not reach the queue here. Searches are still a carrier: a search fetch during a shortfall poisons the target and leaves no audit entry (C1). That logging guard is already reported (`src/lib.rs:136-161`, not repeated) |
| LIM9 `MAX_SEARCHES` | holds (R) | 5 per request, run one after another. It plays no part in the poisoning: the flood was across requests, and it was self-limited by the cache fill (A1, A2) |
| LIM12 `MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS` | holds for this lens (R) | The 8-script cap bounds how much liquid one token holder can pin at once: 8 x 25 x 42.1B, about 8.4T. That is the upper bound of the balance band in which the poisoning can be caused (C4 showed liquid run out across concurrent scripts at a ~3T target margin). It did not prevent the single-script case (C2). Searches not counted: already reported |
| LIM18 TTLs | **finding L8-r5-1** (R, symptom) | `DID_FAIL_TTL_NS` (5 min) is applied to a self-caused, immediately retryable condition. Measured lockouts: 16:25:10-16:29:59Z (C1) and 16:33:35-16:38:07Z (C2). Each ended between 5 and 6.5 minutes after the cause. The failure entry outranks nothing (`cache_get` is read first), so only an empty or expired `DID_CACHE` can be poisoned. That window is reopened every hour per target and at every upgrade. "Stale cache expires into a refusal" is already reported (`src/bridge.rs:284-289`) |
| A3 Bearer-token holder | **finding L8-r5-1** (R) | One script with a valid token and two allowlisted targets (24 calls to one, then `icp.candid` of the other) made the other target unavailable to every caller for 5 minutes (C2). This is deterministic within one execution: the calls reserve liquid before the fetch is polled in the same `join_all` round. Precondition: liquid above the freezing threshold no more than about 24 x 42.1B = 1.0T (one script), and up to about 8.4T with concurrent scripts landing in the same round (C4). Plus a target whose cache entry is absent or expired. The attacker can repeat right after expiry, because an unexpired failure costs nothing to hit |
| A6 Allowlisted target | holds: the target cannot be poisoned by its own downtime when it has public metadata (R, B1); **finding L8-r5-1** as victim | A healthy target (demo_store answered every call before, during and after the tests) was locked out by a condition of the calling canister. A target without public `candid:service` that is stopped or slow during a fetch would cache its reject or a `SysUnknown` timeout after 300 s (bounded wait): C, not reproduced |

##### Not tested

- **Queue-full and `SysTransient` triggers on mainnet.** Ingress induction per block and
  cross-subnet reply latency differ there. With mainnet block rates, the in-flight fetch
  count could be higher than the 25 seen here. Needs a staging subnet.
- **A target without public metadata, stopped or never answering during a fetch** (fallback
  reject or 300 s best-effort timeout cached). No such target is deployed; building one is
  outside this round.
- **Lasting multi-script poisoning above 1T liquid.** C4 showed liquid exhausted across 8
  scripts, but a concurrent successful fetch cleared the entry. Making the poisoning stick
  needs the fetch to be the last one to finish, which was not attempted.
- **Native fault injection** into `IcBridge::candid` (`CallPerformFailed`,
  `InsufficientLiquidCycleBalance`, `SysTransient`) still needs the `Call` seam described in
  round 3 (register #58).

### grid-L9-r1

#### Grid: L9 Failure handling, round 1

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`. Reviewer: L9 lens agent. Question: what happens when a dependency
(target canister, management canister, the platform, stable memory) is slow, wrong, hostile or
absent? Method: read `src/bridge.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/mcp.rs`, `src/search.rs`,
`src/candid_bridge.rs`, `src/policy.rs`, `src/runtimes/*.rs`, `shims/web-time`, and the
dependency code they lean on (ic-cdk 0.20.3 `call.rs`, ic-cdk-macros 0.20.3, candid 0.10.40
`de.rs`, monty-types 1.6.0 `resource/`). Probes ran natively in a private copy as
`tests/l9_failure.rs` (debug, and release `--no-default-features` for the stack probe; shared
target dir, `RUST_MIN_STACK=8388608` to mirror the 8 MiB wasm stack). The live network was used
read-only (controller queries `get_audit_logs`/`get_audit_log_len`): no setting changed, nothing
deployed. Candidate findings are L9-1 ... L9-9 in the lens output.

Evidence: **R** = reproduced natively, **C** = code path unambiguous, **L** = observed on the
local network (read-only).

##### Findings in this grid

| Id | Sev | Title |
|---|---|---|
| L9-1 | High | `__get_candid_interface_tmp_hack` reply decoded with no quota: a 27-byte hostile reply forces unbounded work; the trap rolls back the failure cache, so it repeats on every request |
| L9-2 | High | A nested interface well inside the 512 KiB limit overflows the 8 MiB stack while parsing; same no-memory-of-traps repetition |
| L9-3 | High | Default `unbounded_wait`: a target that never replies holds a run slot forever; 8 such runs refuse every script until an upgrade, and revoking the token does not help |
| L9-4 | Medium | The reply decoding quota is effectively 400,000, not 20,000,000 (candid's 50x untyped penalty): valid replies over ~400 KB, ~36k nat64, ~9k small records fail with a misleading error; register #17 regressed above ~400 KB |
| L9-5 | Low | A transient failure while re-fetching an expired interface discards the still-held interface and blocks every caller for 5 minutes, with an error that blames a missing interface |
| L9-6 | Low | Interface parse errors echo up to 512 KiB of target-controlled text into search results and script errors |
| L9-7 | Low | One allowlisted target without a retrievable interface makes every unscoped search a paid update call |
| L9-8 | Low | `call_timeout_seconds` is not validated (0 accepted: calls time out at once, outcome unknown) and is not applied to interface fetches (always 300 s, twice) |
| L9-9 | Low | When stable memory cannot grow, audit appends trap; a trap in the cleanup callback also loses the `Trapped` entry and leaks the run slot |

### grid-L9-r2

#### Grid: L9 Failure handling, round 2 (Live)

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`. Reviewer: L9 lens agent, round 2. Task: observe on-chain the L9 findings
that round 1 proved only natively or from the code path (L9-1, L9-2, L9-3/L4-5, L4-2, L6-7/L9-7,
register #29, #46, the 300 s cap, cycles held by in-flight calls), using a misbehaving target
(register #55).

##### Setup

- Network: the project's local icp-cli network (port 8010), shared with other audit agents that
  were running at the same time (audit log grew from 898 to over 5,500 entries during this run;
  another agent stopped and upgraded `icp_code_mode` at least twice, changing its module hash from
  the baseline `ad3ee221...` to `224cfa7a...`, set `call_timeout_seconds = 30` for a while, and
  allowlisted its own target `4xhad-gd777-77775-aaacq-cai`). Every observation below is tied to my
  own runs by script hash, run id, method label and timestamp.
- Hostile target (not in the repo; built in a private scratch directory with the shared target
  dir, `ic-cdk 0.20.3`, `candid 0.10.40`): detached canister `4qggx-l3777-77775-aaaca-cai`, no
  `candid:service` metadata, methods:
  - `__get_candid_interface_tmp_hack` (manual-reply query) in three modes: 0 = `DIDL 01 6d7f 02 71 00
    "service : {}" leb(n)` (a `vec null` of length n with no element bytes), 1 = a valid interface,
    2 = `type T = vec vec ... nat` nested to a chosen depth;
  - `hang`: never replies until `release` (keeps its call context open by awaiting `raw_rand`
    in a loop);
  - `pending_only`: `std::future::pending().await` (as the task proposed);
  - `big_reject(n)`: rejects with an n-byte message.
  A second detached canister `46el7-ql777-77775-aaada-cai` carried a 200,047-byte nested
  `candid:service` (depth 50,000) in public metadata. Both were deleted afterwards (cycles recovered).
- Settings changed and restored: allowlist entries for the two targets and `aaaaa-aa` (all removed;
  final allowlist = ledger + demo_store, as found); `set_limits` `max_calls_per_script = 1` for one
  run, `call_timeout_seconds = 600` for one run (restored to the values found; the final state read
  back is `call_timeout_seconds = null, max_calls_per_script = 25, max_instructions = 20e9,
  certified_reads = null`). No override was set. `icp_code_mode` was not deployed or upgraded by me.

Evidence: **L** = observed on the local network in this round (request, response and audit
entries), **C** = code path.

### grid-L9-r5

#### Grid: L9 Failure handling, round 5 (a run that outlives the transport)

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`. Question: when a script runs longer than the HTTP gateway or the MCP
client is willing to wait, what does the client get, does the run still commit, who learns the
outcome, and what does a retry do? Not tried before (L5-r2 "Not tested"; L5r2-1 covers only the
round/suspension-limit trigger).

##### Method

- **Network:** the project's local icp-cli network (port 8010, pocket-ic network launcher
  v16.0.0, gateway built from `ic-gateway` with `ic-agent 0.49.1`). No second network.
- **Why a separate instance:** at the start of this round the shared `icp_code_mode`
  (`4caro-…`) ran module `89b4c117…`, built from the `audit-fixes` branch (it has
  `tool_calls_per_minute` and makes every call `bounded_wait` with a 300 s default), so it was
  not the audited code. Instead of replacing someone else's deployment, the audited module was
  installed in a **detached canister on the same network**: `5iptu-f3777-77775-aaaga-cai`.
- **Build:** `git archive HEAD` into a private temp copy, sources touched,
  `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` = the shared directory, then icp.yaml's own `ic-wasm` steps. Result
  sha256 `224cfa7a…c769`, byte-identical to the HEAD artifact of L13-r2/L13-r4.
- **Install:** `InitArgs { token_sha256 = [hash of a fresh test token kept in the scratchpad,
  never printed], allowlist = [(fixture, ["hang"]), (demo_store 4fbx2-…, ["create_order",
  "list_orders"])], limits = null }` (defaults: 25 calls, 20e9, **unbounded wait**), plus
  `set_candid_override` for the fixture.
- **Fixture** (temp dir only): detached `5pova-id777-77775-aaagq-cai`. `hang(n)` logs
  `hang-enter`, keeps its call context open with one self-call per round until
  `release(true)`, then logs `hang-done` and replies `n`; `events()` returns the log.
- **Script** (one JSON-RPC body, file sha256 `bad9403c…78e9`, JSON-RPC `id` 7, sent
  byte-identical every time):
  `const h = await icp.call(FIX,"hang",1); const o = await icp.call(DS,"create_order",["ix6jd-voa77-xagai-camca-kbq",[{product_id:4,quantity:1}]]); return {h,o};`
- **Client:** Python `urllib` POST to `127.0.0.1:8010/mcp` with `Host: 5iptu-….localhost:8010`
  and the bearer header. "SDK-like" means a 60 s client timeout followed by
  `notifications/cancelled {requestId: 7}`, which is what the TypeScript SDK does.
- **Cleanup:** both detached canisters stopped and deleted (the fixture with
  `--no-recover-cycles`: its self-call loop had burned its cycles below the recovery cost).
  The shared `icp_code_mode`'s allowlist, limits and overrides were never touched. Orders 61-63
  stay in `demo_store` (test data, status `Pending`; 3 units of product 4 reserved). Note: while
  this round ran, someone else redeployed the shared `icp_code_mode` to `224cfa7a…`. That was
  not this lens.

##### Measurements

##### Candidates

###### L9r5-1: a run that outlives the client's timeout commits its effects, and nobody learns the outcome; a retry repeats them

- **Severity:** High (a caller with ordinary access gets a failure for a run that changed state
  on a target, and the standard client reaction, a retry, duplicates every effect; with a
  value-moving method allowlisted (VF4) that is the canister's funds sent twice).
- **Invariant:** I3 (the record and what the client is told disagree), I10 (nothing documents
  it), I4 (a retry multiplies every effect: L4 pattern "a per-item budget that a retry
  multiplies").
- **Where:** `src/mcp.rs:374-412` (`http_update`: a reply is the only outcome channel),
  `src/lib.rs:218-263` (`run_script`: no request id or idempotency key, nothing kept after
  the reply), `src/bridge.rs:524-527` (unbounded wait by default), `src/mcp.rs:77-133` (tool
  description and missing annotations), README "How to read the audit log" and "Options".
- **Evidence:** reproduced (B, R, End above). A client with the MCP SDK's 60 s timeout got
  `timed out`. Its run (4) waited, created order 63, and closed `Ok`. A byte-identical retry
  created order 62. A third send (A) created 61. That is 3 orders and 3 `Ok` runs for one
  intended action, and the client that timed out had no way to learn that its order existed.
  The local gateway itself held a connection for 716 s and delivered the result (A), so locally
  only the client's own timeout triggers this. The mainnet boundary-node timeout was not
  measured.
- **Who learns the outcome:** the target (it executed) and a controller reading the audit log
  (`Ok`, without the result, the arguments or the JSON-RPC id). The token holder, who cannot
  read the audit, and the AI client learn nothing: no result endpoint (`GET /mcp` 405, no SSE,
  no session), no receipt id, and the late reply is dropped with the gateway request.
- **Refuted first:** (a) "the gateway would time out and tell the client": locally it never did
  (716 s). (b) "the cancel stops it": C1/C2 had no effect. (c) "a retry is deduplicated":
  identical body and id, executed again. (d) "the docs warn": they do not (step 5).
- **Distinct from:** L5r2-1 (the server itself reports failure after an effect because of
  round/suspension limits) and #44 (stop/upgrade blocked). Same symptom (failure reported,
  effect committed, retry repeats it), different trigger: the transport.
- **Pattern:** an operation whose effects outlive the request that started it, with the
  response as the only channel for the outcome and no idempotency key.
- **Fix:** give every run a stable id returned at once and store each run's result. Two ways:
  (1) a `get_run_result(run_id)` tool or JSON-RPC method that answers from the audit log plus
  a bounded result store, or (2) the MCP Tasks utility / SSE with resumability. Accept an
  optional client idempotency key (or the JSON-RPC id plus the token hash) and answer a repeat
  within a window with the stored outcome instead of running again. Document in the tool
  description that effects may have happened when a call times out, and that ledger calls
  should carry `created_at_time`. Add `annotations: { idempotentHint: false, destructiveHint:
  true }` explicitly. Regression test: PocketIC, a client times out on a held target, the
  target is released, a retry with the same key returns the first result and does not send a
  second message.

###### L9r5-2: `notifications/cancelled` is silently ignored, and nothing says so

- **Severity:** Low (the spec allows ignoring a cancellation, and the outcome is covered by
  L9r5-1. The fault is the missing documentation and the misleading client experience).
- **Invariant:** I10.
- **Where:** `src/mcp.rs:248-250` (`classify`: every notification -> `Done(None)`, in both
  query and update paths). The cancel arrives as a separate HTTP request, answered by the
  query path, so even a cooperative check inside the run could never see it.
- **Evidence:** reproduced (C1, C2): 202 with an empty body, the runs continued, sent
  `create_order` and closed `Ok`.
- **Fix:** document in the tool description and README that a sent script cannot be cancelled.
  If cancellation is wanted, record cancel requests by (token hash, request id) in an update
  and check them before each send (`reserve`).

##### Not tested

- **Mainnet / boundary-node gateway timeout:** only the local pocket-ic gateway was measured
  (no timeout in 716 s). Whether `ic-gateway` on boundary nodes cuts a long
  `http_request_update` (and with what status) needs the real network (register #57).
- **Python MCP SDK default timeout:** the package is not installed locally, and installing it
  means downloading. TypeScript checked in source (60 s).
- **Ledger re-run:** the value consequence (VF4) was not re-run here; it rests on L5-r2 M6/M8-M10
  and the identical code path.
- **K3/K4 live:** Python and Rhai suspensions under a held target were not run in this round.
- **Gateway-initiated retries:** no automatic re-submission by the local gateway was seen
  (3 sends -> 3 runs, all mine). Boundary-node behaviour is unknown.

### grid-L10-r1

#### Coverage grid: L10 Trust and transport, round 1

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`. Lens question: who can read or alter this in transit or at rest?
Evidence: **R** = reproduced (command or test given), **C** = code path. Candidate findings are
numbered L10-1 to L10-4 (details in the lens report returned to the workflow).

##### Live observations used below (read-only, local network on port 8010)

- `curl -D -` on `GET /`, `POST /mcp` (no token, 401) and `GET /anything/else` (404): all three
  carry the same `IC-Certificate` `tree=` and `expr_path=` (`http_expr/<*>`, expression
  `no_certification`). Decoding the subnet-signed certificate gives
  `certified_data = [85, 236, 195, 28, ...]`, which is `SKIP_CERT_DATA` (`src/lib.rs:55`) and
  equals `ic_http_certification::utils::skip_certification_certified_data()` (the crate's own
  test, `ic-http-certification-3.2.0/src/utils/skip_certification.rs:96-105`).
- The local gateway serves the demo page on the certified (non-raw) domain with status 200, so it
  accepts skip-certified responses.
- `certified_reads` was not toggled (not the Live phase); its effect is read from the code.
