<a id="grid-sweep-r1-5"></a>

### grid-sweep-r1-5

#### Variant sweep r1-5 (Phase 6)

Pattern swept: **"Queued work is discarded at end of run while success is reported. Sibling
runtimes differ in eager versus lazy dispatch."** (source: L2-2, un-awaited `icp.call` /
`icp.call_async`, not re-reported). Searched for in general form: *a driver loop or
dispatcher reaches its end (completion, a count limit, a protocol path) and drops work or a
result that was already queued, sent or produced, while the status it reports does not
match what happened; equivalent paths handle the same end differently.*

Evidence: native tests added to a private copy (`/private/tmp/claude-501/sweep-r1-5.*`,
deleted afterwards), `cargo test --lib`, shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. R = reproduced,
C = code path.

##### New candidates

| Id | Sev | Title | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| SW5-1 | Medium | JS and Python drop a finished run at their round/suspension limit after its last messages were sent, and report an error; Rhai at the same limit succeeds | R (native) |
| SW5-2 | Low | A `tools/call` sent without an `id` is silently not executed, answered `202 Accepted`, with no audit entry, on both the query and update path | R (native) |

###### SW5-1

`src/runtimes/js.rs:374-409`: the loop sends round *i*'s batch, resolves the promises, then
increments; after the 64th round's replies are delivered the loop exits and returns
`Err("script exceeded 64 host round-trips")` without running the jobs or checking the
script's promise. `src/runtimes/python.rs:239-277`: same shape, `progress = next?` is
assigned on the 256th iteration and the loop ends with `Err("script exceeded 256 host
suspensions")` even when `progress` is `RunProgress::Complete`. Rhai
(`src/runtimes/rhai_rt.rs:211`) checks `answers.len() >= MAX_REQUESTS` *before* sending the
65th request, so 64 requests complete.

Native results (MockBridge, script = N sequential calls then return `"done"`):

| Runtime | N | Result | Calls sent |
|---|---|---|---|
| JS | 63 | Ok("done") | 63 |
| JS | 64 | Err("script exceeded 64 host round-trips...") | 64 |
| Python | 255 | Ok("done") | 255 |
| Python | 256 | Err("script exceeded 256 host suspensions") | 256 |
| Rhai | 64 | Ok("done") | 64 |
| Rhai | 65 | Err("script exceeded 64 icp requests") | 64 (65th not sent) |

Reachable under default limits (call cap 25): rounds/suspensions that send nothing still
count. JS: `for (63) await icp.candid(S)` (cached interface: `IcBridge::candid` returns before
`reserve`, `bridge.rs:475-480`) then `await icp.call(S, "create_order", ...)` -> the
`create_order` is sent and executed, run returns `isError:true`, closing audit entry
`Error`. Python: 255 x `icp.principal()` (each a host suspension, no message) then one
`icp.call` -> same. Both reproduced natively with one recorded call and `Err`. The client
(an AI agent) is told the script failed after its effect happened, so a retry repeats it.
README:368/371 document "64 rounds" and "256 suspensions"; the effective limits are 63 and
255 completing ones. Fix: check the promise / `progress` once more after the loop (or count
before dispatch, as Rhai does).

###### SW5-2

`src/mcp.rs:252-254`: `classify` returns `Msg::Done(None)` for any message without `id`,
before looking at `method`, so `tools/call` (`execute_icp_script` or `search_icp_canisters`)
as a notification never reaches `exec`; `finish` answers `202` with an empty body
(`mcp.rs:308`). Native: single message and a two-message batch, `http_update` -> 202, `exec`
ran 0 times; `http_query` -> 202, no upgrade. No audit entry. MCP defines `tools/call` only as
a request, and JSON-RPC 2.0 lets the server skip the reply but not the processing; the
Streamable HTTP rule is "202 if the server accepts the input, else an HTTP error such as
400". The L12 grid recorded this case as holds (spec-permitted); listed here because it is
the swept pattern (submitted work dropped, success status). Verifier to decide.

<a id="grid-sweep-r1-6"></a>

### grid-sweep-r1-6

#### Variant sweep r1-6

Pattern: "A record names the transport instead of the subject of the effect, and a
documented label format that the code never produces."

Source finding (known, not re-reported): interface-fetch audit entries are labelled
`aaaaa-aa.canister_metadata` with `canisters = ["aaaaa-aa"]`, so the canister whose interface
was read is not recorded, while the `.did` / `policy.rs:94` doc promises
`canister.<candid interface>`.

Method: code reading at `295d64b`. Nothing was built, deployed or called. Every place that
writes a record or a label (audit entries, violation and error strings kept in the audit,
`PolicyView`, log-line prefixes, search output, demo_store orders) was checked for two
things: (a) does the record name the party that carried the message rather than the thing
the effect was about, and (b) does a doc describe a label/value format the code never emits.

Result: two new candidates (SW6-1, SW6-2). Everything else is either a known finding or holds.

##### Candidates

| Id | Sev | Title | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| SW6-1 | Medium | Script calls to the management canister are allowlisted, audited and reported by the recipient `aaaaa-aa` only; the canister actually acted on (the `canister_id` argument) is neither checked by policy nor recorded anywhere in the log | code path |
| SW6-2 | Low | Search audit entries put undocumented values in `language` (`"search"`) and `script_sha256` (SHA-256 of an internal `search:<query>:<canister_id>` string built from the caller's raw spelling), where the README documents the field as the script's SHA-256 | code path |

###### SW6-1 detail

- Label: `IcBridge::sent` (`src/bridge.rs:387-389`) builds every audit label as
  `format!("{}.{method}", p.to_text())` and `record_message` (`:395-419`) puts `p` in
  `canisters` and `touched`. `p` is the message recipient.
- Policy: `check_call(p, method)` (`src/policy.rs:193-196`) keys the allowlist by the
  recipient. For `p = aaaaa-aa` the recipient is a proxy: the canister that is stopped,
  deleted, re-configured, uninstalled or read (`canister_status`) is the `canister_id` field
  of the arguments, which neither policy nor the audit look at.
- Reachable configuration: `set_allowlist(aaaaa-aa, vec {"canister_status"})` (any method list
  is accepted, `src/lib.rs:295-298`) plus `set_candid_override(aaaaa-aa, <ic.did>)` (accepted
  for any principal, `src/lib.rs:323-333`; without it the fetch of `aaaaa-aa`'s interface
  fails). A script `icp.call("aaaaa-aa", "canister_status", {canister_id: X})` then passes
  `reserve`, encodes via the override, is sent with `Call::unbounded_wait(aaaaa-aa, ..)`
  (`src/bridge.rs:524-528`), and writes `Started` with `canisters = ["aaaaa-aa"]`,
  `methods = ["aaaaa-aa.canister_status"]`; the closing entry is the same. Only the script's
  SHA-256 is stored (`src/lib.rs:223`), so `X` cannot be recovered from the log. The same
  grant admits `canister_status` on every canister this canister controls, not one chosen
  canister; the same holds for `stop_canister`, `update_settings`, `uninstall_code`,
  `delete_canister`. Error text on failure is also `call aaaaa-aa.<method> failed`
  (`src/bridge.rs:530`).
- Doc: README.md:387-389 "Each outbound message gets its own entry, naming the target and
  method in `methods`". For a management call the "target" recorded is the transport.
- Distinct from known L1-3 (acceptance of `aaaaa-aa` with `"*"`): this is about a narrow
  method grant and about what the record names; the fix for the known fetch-label finding
  (special-casing `fetch_did`) would not change it.
- Refute attempts: (1) does anything else record the subject? `violations` only on refusal;
  `error` only on failure; `run_id`/`script_sha256` don't carry arguments. No. (2) Is
  management access documented as unsupported? No: README never mentions it, and the code
  accepts it. (3) Could the IC route the call so the recipient is `X`? The call is made to
  `aaaaa-aa`; the label uses the `p` passed to `Call::*`, which is `aaaaa-aa`.
- Not reproduced: the production `IcBridge` cannot run natively (register #58), and changing
  the allowlist on the live network is outside this phase.

###### SW6-2 detail

- `src/lib.rs:122-125, 175-177`: `key = format!("search:{}:{}", query, canister_id)` using
  `args.canister_id` as typed; `script_sha256 = sha256(key)`; `language: "search"`.
  `search::scope` trims and canonicalises the id (`src/search.rs:39`), the hash does not, so
  `ryjl3-…`, `RYJL3-…` and ` ryjl3-…` searches of the same canister record three different
  hashes. Neither the key format nor the `"search"` language value is documented anywhere
  (README.md:374 lists "language, script SHA-256"; `grep "search:"` finds only `lib.rs:123`).
- Impact: an auditor cannot map a search entry back to the query without knowing the
  internal format, and equal searches do not hash equal. The subject canister is also
  missing from `canisters` when `canister_metadata` answers (that part is the known finding).

<a id="grid-sweep-r1-7"></a>

### grid-sweep-r1-7

#### Variant sweep r1-7: cleanup-time records that read rolled-back state

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6. Pattern: "A cleanup-time record reads state that the trap
rolled back, so it understates the work it describes." Seed findings (not re-reported): the
`Trapped` entry's `instructions` omits the trapped execution; the `Trapped` entry drops the
"…and N more" violation count; a trap inside cleanup leaks the slot and pending id.

Method: listed every code path that runs during ic-cdk's trap cleanup (`grep` for `impl Drop`
and `is_recovering_from_trap` in `src/`, `demo_store/src/`, `shims/`, plus ic-cdk 0.20.3
`call.rs:943` and `futures.rs:108`), then for each inventory row asked whether it writes or
feeds a record in cleanup, and whether that record reads heap state from the rolled-back
execution. Only three app Drop impls exist: `IcBridge` (`src/bridge.rs:243`), `RunSlot`
(`src/lib.rs:212`), `test_serial::Turn` (`src/runtimes/python.rs:184`, `#[cfg(test)]`).
Evidence is code path (C) unless marked; no request was sent to any running instance.

Candidate ids (SW7-n) refer to the candidates returned with this grid.

| Row(s) | Verdict | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| E5d cleanup callback / K7 | **finding SW7-1**; seeds known | Cleanup drops the whole `http_request_update` future as it was at the last commit. In a batch, an earlier tool call that finished in the trapped execution is still "unfinished" in that state, so its bridge writes the `Trapped` entry, and the tool call that actually trapped (never sent) leaves nothing |
| `Trapped.violations` (bridge.rs:261) | holds (documented) | Violations raised after the last message are rolled back; README.md:407 says the entry lists violations "recorded up to the last message". Same mechanism as the seeds, but disclosed. Dropped count: seed |
| `Trapped.calls` / `methods` / `canisters` | holds | `messages` and `touched` are only written in `record_message`, in the same execution as the send (K1); a send in the trapped execution is rolled back with its message, so the counts match what went out |
| `Trapped.timestamp_ns`, `caller`, `language`, `script_sha256`, `run_id` | holds for a single tool call; see SW7-1 for batches | Taken from `audit_key` / `started`, set before the first commit |
| `Trapped.instructions` | seed (known) | |
| `Trapped.error` | holds | Constant text; for a search it says "the script's result", wording only |

### grid-sweep-r1-8

#### Variant sweep r1-8

Pattern: **a limit marker added in one writer of a record type and missing in a sibling
writer** (seed: the `Trapped` entry drops the `…and N more` violation count that the
`run_script` and `run_search` closing entries add).

Method: grep for every marker and cap (`truncate`, `…[truncated]`, `…[output truncated]`,
`…and N more`, `omitted_methods`, `note`, `slice(`, `MAX_*`), group the writers by the record
they produce, and compare each writer with its siblings. Probes ran natively in a private copy
(`cargo test --lib`, shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`), copy deleted afterwards.

### grid-sweep-r1-9

#### Variant sweep r1-9: release bundled with a fallible write

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6. Pattern (from the confirmed finding "a trap inside the
cleanup callback leaks a run slot, a pending run id and the run's task until upgrade"):

> Cleanup that releases shared resources in the same step as a write that can fail, so a
> failed write also cancels the release.

Generalised for the sweep: any release of a shared resource (counter slot, pending-set
entry, executor task, lock, UI busy state, temp directory, child process, debug port) that
is committed in one atomic step (one IC message execution, one function without
`finally`) together with a write or other work that can fail, so that the failure undoes
or skips the release and nothing retries it.

Method: code reading of every release site found by `grep` for `impl Drop`, `fn drop`,
`is_recovering_from_trap`, `saturating_sub`, `remove(`, `finally`, `kill`, `close`,
`rmSync`, `disabled`, `trap`, `mktemp` across `src/`, `demo_store/src/`, `shims/`,
`scripts/`, `video/`; ic-cdk-executor 2.0.0 `machinery.rs` (`cancel_all_tasks_attached_to_method`,
`in_trap_recovery_context_for`) read for what the cleanup callback releases. Evidence is
code path only; nothing was built or run (the L2 reviewer already reproduced the cleanup
path live, `grid-L2-r1.md` K7). Result: **no new candidate**; every hit reduces to the known
root cause.

Release sites that exist in the code (complete list):

| Release | Where | Committed with |
|---|---|---|
| `ACTIVE_RUNS` slot | `RunSlot::drop` `src/lib.rs:212-216` | the execution that drops the run's future: normal end (K6) or cleanup (K7) |
| `PENDING_RUNS` id | `IcBridge::drop` `src/bridge.rs:246` | same execution as the `Trapped` append in K7, or as the closing append in K6 |
| executor task + method context | ic-cdk-executor `cancel_all_tasks_attached_to_method` | the cleanup callback execution, together with the task destructors (`IcBridge::drop` append) |
| Boa GC garbage | `boa_gc::force_collect` `src/runtimes/js.rs:361` | end of `js::run` |
| Python memory baseline | `rebased` `src/runtimes/python.rs:151-157` | each resumption |
| heap interface caches | `evict_interface` `src/bridge.rs:270-275` | `remove_allowlist` execution, with the stable remove |
| demo_store `reserved` | `cancel_order` `demo_store/src/lib.rs:314-328` | the same update, with the status write |
| demo page busy state | `rpc()` / `runComparison()` `finally` `src/demo.html:235, 513` | `finally` |
| Chrome process / DevTools port / profile dir | `cdp.mjs close()`; callers `render.mjs:27`, `stills.mjs:17`, `capture-demo.mjs:43` | end of script, no `finally` |
| frame directory | `render.mjs:35` `rmSync` | end of script |

Out-of-pattern observation (not a candidate here, recorded for the next round): when a
completed script and a following cached search share one HTTP request and the search traps
before any await (for example the known unbounded search render), the script's committed-looking

its result was indeed discarded with the reply, so the record is defensible. Code path only.

### grid-sweep-r1-10

#### Variant sweep r1-10: documented exhaustive lists the code does not match

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6. Pattern (from the confirmed "two kinds of request write
no entries" finding): **a documented exhaustive list ("two kinds", "exactly one of these",
"every", "only", "nothing can", an enumerated set of shapes or cases) that the code's
condition does not match**. Every row of `inventory.md` was searched for a list or an
absolute in its docs, interface comments, tool descriptions or code comments, and the
list was compared with the condition the code actually tests.

Evidence: reading the code at `295d64b`; native probe tests in a private `git archive`
copy (`cargo test --lib sweep_`, shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, copy deleted afterwards);
Boa 0.22.0 and Monty 1.6.0 sources in the cargo registry. Nothing deployed or changed.

##### New candidates

| Id | Sev | Title | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| SW10-1 | Low | `BoundedJobs::enqueue_job` drops every job that is not a promise or generic job, on the stated ground that "nothing in the sandbox can create them (no host async functions, no timers; Atomics and FinalizationRegistry are removed)". Dynamic `import()` creates one (`Job::AsyncJob`, Boa `vm/opcode/call/mod.rs:604-611`). The job is dropped, so the promise never settles: `try { await import("x") } catch (e) {}` cannot catch, and the run fails with "script stopped before finishing: a runtime limit ... was hit after an await, or it awaits a promise that never settles" instead of the loader's "Module could not be found." | reproduced (native): try/catch -> `Err("script stopped before finishing: ...")`; `import("x")` state after microtasks -> `"pending"`; the same TypeError delivered as a rejected promise is caught normally |
| SW10-2 | Low | Variant shorthand `"Tag"` is documented for a null payload only (README:355 "for a null payload, `"Tag"` alone also works"; SEARCH_DESCRIPTION "or "Tag" with no payload"; code comment candid_bridge.rs:281 "for null/reserved payloads"). The code passes JSON `null` to whatever the payload type is, so it is also accepted for `opt T` (and empty-record) payloads and silently sends `Tag = null` | reproduced (native): `variant { Set : opt nat; ... }` given `"Set"` -> sent `variant { Set = null }`; `{"Set":5}` -> `opt 5`; `"Num"` (nat payload) and `"Rec"` (non-empty record) correctly refused |
| SW10-3 | Low | `classify` ignores any invalid message that has a `result` or `error` key, per the comment "Responses from the client ... carry no method: ignore them"; the code never checks that `method` is absent. A request with an invalid id or `jsonrpc` gets `-32600` normally, but the same request with a stray `result`/`error` key is dropped without a reply (202 when it is the only message) | reproduced (native, `http_query`): `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":null,"method":"ping"}` -> 200 `-32600`; same plus `"result":0` -> 202 empty; `jsonrpc:"1.0"` + method + `error` -> 202; object id + `tools/call` + `result` -> 202 |
| SW10-4 | Low | `src/mcp.rs:4-5` module doc: the query "asks the gateway to upgrade anything containing `tools/call`" and "answers everything that is read-only". Code upgrades only an `execute_icp_script` or a search needing a fetch; a cached search and a `tools/call` with bad params (`-32602`) are answered in the query, and a read-only search that needs a fetch is upgraded | code path (`http_query` src/mcp.rs:358-367) + existing test `mcp::tests` cached-search-in-query |
| SW10-5 | Low | `certified_reads = true` is documented as "every request goes through an update call" (README:437) and "every MCP request goes through an update call" (`.did` / policy.rs:34 Limits doc). The code upgrades only requests that pass `authenticate`; wrong path (404), non-POST (405) and missing/invalid token (401) are still answered by the uncertified query, and so is the "demo page disabled" 404. (`mcp.rs:337` itself says "every authenticated request".) Related to, but not the same as, the known skip-certification finding | reproduced (native, `http_query(.., certified=true, ..)`): POST /mcp bad token -> (401, upgrade None); GET /mcp -> (405, None); POST /other -> (404, None); GET / -> (404, None) |

|---|---|---|
| README's list of requests that write no audit entry is incomplete (remembered fetch failure; L16-12) | The comment at src/lib.rs:159-160 lists the audited cases as "sent messages ... or was refused by policy" (`calls > 0 \|\| !violations.is_empty()`). A search whose fetch took a cap slot but whose messages were both refused on the spot by the system (queue full, no cycles) has `calls == 0` and no violation, so it writes no entry while the client gets a fetch error | code path |

The condition is `e.starts_with("policy:")`, which also matches "canister X is not allowlisted"; after a controller removes one canister mid-search, every later (still allowlisted) canister is reported "not fetched: policy: canister X is not allowlisted" and not tried | code path |
| JS per-round cap exceeded by a getter in call arguments | `SNAPSHOT_JS` doc (js.rs:41) says the copy takes "own data properties only"; `Object.keys` + `x[k]` also reads own enumerable accessor properties and runs their getters, which is how the known getter finding reaches `icp.call` | code path |
| L7-15 (`opt vec` given `[]`) | README:348-351 three-way rule ("An array: positional arguments") vs the array-like exception in `encode_args` (candid_bridge.rs:67-73): for a single `vec` argument, `[5]` is sent as `vec {5}` (not `5`) and `[1,2]` as one argument (not "takes 1 argument, got 2"). Same root cause as L7-15 | code path |

### grid-sweep-r1-11

#### Variant sweep r1-11: dependency recursion the app's limits do not bound

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6. Pattern under test:

> A recursion inside a dependency (parser or built-in) that no app limit bounds, where the
> app bounds only bytes, element counts or interpreter-level depth.

Already known and not re-reported here: Boa parser on deep parens/brackets, Boa built-ins on
deep data, candid_parser on nested interfaces, candid's decoder on deep replies (depth guard
is a no-op on wasm), the tmp_hack decode without quota, json_to_idl cost, Rhai deep arrays
(not reachable under default limits).

Result: **no new candidate.** Every other dependency recursion reachable from an untrusted
input either has its own depth limit or is stopped by an app limit or quota first.

##### How it was tested

- Private copy of the tree (no `target/`, `design/`, `docs/per-customer-canisters-plan.md`,
  `video/`, `.env`) in `/private/tmp/claude-501/sweep11.*`, shared
  `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/audit-target`. A probe `cdylib` (workspace member
  in the copy only) depends on `icp_code_mode` with default features and exports
  `run_js`, `run_py` (the app's own `runtimes::js::run` / `runtimes::python::run`, polled once
  with a no-op waker and a bridge that refuses calls) and `cand` (the app's
  `candid_bridge::Service::parse`, `encode_args`, `decode_reply`).
- Built `--release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` with the repo's `.cargo/config.toml`
  (verified in the artifact: `__stack_pointer` init 8,388,608, first data segment at
  8,388,608, so stack-first and an overflow traps). Run in Node 26 inside a Worker with a
  1,000 MB V8 stack and all 36 `ic0` imports stubbed, a fresh instance per case. A trap
  would show as `TRAP`; every case below ended in `OK` or a clean `ERR`.
- No live canister was touched. Evidence for each cell: R = reproduced in the wasm probe,
  CP = the code path settles it.

##### Cells

| Row | Dependency recursion | Cell | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| W8 / LIM24 (JS) | Boa re-entering `Context::run` from native code (callbacks, accessors, traps, coercions) | holds (R) | Boa counts `host_call_depth` together with frames against the recursion limit of 256 (`boa_engine-0.22.0/src/vm/mod.rs:1016-1030`). At depths 100, 200 and 255 every re-entry path ended in a clean `RuntimeLimitError` or `OK`, never a trap: `Array.prototype.map` callback, getter, Proxy `get` trap, `toString` and `valueOf` coercion, `sort` comparator, `String.prototype.replace` callback, `Function.prototype.apply`, `Reflect.construct`, generator through `Array.from`, `toJSON` through `JSON.stringify`, Promise executor |
| W8 (JS) | regress, the RegExp engine (parser, IR passes, backtracker) | holds (R) | `regress-0.12.0/src/types.rs:23` `MAX_NESTING_DEPTH = 256`. 255 nested groups, nested `(?:..)*`, nested lookaheads, `v`-mode nested classes and 255 named groups compile and run; 256 groups give `SyntaxError: ... too deeply nested` |
| W8 / B8 (JS) | `JSON.parse` | holds (R, CP) | Boa validates with `serde_json::from_str` first (`boa_engine-0.22.0/src/builtins/json/mod.rs:250`), so serde_json's 128-level limit refuses deep text before Boa's parser sees it; the reviver tree walk uses an explicit stack (`:75-164`) |

Over the threshold (5,000 unary minus) the scan refuses cleanly. L3's 50k/100k cases cover the scanned path |
| W10 (Python) | Monty heap -> host object export, `json`, `re`, `tomllib`, `copy` | holds (CP) | Export takes a VM recursion guard per level (`monty-1.6.0/src/object_bridge.rs:183-187`); `json.loads` limit 200 (`modules/json/load.rs:57, 440`), `json.dumps` takes recursion tokens (`dump.rs:551, 580`); `re` translator `MAX_NESTING = 64` (`types/re_syntax.rs:39`) and fancy-regex `MAX_RECURSION = 64` (`fancy-regex-0.20.2/src/lib.rs:147`, `parse.rs:1027`); `tomllib` builds with an explicit stack (`modules/tomllib/value.rs:5-6`). All are tied to the interpreter recursion limit or a fixed depth, not to bytes |

Nothing traps below the depth where `candid_parser` itself overflows (known finding) |
| B7 / W3 (search) | candid pretty-printer in `search::render` | holds | L3 measured 30,000-deep types rendering without a trap; not repeated |

Not a finding |
| E4 / E5 / E6-E14 / E20-E23 / U13 | ic-cdk argument decoding of every method in both canisters | holds (CP) | ic-cdk 0.20.3's generated entry points set `skipping_quota(10000)` (`ic-cdk-macros-0.20.3/src/export.rs:258-260`), and skipped values are charged 50x (`candid-0.10.40/src/de.rs:562-585`), so a deep skipped field is refused after about 200 levels; the expected types (`HttpRequest`, `HttpUpdateRequest`, admin args, demo_store args) have no deep typed path |
| W1 / U3 | serde_json on the request body and on JS call arguments | holds (CP) | serde_json's default recursion limit of 128 applies to `parse_body` and `js.rs:395`; nothing deeper reaches a recursive `Value` walk |
| W12 / B11 | `serde_json::to_string` of results and replies | holds (CP) | Values are built by bounded walks (snapshot, `to_json`, `idl_to_json` at most 128 deep) |
| B12 / D1-D5 | Candid `Decode!` of stable records | n/a | Written only by the app or a controller, flat record types |
| B17 / W16 / C5 | Demo page (browser JSON parsing and regex) | n/a | Runs in the user's browser on replies the canister built at most 128 deep; the regex cost issue is a known finding |
| C12 / C6 / C13 | Video tooling, setup script, audit tooling | n/a | Not deployed; no untrusted recursive input reaches a dependency |
| App-level `is_array_like` (`src/candid_bridge.rs:117-124`) | recursion over nested `opt` with no depth bound | holds (R) | App code, not a dependency. `encode_args("f", [null])` (the only path that calls it) on `f : (opt^n nat) -> (nat)` for n = 10,000, 20,000 and 40,000, which `candid_parser` parses: all encode, no trap |

None.

### grid-sweep-r2-0

#### Variant sweep r2-0: byte limits standing in for super-linear cost; cache writes in a trapping execution

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 2. Pattern:

> A size limit (bytes) standing in for a cost limit that is super-linear or recursive in the
> input's structure; a failure-cache write in the same execution as the work that can trap.

Not re-reported (known): candid_parser parse cost/stack on interfaces under 512 KiB, the
uncached fetch trap, json_to_idl value-driven cost, decoder depth and quota, Boa parser
stack overflow, Boa built-ins, synchronous JS never checking the budget, Python eval/exec,
search keywords x methods, demo page regex, Rhai O(requests^2) replay (documented).

Result: **three new candidates** (SW2-0-1 encoder type table, SW2-0-2 Boa compile of bindings,
SW2-0-3 override validated under the update limit, parsed under the query limit).

##### How it was tested

- Private copy of the tree (no `target/`, `design/`, `docs/per-customer-canisters-plan.md`,
  `video/`, `.env`) at `/private/tmp/claude-501/sweep-r2-0.*`, shared
  `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/audit-target`. The copy's package was renamed
  (`icp_code_mode_sweepr20`, lib name unchanged) because copies of the same workspace in the
  shared target dir get the same metadata hash and overwrite each other's test binary.
- One `#[cfg(test)]` probe (`src/sweep_probe.rs` in the copy only), `cargo test --release
  --lib`, each case on a thread with a 2 GiB stack, one process per case. Cost = macOS
  `/usr/bin/time -l` "instructions retired" for the whole process (native aarch64; a proxy for
  wasm instructions, not an on-chain count; process overhead about 0.03 B). Calls go through
  the app's own `Service::parse`, `Service::encode_args`, `Service::decode_reply`,
  `search::render`, and `runtimes::{js,python,rhai_rt}::run` with `MockBridge`.
- No live canister was touched; nothing was deployed and no setting changed.

##### Measurements

| Case | Input | Bytes | Native instructions |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Service::parse` | `f : (opt^16000 nat) -> ()` | 64,030 | 0.54 B |
| `encode_args("f", [null])` | same interface, `opt^N nat`, N = 1k / 2k / 4k / 8k / 12k / 16k | 4 KB - 64 KB | 0.25 / 1.00 / 4.41 / 18.4 / **43.7** / **80.5** B (quadratic) |
| `search::render` | same interface, 16k | 64 KB | 0.64 B |
| `decode_reply` | rets `opt^N nat`, hostile tables (N-entry chain, 1-entry `μT. opt T`), N up to 16k | | <= 0.55 B (clean error or `null`) |
| JS `(function(_0,_1,...){return 1}), 1` never called | 10,000 / 20,000 params | 48,692 / 98,692 | 15.8 / **65.2** B (quadratic) |
| JS `(function(){var a0=0;...}), 1` never called | 8,000 vars | 94,907 | 11.1 B |
| JS object literal / `switch` cases | 8,000 | 63-79 KB | 0.30 / 0.21 B |
| Python module assigns / function locals / dict literal | 8,000 | 63-79 KB | 0.15-0.17 B |
| Rhai map literal | 4,500 / 10,000 keys (10,001+ refused at parse) | 35 / 79 KB | 0.71 / 3.52 B |
| Rhai 9,000 statements, 256 functions | | 98 KB | 0.67 B / 0.04 B |
| `Service::parse` alias chain `type t_i = t_{i+1}` | 1,000 / 2,000 / 4,000 | 18 / 38 / 78 KB | 1.20 / 4.65 / **20.97** B |

##### Cells

| Row | Cell | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| LIM19 `MAX_DID_BYTES` / W5 / B5 encoder | **finding SW2-0-1** | 512 KiB bounds text; candid's `TypeSerialize::build_type` keys a `BTreeMap<Type, i32>` by structurally compared types, so encoding any value of a deeply nested inline arg type is O(depth^2 log depth). 48-64 KB interface: 44-80 B native per call, parse 0.5 B (R) |

| W16 / B17 demo page | known | regex quadratic |

| A* / CL* | n/a for this pattern | Claims about size limits: CL22 "Interfaces over 512 KiB are refused" holds literally; README does not claim 512 KiB bounds cost |

##### Candidates

###### SW2-0-1 Encoding a call against a deeply nested inline argument type costs O(depth^2) inside candid's encoder; a 48 KB interface traps every call to that method

- Where: `src/candid_bridge.rs:88-90` (`IDLArgs::to_bytes_with_types`), reached from
  `IcBridge::call` (`src/bridge.rs:517`); cost in `candid-0.10.40/src/ser.rs:264-290`
  (`TypeSerialize::build_type`, `type_map: BTreeMap<Type, i32>`, derived structural `Ord`).
- Repro (native): `Service::parse("service : { f : (opt^12000 nat) -> (); }")` 0.44 B;
  `encode_args("f", [null])` 43.7 B; at 16,000: 80.5 B. Interface 48-64 KB, value trivial.
- On chain (inferred, not run): the encode runs after `reserve` and before the send, in one
  execution, with no budget check, so it reaches the 40 B per-message limit and traps. If the
  interface is already cached (any earlier search) nothing was sent: the request rolls back
  with no audit entry, and every later call does the same for the hour the cache entry lives.
  If not cached, the fetch messages are logged, then parse, `DID_CACHE` insert and encode run in
  one callback execution: the trap rolls the cache insert back, a `Trapped` entry is written,
  and every later call re-sends both fetch messages and traps again.

###### SW2-0-2 Boa's parse/compile of a script is quadratic in bindings per scope; a 98.7 KB script costs 65 B instructions before any limit is checked

- Where: `src/runtimes/js.rs:366-368` (`ctx.eval` of the wrapped source), guarded only by
  `MAX_CODE_BYTES` (`src/runtimes/mod.rs:15, 52`).
- Repro (native): `(function(_0,_1,...,_<20,000 base-36 names>){return 1}), 1` (98,692 B,
  function never called) 65.2 B; 10,000 params 15.8 B; `(function(){var a0=0;... x8000}), 1`
  (94,907 B) 11.1 B.
- Distinct from the known findings: not stack (no nesting), not runtime (nothing runs), and
  a budget hook inside Boa's VM loop would not reach the compile step.

###### SW2-0-3 `set_candid_override` validates under the update limit, but the query path re-parses the override under the 5 B query limit and never keeps the result

- Where: `src/lib.rs:324-333` (validation in an update), `src/lib.rs:111-117` and
  `src/bridge.rs:207-227` (parse in `http_request`, insert discarded with the query).
- Measured: alias-chain overrides 2,000 / 4,000 types (38 / 78 KB) parse in 4.65 / 20.97 B
  native; about 3,000 aliases (~57 KB) lands between the two limits.
- Effect (code path): with such an override set, every query-path search whose scope
  includes that canister (every unscoped search) fails instead of answering or returning
  `upgrade`, so it never reaches the update path that would cache the parse. Only a script
  call to that canister (which needs an allowed method) or `certified_reads` gets past it, and
  the heap cache is empty again after each upgrade. Not reproduced live: setting an override
  is a configuration change outside the Live phase.

<a id="grid-sweep-r2-1"></a>

### grid-sweep-r2-1

#### Variant sweep r2-1

Pattern: **"A value budget that counts nodes while the per-node cost scales with the target
type's width; a budget checked before and after work but not during it."** Seed (known, not
re-reported): `json_to_idl` cost is value nodes x variant tags / record fields (L3-3).

Question asked of every inventory row: does this row convert, decode, render or copy a value
under a budget that counts *items* (nodes, values, methods, requests, entries, bytes on the
wire) while the work done *per item* grows with something the budget does not count (type
width, number size, text length, a memo table, a repr); and is any budget (value budget,
decoding quota, instruction budget) checked only before and after that work?

Evidence: code reading at `295d64b` plus native probes in a private copy
(`/private/tmp/claude-501/sweep-r2-1.*`, no `target/`, shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`,
`cargo test --release --lib sweep_*`, deleted afterwards). Instruction counts are macOS
`/usr/bin/time -l` "instructions retired" for the whole test process (native aarch64, a proxy
for wasm instructions, not an on-chain count; wasm32 has no native 64x64->128 multiply, so
bignum work is, if anything, dearer on-chain). Nothing deployed, nothing live touched.
R = reproduced, C = code path.

##### New candidates

| Id | Sev | Title | Ev |
|---|---|---|---|
| SW2-1-1 | High | Python `to_json` turns big ints and unsupported objects into `py_repr()` text that is never charged to the 4 MiB byte budget and costs time that scales with the value's size, while the node budget counts each as one node; no instruction check runs during the conversion | R |
| SW2-1-2 | High (may merge with L3-3) | A `nat`/`int` argument given as decimal text is parsed with a quadratic algorithm (`BigUint::parse_bytes`), while the value budget charges it once (1 node, linear bytes): one 4 MB string costs ~284B native instructions inside one uninterruptible encode | R |
| SW2-1-3 | Medium | candid's decoding quota charges 1 unit per `opt` value, but every `opt` value clones the decoder's subtype memo (`gamma`), whose size grows with the expected interface's width; a hostile allowlisted target makes one 85 KB reply cost ~75B native instructions in the reply callback | R |

###### SW2-1-1 (Python repr bypasses the value byte cap and the budget)

`src/runtimes/python.rs:62-100`: `budget.node()` once per object; `"int"` beyond i64
(`:71`), non-bytes `bytes` nodes (`:84`) and every other type (`:98`) become
`Value::String(o.py_repr())` with no `budget.bytes(..)`; dict keys are repr'd first and
counted after (`:92-93`). Python objects are shared, so `[x] * N` is N references in the VM
and N full reprs out of it. Probes (`run()` with `MockBridge`):

| Script | Outcome | Native instr. |
|---|---|---|
| `s = '1' * 30103` / `[s] * 1000` (control: same text as `str`) | refused: "more than 4194304 bytes of text" | 46M |
| `x = 1 << 100000` / `[x] * 1000` | **Ok**, 30,106,001 B of JSON (7x the cap) | 22.3B |
| same, as `icp.call(L, 'icrc1_balance_of', [x] * 1000)` | bridge receives a 30,106,001 B argument | 22.3B |
| `k = {'a' * 100000: 1}.keys()` / `[k] * 1000` | **Ok**, 100,028,001 B of JSON (24x the cap) | 13.7B |
| `x = 1 << 3000000` / `1` (VM work only) | Ok | 32M |
| `x = 1 << 3000000` / `x` | Ok, 903,092 B | 4.0B |
| `x = 1 << 3000000` / `[x] * 10` | Ok, 9 MB | 39.8B |

So a ~30-byte script reaches the 40B per-message limit in host code (`[x] * 20`), outside
Monty's budget (which stops at the VM boundary) and with no `check_budget` in `to_json`.
If the script made no call, the trap rolls back the whole request: no audit entry (K8).
Second symptom, same root cause (one node charged for a value whose expansion scales with
its width): a `bytes` value is one node and expands to `len` JSON elements, so
`b'a' * 4000000` leaves as a 4,000,000-element array (20x the 200k element cap, 155 MB RSS)
(R). JS (`SNAPSHOT_JS` counts every element and every string's length) and Rhai (blobs
count against `max_array_size` 10,000; `rhai-1.27.0/src/eval/data_check.rs:33,76,108`)
hold. Violates CL10 (README.md:369) and invariant 4. Relation to known findings: L7-6
(repr instead of an error, fidelity) and "Python's VM budget is not checked inside one
native operation (bigint power, repr)" are the VM side; this is the host conversion, and
the byte-cap bypass is not in either.

###### SW2-1-2 (quadratic bignum text parse in `json_to_idl`)

`src/candid_bridge.rs:206-207` -> `int::<Nat>` / `int::<Int>` -> `num_text` (`:160`, copies
with `replace('_', "")`) -> `Nat::from_str` -> `BigUint::parse_bytes(v, 10)`
(`candid-0.10.40/src/types/number.rs:57-67`; num-bigint 0.4.8 `from_radix_digits_be`,
`convert.rs:91`, multiply-accumulate per chunk, O(n^2)). The value budget charges the
string one node and its length in bytes (linear); the encode is one uninterruptible step
(`bridge.rs:516`, no budget check between `reserve` and send). Probe
`Service::parse("service : { f : (nat) -> () }").encode_args("f", "7" x d)`:

| digits | encoded bytes | native instr. |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | 12 | 39M (process) |
| 1,000,000 | 474,569 | 17.9B |
| 4,000,000 (inside the 4 MiB value cap) | 1,898,252 (fits a 2 MiB message) | 284.5B |

Reachable by any token holder with one string (JS `'7'.repeat(4e6)`, Python `'7' * 4000000`)
against any allowlisted method with a `nat` or `int` anywhere in its arguments (e.g. ICRC-1
`icrc1_transfer.amount`); ~1.5M digits already pass 40B. With the interface cached the
encode runs in the first execution, so the trap leaves no audit entry. demo_store's
arguments have no `nat`/`int` (only `nat64`/`nat32`, parsed by `u64`/`u32::from_str`,
linear), so the demo deployment is not exposed. Same function as L3-3 but a different cost
driver (number width, not type width); a fix for L3-3 (tag index, per-node budget check)
does not bound one `parse_bytes` call. Proposed fix: cap decimal text for `nat`/`int`
(e.g. 2^14 digits, far beyond any token amount) before parsing.

###### SW2-1-3 (candid decoder: per-`opt` clone of the subtype memo)

`candid-0.10.40/src/de.rs:801-842` `recoverable_visit_some` does `let self_clone =
self.clone()` for every `opt` value whose wire and expected types are both `opt`
(`:1158-1166`); `Deserializer` (`:309-336`) holds `gamma: HashSet<(Type, Type)>` by value.
`check_subtype` (`:515-528`, called for every `func`/`service` value, `:728, :740`) leaves
every proved `(Var, _)` pair in `gamma` (`types/subtype.rs:44-50, 660-683`; only failures
are retracted). The quota charges `add_cost(1)` per option (`:1155`, x50 untyped) and
nothing for the clone. Expected type (the target's own interface, `get : () -> (func () ->
(record { 0 : a0; ...; m-1 : a{m-1} }) query, vec opt null) query` with `type a{i} =
reserved`), reply = one `func` value (3 wire table entries) + `vec opt null` of n:

| m (interface bytes) | n (reply bytes) | decode | native instr. (decode only) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (83) | 70,000 (70 KB) | Ok, 16 ms | 0.6B (whole process) |
| 1,000 (28 KB) | 70,000 (73 KB) | Ok, 1.5 s | n/m |
| 5,000 (152 KB) | 70,000 (85 KB) | Ok, 7.0 s | ~74.8B (78.4B - 3.6B setup) |
| 15,000 (477 KB, under `MAX_DID_BYTES`) | 70,000 (115 KB) | Ok, 23.3 s | ~227.5B (258.4B - 30.8B setup) |

n = 80,000 runs out of quota, but only after the same time is spent (8.1 s at m = 5,000).
`decode_reply` runs in the reply callback (`bridge.rs:532`) with no budget check, so on
chain the callback exceeds 40B and traps (Trapped entry; repeated on every call to that
method). The reply is 85 KB, far under the ~400 KB the quota otherwise admits. Needs a
hostile allowlisted target (it controls both the interface and the reply); the deep-reply
stack overflow and the candid_parser cost findings are other routes for the same actor, but
this one has a different root cause (quota does not charge the memo clone) and is not fixed
by bounding depth or interface size. Proposed fix: decode untyped (`IDLArgs::from_bytes`)
and coerce with app code, or report upstream; app-side, a reply-callback budget check cannot
interrupt it.

<a id="grid-sweep-r2-2"></a>

### grid-sweep-r2-2

#### Variant sweep r2-2: limit applied after a dependency's recursive work; dependency guard absent on wasm

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 2. Pattern under test:

> A depth limit applied to the output of a recursive dependency instead of its input; a
> dependency's safety guard compiled out on the deployment target.

Searched in its general form: (a) any app limit (depth, node count, text bytes) that is
checked on what a dependency produced, after the dependency already did work sized by the
input; (b) any guard inside a dependency that is absent or different in the shipped build
(wasm32, release: `cfg(target_family = "wasm")`, `cfg(debug_assertions)`, 32-bit `usize`).

Not re-reported (known): candid decoder depth guard no-op on wasm, candid_parser on nested
interfaces, Boa parser/built-ins on deep data, Boa `capacity overflow` built-ins, tmp_hack
decode without quota, json_to_idl cost, Rhai deep data, inspect_message decode quota, Python
VM-side repr/bigint past the budget, Python print formatting in full.

##### How it was tested

- Private copy of the tree (no `target/`, `design/`, `docs/per-customer-canisters-plan.md`,
  `video/`, `.env`) in `/private/tmp/claude-501/sweep-r2-2.*` (deleted afterwards), shared
  `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/audit-target`. A probe `cdylib` (workspace member
  in the copy only) calls the app's own `runtimes::{python,js,rhai_rt}::run` with a bridge
  that refuses calls, polled once.
- Built `--release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` with the repo's `.cargo/config.toml`
  (artifact checked: `__stack_pointer` init 8,388,608, stack-first). Run in Node 26 Workers
  (1,000 MB V8 stack, all `ic0` imports stubbed, `performance_counter` = 0, so the instruction
  budget never fires in the probe). `TRAP` = wasm trap; `ERR` = clean error.
- `cargo tree --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -e normal` listed the 299 crates in the canister;
  each was grepped for wasm/debug-gated code.
- Evidence: R = reproduced in the wasm probe, CP = code path. No live canister was touched.

   - `class P:\n def __init__(s,x): s.x=x\na=[1]\nfor i in range(N):\n a=[a,a]\nP(a)` (88 bytes):
     N=18 -> OK, 1,835,011-byte result; N=24 -> OK, 117,440,515 bytes (3.5 s); N=26 -> OK,
     469,762,051 bytes (13.8 s); N=29 -> `TRAP RuntimeError: unreachable` (27.8 s, out of
     memory abort). Same with `@dataclass` and inside a dict/list.
   - `1 << 64000000` (13 bytes): OK, 19,265,922-byte decimal string after 58.5 s of wasm;
     `1 << 16000000` 4,816,482 bytes in 7.4 s. The VM refuses `len(str(1 << 1000000))` with
     `Exceeds the limit (4300 digits)`; the host-side conversion has no such limit.
   - Control: the plain list `a` at N=20 is refused (`value has more than 200000 elements`);
     a tuple dict key at N=26 is refused (`more than 4194304 bytes of text`) only after 11.5 s
     building the key's repr.
   Contradicts README:369 / CL10 (4 MiB of text in all three languages). With a 64 MiB Python
   heap, a short script makes the host do work and allocation far past `max_instructions` and
   the heap cap; on the IC this ends in the 40B-instruction or out-of-memory trap (the probe
   reached the OOM trap; the 40B figure was not measured). A run with no host call traps in
   its first message, so it leaves no audit entry. Related but distinct from L7-6 (same
   branch, fidelity) and the known VM-side repr/bigint budget finding (this runs outside the
   VM, after it finished).

No other cell produced a candidate.

### grid-sweep-r2-3

#### Variant sweep r2-3: limits the dependency scales differently

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 2. Pattern (from the confirmed DECODING_QUOTA
finding, not re-reported):

> A limit tuned without regard to how the dependency scales it, refusing valid data far
> below the transport limit; an error message that hides the real cause.

Question asked of every inventory row: does the app set a number (size, count, depth,
iterations) that a dependency or conversion layer then counts in a different unit
(summed, multiplied, per-frame, per-byte), so valid input well under the transport or
documented limit is refused, and does the error say why?

Evidence: **R** = reproduced natively at `295d64b` in a private copy (probe tests added to
`src/runtimes/mod.rs` of the copy, `cargo test --lib sweep_probe`, debug profile, shared
`CARGO_TARGET_DIR`); replies were built by encoding real Candid and decoding through
`Service::decode_reply`, the production reply path. **C** = code path. The copy was deleted.

##### New candidates

| Id | Sev | Candidate | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| SW2-3-1 | Medium | Rhai's array/map/string limits are summed over the whole nested value by Rhai (`calc_data_sizes`), while the app set them as per-container caps (10,000 / 10,000 / 1 MiB). A demo_store-shaped `vec Order` reply of 1,112 single-item orders (39,008 B on the wire) fails with `Size of object map too large`; 1,111 passes. `vec Product` fails at 2,600 (76,925 B). `vec vec nat64` 101x100 (80,913 B) fails with `Size of array/BLOB too large`. JS and Python accept all of them. The call has already executed. No map in the reply has more than 6 keys, so the message points at the wrong thing. Script-built data is hit the same way (1,700 six-field records). | R |
| SW2-3-2 | Low | Boa's 1M loop limit is one counter per call frame for all its loops, never reset, and `String.prototype.repeat` charges one iteration per repetition. Refused: `'ab'.repeat(1100000).length` (no loop in the script); two 600k loops in one frame (the same loops in two functions pass); three passes over a 400,000-element reply (the reply decodes, at the decoding quota); 500k iterations before an `await` plus 600k after. After an await, the error is the generic "a runtime limit (loop iterations, recursion, stack) was hit after an await, or it awaits a promise that never settles". README:370 says "1M loop iterations". | R |
| SW2-3-3 | Low | Rhai `set_max_expr_depths(64, 32)` was meant for nesting, but Rhai counts each operator in a flat chain as one level. `x + x + ...` with 66 terms at top level, about 28 in a function, or 25 inside a for/if in a function, fails with `syntax error: Expression exceeds maximum complexity`, which does not name a depth. A 70-term `&&` chain fails at top level. All are tiny sources, far under the 100 KiB code limit. | R |
| SW2-3-4 | Low | `MAX_VALUE_NODES` (200k) counts a blob as one element per byte once `idl_to_json` turns it into a JSON array. A 250,000-byte blob reply decodes, but forwarding it as a call argument fails in JS and Python with `value has more than 200000 elements`. The inter-canister limit is 2 MiB, and Python `bytes` and Rhai blobs are counted as bytes, not elements. Python cannot convert the list (`bytes(list)` gives `TypeError` in Monty). JS can work around it with a hex string (500,004-byte argument sent). | R |
| SW2-3-5 | Low | The interface-fetch fallback hides the first failure. When `canister_metadata` rejects (for example a private `candid:service` section) or its reply does not decode, `fetch_did` (`src/bridge.rs:424-435`) discards that error and returns only the `__get_candid_interface_tmp_hack` error, which is cached in `DID_FAILED` for 5 minutes. This matches only the second half of the pattern (no limit involved). | C |

### grid-sweep-r2-4

#### Variant sweep r2-4: input count unbounded where only output is capped

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 2. Pattern (seed, known, not re-reported: search
keyword count and length are unbounded while `MAX_METHODS` caps only what is shown):

> A cap that bounds what is stored or returned, while the number (or size) of inputs that
> feed the work before the cap is applied is unbounded, so the work and memory scale with
> the input and only the output looks bounded.

Method: listed every cap in the Limits inventory and every `truncate`, `MAX_*`, `.take(`,
`join(` and early-return guard in `src/`, then asked for each one whether it counts the
inputs that do the work or only what is kept or returned. Probes ran natively in a private
copy (`cargo test --lib`, shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, own test binary copied out because the
shared build dir was being overwritten by other agents' builds). The copy was deleted
afterwards. No live instance was touched.

##### Findings

###### SW24-1 (new): the log cap counts line bytes, never lines; empty lines are free

`console_fn` (`src/runtimes/js.rs:227-248`), Rhai `RunState::log`
(`src/runtimes/rhai_rt.rs:46-54`) and `LogBuf::push` (`src/bridge.rs:106-119`) add only
`line.len()` to the 64 KiB counter. `console.log()` / `console.log("")` / Rhai `print("")`
add 0 bytes and are always accepted, so the `Vec<String>` of lines grows without a count
limit while the run lasts (JS keeps it in `State` across every await). `tool_result`
(`src/mcp.rs:164-167`) then joins all of them with `\n` and truncates to 250 KB escaped.

Reproduced natively (test in the private copy, `MockBridge`):

| Script | Lines kept | Bytes counted | Console text returned | Peak RSS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| JS `function f(){for(let i=0;i<1e6;i++) console.log()} for(let j=0;j<1;j++) f()` | 1,000,000 | 0 | 125,031 chars | 79 MB |
| same, 5 frames | 5,000,000 | 0 | 125,031 | 357 MB |
| same, 20 frames | 20,000,000 | 0 | 125,031 | 1.49 GB |
| Rhai `for i in 0..400000 { print(""); } 1` | 333,332 (op limit hit, logs still kept) | 0 | | |

On chain the only bound is the instruction budget (each `console.log` checks it); the
number of lines that fit in 20B instructions was not measured (no live run in this sweep).
Python holds: Monty counts the newline of every `print`.

###### SW24-2 (new): JS `console.log` formats every argument in full before applying the cap

`console_fn` checks `log_bytes >= MAX_LOG_BYTES` once, then runs
`args.iter().map(display).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" ")` and only then truncates the line
to the remaining budget. The number of arguments is unbounded (`console.log.apply(null, a)`),
each object argument gets its own 200k-node / 4 MiB snapshot budget, and string arguments
are copied by `to_std_string_escaped` with no size check at all. The work is one native
call with no instruction-budget check inside it.

Reproduced natively: `let s='x'.repeat(1<<19); s=s+s; const a=Array(N).fill(s);
console.log.apply(null, a); return 1` (JS heap: one 1 MiB string and an N-element array):

| N | Result | Line kept | Peak RSS | Time (debug build) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Ok | 21 B (`…[output truncated]`) | 33 MB | 0.05 s |
| 300 | Ok | 21 B | 662 MB | 3.8 s |
| 1000 | Ok | 21 B | 2.13 GB | 12.6 s |

About 2 MB of host memory per argument (the copies plus the joined string). On wasm32
(4 GiB address space, 3 GiB default `wasm_memory_limit`) N of about 1,500 exceeds memory. The
on-chain outcome (out-of-memory trap, or, after an await, heap growth past
`wasm_memory_limit` as in the known L3 memory finding) was not run on a live canister.

##### Unverified note (not a finding)

JS `icp.call` / `icp.candid` copy the canister and method strings (`arg_string`,
`js.rs:195-200`) into up to 64 pending requests per round before `MAX_METHOD_LEN` and the
80 B principal echo apply, at dispatch. Count is bounded (64), so this is a size check after
the copy, not this pattern. Not measured.

<a id="grid-sweep-r2-5"></a>

### grid-sweep-r2-5

#### Variant sweep r2-5

Pattern: "A limit on count only, where the size of each item is unbounded or configurable."

Question asked of every inventory row: does a limit here count items (nodes, elements,
entries, arguments, requests, methods, pages) while the size of each item is not counted,
or is counted on a path the item can avoid?

Method: code reading at `295d64b` plus native tests in a private copy
(`/private/tmp/claude-501/sweep-r2-5.*`, deleted afterwards; `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` the shared
audit target, debug test profile, the binary copied out right after each build because the
shared target directory is rebuilt by other agents). The tests called
`runtimes::{python,rhai_rt,js}::run` and `search::render` paths with the existing
`bridge::mock::MockBridge`; peak memory measured with `/usr/bin/time -l` (macOS, max RSS).
Nothing was deployed and no running instance was contacted.

Evidence key: **R** = reproduced natively; **C** = code path; **known** = already in the
list of known findings (not re-reported).

##### New candidates

| Id | Severity | Title | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| SW2-5a | High | Python values that are not `str` (big ints, exceptions, Decimal, any repr fallback) count as one node with no text bytes, so one shared value referenced N times leaves the script as N copies: register #21 regressed for Python | R |
| SW2-5b | High | Rhai's size limits count array elements, map entries and value-string bytes only: map keys and curried `FnPtr` contents are not counted, so a Rhai run's memory and nesting depth are unbounded (2 GB held, 18M elements under the 10,000-element limit, native stack overflow from a 3-line script) | R |
| SW2-5c | Medium | JS `console.log` / `print` applies the value budget per argument and formats every argument before the log cap: one call with N references to one 1 MB string makes the host allocate about 2N MB | R |
| SW2-5d | Low | `search::MAX_METHODS` caps the number of methods in a search result, not its size; the code calls searches "size-capped" | C |

###### SW2-5a: Python repr fallbacks bypass `MAX_VALUE_BYTES`

`src/runtimes/python.rs:61-100` `to_json` calls `budget.node()` for every value but
`budget.bytes()` only for `str`, `bytes` and dict keys. Ints beyond i64 become
`Value::String(o.py_repr())` (`:71`), and every other type falls to
`_ => Value::String(o.py_repr())` (`:98`), with no byte charge. `monty_types` `py_repr` of a
`BigInt` is `write!(f, "{v}")` (`monty-types-1.6.0/src/object.rs:717`), with no 4300-digit
cap (that cap lives in the VM, not in the export); an `Exception` node carries its full
`arg: Option<String>` (`graph.rs:95-100`) and its repr includes it. The same `to_json` is
used for results and for `icp.call` arguments (`python.rs:244`).

| Script (Python, MockBridge) | Outcome |
|---|---|
| `x = str(10**4000)` then `[x] * 2000` (control) | refused: `value holds more than 4194304 bytes of text` |
| `x = 10**4000` then `[x] * 2000` | Ok, 8,008,001 bytes of JSON |
| `x = 10**200000` then `[x] * 50` | Ok, 10,000,201 bytes |
| `icp.call(L, 'icrc1_balance_of', {'owner': [10**4000] * 2000})` | call made with 8,008,011 bytes of arguments |
| `e = ValueError('x' * 1000000)` then `[e] * 20` | Ok, 20,000,341 bytes |
| same, `[e] * 500` | Ok, 500,008,501 bytes, 963 MB peak RSS, 258 s (debug); the VM held about 1 MB, inside its 64 MiB cap |

README.md:369 says every value leaving a script is limited to 4 MiB of text "in all three
languages". It is not for Python, and the amplification is the one register #21 was fixed
for: small in the VM, gigabytes once copied out. Not run on-chain. By the code path, about
3,000 references to a 1 MB exception take more than 3 GiB of host memory, which ends the
message in an out-of-memory trap (no audit entry if no message was sent yet; register #11).
Fix: charge `py_repr` text to `budget.bytes()` before building the string. For big ints,
check the digit count before formatting: `bits * log10(2)` gives an upper bound. Regression
test: add `[10**4000] * 2000` and `[ValueError('x' * 1000000)] * 20` to
`python::values_are_bounded`.

###### SW2-5b: Rhai's size limits leave out map keys and `FnPtr` curry payloads

`rhai-1.27.0/src/eval/data_check.rs:19-101`: `calc_array_sizes` / `calc_map_sizes` count one
per element or entry and add `Str` value lengths. They never look at map keys
(`map.values()` only) and give 0 for `Union::FnPtr`, including its curried `Dynamic`s. The
engine is configured with only these limits (`rhai_rt.rs:122-131`): string 1 MiB, array
10,000, map 10,000, variables 1,000. README.md:451 says "Rhai [is limited] by its size
limits", and register #24 accepts the missing memory cap for JS only.

| Script (Rhai, MockBridge) | Outcome |
|---|---|
| `let m = #{}; let s = "k"; s.pad(1000000, 'k'); for i in 0..N { m[s + i] = 1; } m.len()`, N = 1 / 500 / 2000 | Ok; peak RSS 15 MB / 529 MB / 2,055 MB (about 6k operations for N = 2000) |
| `let big = []; for i in 0..9000 { big.push(i); } let f = Fn("x").curry(big); let a = []; for i in 0..2000 { a.push(f); } a.len()` | Ok, 2000: one array holding 18M elements under the 10,000-element limit; 446 MB RSS |
| `let f = Fn("x"); for i in 0..N { f = Fn("x").curry(take(f)); } 1`, thread stack 8 MiB | N = 1000 Ok; N = 20,000, 30,000 and 100,000: **`thread has overflowed its stack`, process abort** (recursive drop/clone of the nested `FnPtr`). N up to about 100,000 fits in the 1M-operation limit (125,000 hits `Too many operations`) |

The same values cannot leave the script: `to_json_value` counts map-key bytes, and
`rhai::serde::from_dynamic` refuses `FnPtr` ("Output type incorrect: Fn"). So the harm is
inside the run: memory beyond the 3 GiB Wasm limit (about 3,500 one-MB keys) and native
recursion. On-chain, both end in a trap, which leaves no audit entry before the first send
and a `Trapped` entry after it. Not run on-chain: wasm frame sizes differ from native debug,
so the overflow depth on wasm is unverified; the 100k depth reachable here is about 5x the
native-debug threshold. This also contradicts the "Rhai variant not reachable under default
limits" part of the known native-stack-overflow finding: the known analysis bounded Rhai
nesting through the array-size limit, which `FnPtr` nesting escapes. Fix: make
`to_json_value`, `print` and `debug` refuse `FnPtr`. For memory, give Rhai the same
counting-allocator cap as Python (the allocator already exists, `lib.rs:357-425`), or
disallow `curry` and cap total map-key bytes through an `on_var`/`on_def_var` check.
Regression test: the three scripts above must fail cleanly.

###### SW2-5c: JS console formats all arguments before the cap

`src/runtimes/js.rs:227-248` `console_fn` checks `budget(st)` and `log_bytes >= MAX_LOG_BYTES`
once, then runs `display` on **every** argument and joins them before truncating to
the 64 KiB cap. `display` (`:217-225`) copies strings in full with `to_std_string_escaped`
(no snapshot, no 4 MiB check), and gives every other argument its own snapshot with a fresh
4 MiB budget. The argument count is bounded only by Boa's stack-size limit (10,240 values).

| Script (JS, MockBridge, debug) | Peak RSS | Log kept |
|---|---|---|
| `const s = 'x'.repeat(1e6); const a = Array(1).fill(s); console.log(...a)` plus the same with `[s,s,s,s]` elements | 57 MB | 21 bytes |
| same, 500 arguments | 4,918 MB (71 s) | 21 bytes |
| same, 2000 arguments | 15,946 MB (287 s) | 21 bytes |

The engine holds one 1 MB string and an array of references. The host makes the copies, so
this is the register #21 amplification on the print path, not the JS-heap hoarding that
register #24 accepts. README.md:369 lists "printed values" under the 4 MiB limit. On-chain
(not run), about 2,000 one-MB arguments pass 4 GiB and trap the message. If the call
happens in a response callback and stays under 4 GiB, it reaches the known "JS heap past
wasm_memory_limit after an await" state by a different route. That is not run: it would
be destructive and needs the Live phase. The 21-byte log kept is the known LogBuf marker
issue. Fix: format arguments one at a time against the remaining log bytes, stop at the cap,
and run strings through the same byte budget. Regression test: extend
`js::console_output_is_capped_while_running` with `console.log(...Array(500).fill(s))` and
assert the bytes allocated (counting allocator) stay near the cap.

###### SW2-5d: search result size is count-capped only

`src/search.rs:17` `MAX_METHODS = 40` limits shown methods. Each shown method's `signature`
is the full one-line pretty-print of its (possibly inline) types, and every named type it
references is printed in `types` (`search.rs:118-139`). An interface is limited only to
512 KiB (`MAX_DID_BYTES`) and the number of allowlisted canisters is unlimited, so one
search can exceed `MAX_RESULT_BYTES` once two or more large interfaces are in scope. It is
then cut to invalid JSON (known L7-1), and five such searches overflow the batch reply
(known). `mcp.rs:390-391` exempts searches from the one-tool rule because they are
"size-capped", and the inventory lists LIM32 as protecting result size. Only the claim and
the count-only cap are new; the downstream effects are known. Fix: cap the rendered bytes
(stop adding methods and types at a byte budget, then report `omitted_methods`).

### grid-sweep-r2-6

#### Variant sweep r2-6

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6. Pattern: **"Storage that grows from unauthenticated or
cheap requests; a read whose reply size grows with storage."** Seeds (known, not
re-reported): demo_store orders / zero-quantity lines and `list_orders(null)`; audit log
growth (register #31); `get_audit_logs` page capped by count, not bytes; Boa `Symbol.for`
registry; admin inputs returned whole by `get_policy`.

Method: code reading at `295d64b` plus a scan of every process-global or thread-local store
in the app and in the dependencies that run inside the canister (`grep` for `thread_local!`,
`static … Mutex/RwLock/OnceLock/LazyLock/RefCell` in boa_engine/boa_gc/boa_string/
boa_interner 0.22.0, monty/monty-types 1.6.0, rhai 1.27.0, candid 0.10.40,
candid_parser 0.4.1, ic-cdk 0.20.3, ic-cdk-executor 2.0.0). Nothing compiled or run (every
cell is a code-path statement, C). For each row the questions were: (a) can an
unauthenticated or cheap request make something that outlives the request grow, and
(b) does any read return, or iterate, an amount that grows with that store?

Result: **no new candidate.** Every growing store or growing read is an already-known
finding, or is bounded by something only a controller sets.

<a id="grid-sweep-r2-7"></a>

### grid-sweep-r2-7

#### Variant sweep r2-7: per-key cache filled after an await, no in-flight marker

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 2. Pattern: **"A per-key cache filled only after an
await, with no in-flight marker, so N concurrent misses do the work N times and each is
charged against a shared budget."** Seed (known, not re-reported): L4-1, concurrent misses on
one interface each send their own fetch (`IcBridge::candid`, `src/bridge.rs:471-508`), within
one JS `Promise.all` / Python `gather` batch and across concurrent scripts and searches; L9-5
(expired entry discarded on a failed refresh).

Method: listed every cache, memo, map and set that outlives one step (`thread_local!`,
`static`, `BTreeMap`/`HashMap`, `cache`, `memo`, `seen`) in `src/`, `src/runtimes/`,
`demo_store/src/`, `shims/`, `src/demo.html`, `video/*.mjs`, `scripts/`; for each, found where
it is read, where it is written, and whether an `await` (or a JS `await`) separates the two;
then looked for concurrent callers of that path and the budget each miss is charged to. Also
asked the inverse question the pattern implies: without an in-flight marker, can a fill that
lands after the await undo something done during the wait (eviction, refresh)? Evidence: C =
code path. Nothing was built and nothing live was touched (`IcBridge` cannot run natively,
register #58). Excluded: `docs/per-customer-canisters-plan.md`, `design/`.

##### Candidate findings

| Id | Sev | Title | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| SW7-1 | Low | An interface fetch in flight when `remove_allowlist` runs re-inserts the removed canister's interface into `DID_CACHE` (fresh 1 h timestamp) after the eviction, so `icp.candid` keeps serving it with no allowlist check, and the cache is no longer "bounded by the allowlist size" | C |

###### SW7-1 detail

`remove_allowlist` (`src/lib.rs:301-304`) calls `bridge::evict_interface` (`src/bridge.rs:270-275`,
"Forget everything cached about a canister (called when it leaves the allowlist)"), which
removes the key from `DID_CACHE`, `DID_FAILED` and `OVERRIDES`. `IcBridge::candid`
(`src/bridge.rs:486-507`) reserves, awaits `fetch_did` (one or two messages), then in the
reply continuation inserts `DID_CACHE[key] = (did, svc, now)` unconditionally: there is no
in-flight marker or generation for the key, and the allowlist is not re-read. Sequence:

1. A script (or update-path search) calls `icp.candid(X)` / `icp.call(X, ..)` on a cold X;
   `reserve` passes, `canister_metadata` is sent (await).
2. The controller calls `remove_allowlist(X)`; `evict_interface` finds nothing to remove.
3. The fetch reply arrives; line 499 inserts X's interface with `now` as its fetch time.
4. For the next hour, any script's `icp.candid(X)` returns it from `cache_get` at line 478,
   before `reserve`, so with no allowlist check (known finding: `icp.candid` serves cached
   interfaces without an allowlist check; eviction was the only thing bounding it).

A failed fetch lands the same way in `DID_FAILED` (line 504): after `remove_allowlist(X)` +
`set_allowlist(X, ..)` during the window, X is refused for 5 minutes with the stale error.

Window: normally one round trip. X itself controls its length: if X does not publish
`candid:service`, the fetch falls back to `X.__get_candid_interface_tmp_hack` with
`bounded_wait` (ic-cdk default 300 s), so a target being removed for misbehaving can hold the
fill open for up to 300 s. The comment at `src/bridge.rs:192-193` ("bounded by the allowlist
size") also stops being true: repeated add/remove cycles leave entries for canisters that are
not allowlisted, until upgrade. Overlap: the known finding "Allowlist and token checks taken
before a suspension are trusted after it" covers a *call* sent after removal; this is the
cache fill, a different effect of the same missing re-check. A verifier may merge them.
Fix: in the continuation, insert only if `policy::is_allowlisted(p)` still holds (or keep a
per-key generation bumped by `evict_interface` and drop fills from an older generation).
Regression test: needs the `IcBridge` seam asked for by register #58.

##### Refuted while sweeping

- **Stale interface overwriting a newer one across a target upgrade.** Two concurrent fetches
  that straddle the target's upgrade: the later reply wins, and it gets a fresh `now`. Both
  `canister_metadata` requests go from this canister to the management canister, which
  answers in request order, so the later reply is the newer read. Mixed paths (one metadata,
  one `tmp_hack` fallback) could in theory invert the order, but that needs the target to
  drop its `candid:service` section and be upgraded inside one fetch window; not reproduced,
  left as unverified.
- **Success/failure last-writer race on V2/V4.** Harmless: lookups check `DID_CACHE` first.

<a id="grid-sweep-r2-8"></a>

### grid-sweep-r2-8

#### Variant sweep r2-8

Pattern: "A limit counted per logical operation while the operation fans out to several
outbound messages."

Method: code reading at `295d64b`, plus one live probe of read-only requests against the local
network on port 8010. Nothing was deployed, upgraded or reconfigured. The bearer token was read
from `.env` into a shell variable and was not printed. For each inventory row the question was:
is a limit counted once for an operation that can send more than one message (or HTTP request,
run, or retry), so that the real number of messages is a multiple of the limit?

Evidence keys: **C** = the code path produces it unambiguously; **R** = reproduced.

Result: **no new candidate.** Every hit in the code is already known (the fetch slot that can
send 2 messages, the duplicate fetches on concurrent misses, Python's lack of a per-batch request
cap, the JS getter that gets past the per-round cap, the 5-searches cap that applies only on the
update path, searches taking no run slot, the 8 runs x 25 calls of held prepayment, the
fetch timeout that is not `call_timeout_seconds`, and the budget that is not re-checked before
sending). One new place where the pattern could apply, the demo page's classic side sending 12
concurrent HTTP requests against the 8-run cap, was tested live and holds on the local network.

##### Outbound-message rows

| Row | Limit and its unit | Fan-out under one unit | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| O2 / LIM1: an interface fetch (`IcBridge::candid`, `bridge.rs:486`) | One call-cap slot per fetch (`reserve(p, None)`) | `fetch_did` (`bridge.rs:424-437`) sends `canister_metadata` and then `__get_candid_interface_tmp_hack`. That is 2 messages for 1 slot, and the second has no `reserve` | **known** (L4-2: "one call-cap slot can send two messages"; the missing budget and allowlist re-checks before the send are already listed as separate known findings) |
| O1 + O2: `icp.call` on a cold cache (`bridge.rs:510-516`) | 2 slots (one for the call, one for the fetch inside `service()`) | Up to 3 messages for 2 slots | **known** (L4-1/L4-2; documented by CL7, "every interface fetch that misses the cache") |
| O2 from concurrent misses (JS `join_all`, Python `gather`, concurrent requests) | One slot per request | N requests send N identical fetches (no single-flight) | **known** (L4-1) |
| LIM3 `call_timeout_seconds` | Applies to each script call | A fetch makes 2 `bounded_wait` calls at ic-cdk's default 300 s each, and ignores the setting | **known** ("call_timeout_seconds is not applied to interface fetches, which use ic-cdk's default 300 s each") |
| LIM2 instruction budget | Checked once per host request in `reserve` | One request does fetch, parse, encode and then sends | **known** ("Budget checked before the interface-fetch await and not again before send") |

Without that, holds: L4 found that requests past the cap are refused in `reserve` before any await |

### grid-sweep-r2-9

#### Variant sweep r2-9: per-request limit enforced in one of two sibling handlers

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 2. Pattern (seed: known finding "MAX_SEARCHES is
enforced only in http_update; the query path answers up to 50 cached searches"):

> A per-request limit enforced in one of two sibling handlers for the same request.

Generalised for the sweep: two or more handlers that serve the same logical request (query
and update routes, `inspect_message` and the method, sibling SDK functions or sibling
arguments of one SDK call, the three runtimes, admin endpoint and `InitArgs`, the
`canister_metadata` and `__get_candid_interface_tmp_hack` fetch paths, `rpc()` and `post()` on
the demo page), where a size, count, depth, budget or cap check exists in one and is missing
or different in the other.

Method: listed every limit constant and check site (`grep` for `MAX_`, `len() >`, `>=`,
`truncate`, `budget`, `quota`, `set_max_`, `limit`) in `src/`, `src/runtimes/`,
`demo_store/src/`, `src/demo.html`; for each, found every handler that serves the same
request and compared. One native reproduction (below) in a private copy built with the shared
`CARGO_TARGET_DIR`; the copy was deleted afterwards. Known findings listed in the task were
not re-reported.

- **Sibling handlers:** the three arguments of one `icp.call` request (only `args` is
  snapshotted); and the same request in Python (`python.rs:243-244` counts every positional
  argument in one `ValueBudget`) and Rhai (1 MiB string cap).
- **Reproduced** natively (MockBridge, default features), private copy, one added test:
  - JS `icp.call(L, <5 MiB string>, null)`: Ok, the bridge received a 5,242,880-byte method.
  - Python `icp.call(L, 'm' * 5 MiB)`: `value holds more than 4194304 bytes of text`, no call.
  - Rhai: `Length of string too large`, no call.
  - JS `icp.candid(<5 MiB string>)`: the 5 MiB id reached the bridge (error text 5,242,923 bytes
    from MockBridge's echo; Python refuses at 4 MiB).
  - JS `Promise.all` of 64 `icp.call(L, m, null)` sharing one 5 MiB string `m`: Ok, 64 calls,
    335,544,320 bytes of method text handed to the host in one round. That is the
    amplification `MAX_VALUE_BYTES` exists to stop (`bridge.rs:43-46`: "one 1 MB string
    referenced 5,000 times is a small value inside the engine and a 5 GB one once copied out").
- **On-chain effect (code path):** `IcBridge::call` refuses methods over 256 B and
  `parse_principal` truncates the echoed id to 80 B, so nothing oversized is sent or audited.
  The copies are still made, one Rust `String` per pending request, and held until the
  round is dispatched: up to 64 x the string's size in heap per round, outside every value
  limit. JS has no memory cap (register #24), so the reachable size is bounded only by the
  Wasm memory limit.
- **Severity:** Medium (a documented limit is inconsistent between handlers; CL10 is false
  for JS call arguments). Not graded higher: no trap or wrong effect was demonstrated on-chain.
- **Fix:** count `canister` and `method` in the same `ValueBudget` (or refuse
  canister ids over the 63-char principal text maximum and methods over `MAX_METHOD_LEN`)
  inside `request_fn`, before `to_std_string_escaped`.

<a id="grid-sweep-r2-10"></a>

### grid-sweep-r2-10

#### Variant sweep r2-10: a concurrency cap that covers one kind of suspended request but not a sibling

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 2. Source finding: searches take no run slot, so
concurrent searches suspended on interface fetches are not capped by `MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS`
and not counted in `active_runs`.

Pattern, stated generally: **a cap on things that are suspended at once (runs, requests per
round, in-flight calls) counts one kind of suspended work, while a sibling kind that waits
on the same awaits is not counted.**

For each row the question is: does this row cap or count concurrently suspended work, and
is there other work that suspends on the same awaits and escapes the count? Known findings
are marked **known** and not reported again.

Evidence key: **R** = reproduced here; **CP** = code path unambiguous; **R-prior** = cited grid.

##### Result

One new candidate:

- **SW10-1 (CP).** When a run traps in a reply callback, ic-cdk's cleanup drops the run's
  task, which returns its `RunSlot` and removes it from `PENDING_RUNS`. The other calls of
  the same `join_all` batch are still outstanding at the system level (ic-cdk only marks
  their state `Trapped`; `ic-cdk-0.20.3/src/call.rs:943-950, 977-981, 1003-1038`). Those
  orphaned calls keep waiting, but neither the run cap nor `pending_run_ids` counts them.

One observation that is not a finding: the demo page's comparison fans out 12 concurrent
`execute_icp_script` requests. That did not trip the 8-run cap on the local network
(see C5).
