### grid-sweep-r2-11

#### Variant sweep r2-11: global slot cap held across an external wait with no deadline

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6. Pattern under test:

> A global per-process slot cap held across an external wait with no deadline, letting one
> caller's waits starve all callers.

Already known and not re-reported here: a run slot is held across unbounded-wait calls, so
8 runs waiting on a silent target make every later script "busy"; in-flight response
prepayment held by unbounded waits; searches take no run slot; no single-flight on interface
fetches; `call_timeout_seconds` not applied to interface fetches (300 s each); a call
timeout bounds each call, not the stop; Python and JS heaps held while suspended
(`wasm_memory_limit`, Boa GC heap, Python memory accounting); DID_FAILED blocking all callers
for 5 minutes.

Method: listed every per-process cap, counter, pool and lock (grep for `thread_local!`,
`static`, `Cell<`, atomics, `Mutex`, `bounded_wait`, `unbounded_wait`, `change_timeout`,
`deadline`, `timeout` in `src/`, `shims/`, `demo_store/src/`), then for each one asked whether
it is held across an `await` on another party and what ends that wait. Evidence: CP = the
code path settles it. Nothing was built or run: the only candidate needs a target that does
not reply, which only the Live phase may deploy, and `IcBridge` cannot run natively
(register #58).

##### Cells

| Row | Item | Cell | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| V1 / LIM12 / E5a | `ACTIVE_RUNS` run slots (8, process-wide) with `call_timeout_seconds` **set** | **finding (CP), candidate 1** | `RunSlot` is held until `run_script` returns (`src/lib.rs:218-262`). The only run-level deadline is the instruction deadline (`src/bridge.rs:25-38`), and instructions do not advance while a call waits. `call_timeout_seconds` is applied per call (`src/bridge.rs:524-527`). So with the timeout configured, a run still holds its slot for up to (number of sequential host round-trips) x timeout: at defaults (25-call cap, IC cap 300 s) 24 sequential calls x 300 s plus the fetch, about 2 h per run; with a raised `max_calls_per_script` it grows to JS 64 rounds (`js.rs:26, 374`), Rhai 64 requests (`rhai_rt.rs:23, 211`) or Python 256 suspensions (`python.rs`), i.e. up to about 21 h. Slots are not shared per caller (the caller hash is computed but never used for slot accounting, `lib.rs:221`), so one token holder who keeps 8 such runs in flight and resubmits as each ends keeps every other caller "busy" indefinitely, with the documented remedy enabled |
| V1 / LIM3 (timeout unset) | Same, default unbounded wait | not re-reported | Known finding |
| V1 / E5b | Searches and the run slot | not re-reported | Known (searches take no slot) |
| V2 / V4 / K5 / O2 | DID cache / DID_FAILED around the interface fetch | holds for this pattern (CP) | Not a slot count: nothing is reserved while the fetch waits; a waiter blocks nobody else (no single-flight, known). Both fetch messages are `bounded_wait` (`bridge.rs:426, 434`), so the wait has the default 300 s deadline. DID_FAILED's 5-minute block is known |
| V3 | `PENDING_RUNS` | n/a | Uncapped set used for reporting; it refuses nothing, so it cannot starve callers |
| V5 | Parsed-override cache | n/a | No wait, no cap |
| V6 | Python `LIVE_MEMORY` / `BASELINE_MEMORY` | holds for this pattern (CP) | Process-wide counter, but `rebased` (`python.rs:151-157`) re-bases around every await, so one run's suspended heap is not charged to another run's 64 MiB limit; total heap held by suspended runs is the known memory finding |
| V7 | getrandom `STATE` | n/a | Not a cap, no wait |
| V8 / V9 / V10 | Boa GC heap, ic-cdk executor, engine statics | not re-reported | Heap held by suspended runs is known (Boa GC heap; `wasm_memory_limit` after an await); no count-type slot exists in them |
| `python.rs:168` `LOCK: Mutex<()>` held across awaits | test-only serialisation lock | n/a | Under `#[cfg(test)]` (`python.rs:162-193`); not in the shipped Wasm |
| E5 batch loop (`mcp.rs:386-404`) | sequential tool calls within one HTTP request | holds (CP) | The slot is taken inside `run_script` and dropped when it returns, not held for the rest of the batch; searches after a script in the same batch do not hold it, and a script after searches takes it only when it starts |
| LIM9 / LIM10 / LIM8 | per-request caps (5 searches, 1 script, 50 messages) | n/a | Per request, not process-wide; they reserve nothing across a wait |
| LIM25 / LIM26 / LIM27 | JS `MAX_PENDING`/`MAX_ROUNDS`, Python suspensions, Rhai `MAX_REQUESTS` | n/a for starvation | Per run; they shape candidate 1's maximum hold time only |
| LIM1 / LIM2 / O1 | call cap and instruction budget | n/a | Per run; reserved per run in `IcBridge`, not shared across callers |
| LIM30 platform: per-destination reservation (queue capacity) and callback quotas | platform slot held by each outstanding call | unverified, not a candidate | At defaults script calls in flight are at most 8 x 25 = 200, below the platform per-destination capacity; reaching it needs a raised `max_calls_per_script` (config) or many concurrent searches whose fallback fetches go to one silent target (bounded at 300 s). Not reproducible without deploying a silent target (Live phase); recorded as unverified |
| VF1 / VF5 | cycles held by waits | not re-reported | Response prepayment held by unbounded waits is known |
| E1 / E2 / K11 | upgrade/stop while runs wait | not re-reported | Known (stop stuck; slots lost on upgrade with heap) |
| E3 / E4 / E6-E14 | ingress filter, query path, admin endpoints | n/a | No awaits; nothing held across a wait |
| K1-K10 | commit points | n/a beyond V1 | The only resource held across K2-K5 that other callers compete for is the run slot (candidate 1) and heap (known) |
| C2 / E20-E25 / D8 / V11 | demo_store | n/a | No awaits, no caps |
| D1-D7 | durable state | n/a | Written synchronously; no reservation held across a wait |

| A1-A12 / U1-U16 / W1-W16 / F1-F16 / B1-B16 / AD1-AD9 / CL1-CL37 / T1-T12 | remaining rows | n/a except as noted | None holds a process-wide count across an outbound await; claims touched by candidate 1: CL9 ("At most 8 scripts run at once"), README:416-418 and :430-433 (timeout presented as the remedy for waits that never end); T1 tests the cap but not hold time |

##### Candidates

1. **With `call_timeout_seconds` set, a run still holds its slot for up to (round-trips x
   timeout), about 2 h at defaults, and slots have no per-caller share, so one token holder
   keeps every other script "busy" indefinitely with the documented remedy on.** L4/L9,
   Medium, CP. `src/lib.rs:198-221` (process-wide `ACTIVE_RUNS`, no per-caller accounting),
   `src/bridge.rs:25-38` (only an instruction deadline), `src/bridge.rs:524-527` (per-call

<a id="grid-sweep-r3-0"></a>

### grid-sweep-r3-0

#### Variant sweep r3-0: cost per accepted request, record per message or run

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 3. Pattern under test (from confirmed L5-1):

> Cost is incurred per accepted request but recorded per outbound message or tool run, so
> paid work that sends nothing leaves no trace (a record keyed to a different unit than the
> cost).

Method: code reading at `295d64b` plus the ic-cdk 0.20.3 call future
(`ic-cdk-0.20.3/src/call.rs:896-940`, `get_cost` at 323, liquid-balance check at 753). No
build, no live request; nothing deployed or changed. For each inventory row the question was:
does this row incur a cost (update execution, ingress bytes, outbound message, slot, shared
state change) whose record is written only when some *other* unit (a sent message, a policy
refusal, a tool run) occurs?

Known and not re-reported: L5-1 (authenticated update requests that run no tool; cached
searches in the update path incl. `certified_reads`), L5-2 / L2-6 (searches refused by a
remembered fetch failure), L5-3 (tokenless canister callers), L5-5 (demo_store), register
#11 (trap before first send), busy refusals (documented, CL19), upgrades leave no trace,
DID_FAILED caching transient/self-caused send failures, Trapped-entry undercounts.

##### Grid

| Row(s) | Result | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| E1/E2 init, post_upgrade | n/a | Controller-initiated install; no per-request cost from other actors. "Upgrades leave no audit trace" is known |
| E3 inspect_message | holds | Runs at no charge; refuses tokenless ingress before cost |
| E4/E4a/E4b query path | holds | Queries are free to the canister on mainnet; `upgrade` only after `authenticate` |
| E5 http_request_update (non-tool messages, parse errors, revoked-token race, 1.9 MB padding around a tool call) | known (L5-1) | Paid per accepted request; entries exist only for tool runs. The non-tool part of a tool request (body parse, reply re-serialisation at `mcp.rs:405`, `finish`) is outside the entry's `instructions` window (`IcBridge::new` .. closing entry); the ingress byte fee is recorded nowhere. Same root as L5-1; the entry itself exists, so no new trace gap |
| E5a run_script | holds | `append_audit` at `lib.rs:246` is unconditional after `RunSlot::take`; a run that sends nothing (policy refusal, sync send failure, script error, oversized code, unknown language reaching `execute`) still gets a closing entry. Busy refusal (`lib.rs:219-221`) is the documented exception (CL19) |
| E5b run_search, cached / DID_FAILED / certified_reads | known (L5-1, L5-2, L2-6) | Condition `bridge.calls() > 0 \|\| !violations.is_empty()` (`lib.rs:161`) |
| E5b run_search, fetch passes policy, send refused by the system | **candidate SW3-0-1** | `reserve` takes a slot (`bridge.rs:486`), both `self.sent(...)` futures resolve `Ready(Err)` on first poll (`InsufficientLiquidCycleBalance` or `CallPerformFailed`), so `record_message` never runs and `calls()` stays 0; the error does not start with `policy:` so it goes to `fetch_errors`, not `violations`; `lib.rs:161` skips the entry. ##### Candidate

###### SW3-0-1 A search whose interface fetch is refused at send writes no audit entry but caches the failure for every caller (Low, code path)

- Where: `src/lib.rs:159-187` (condition at 161), `src/bridge.rs:424-437, 483-506`;
  ic-cdk 0.20.3 `CallFuture::poll` (`call.rs:899-922`).
- Path: a search reaches an uncached, unfailed, allowlisted canister. `reserve` passes and
  takes a call-cap slot. `fetch_did` builds `canister_metadata`; on first poll ic-cdk
  returns `Ready(Err(InsufficientLiquidCycleBalance))` when the liquid balance is below
  `cost_call` (which includes the max-response prepayment), or `Ready(Err(CallPerformFailed))`
  when `call_perform` refuses (queue full, out of cycles). `on_first_pending` never fires,
  so no `Started` entry; the fallback `__get_candid_interface_tmp_hack` fails the same way.
  `candid()` writes `DID_FAILED[key]` and returns an error without the `policy:` prefix, so
  it lands in `fetch_errors`. `calls() == 0` and `violations` is empty, so no closing entry.
- Outcome: for 5 minutes every script and search touching that canister, from any caller,
  gets "could not fetch candid for X (...)", and the audit log holds nothing that shows which
  request caused it or when. A script hitting the same refusal does get a closing `Error`
  entry (`lib.rs:246`), so the two tools disagree. README:405 says a search that could not
  fetch closes with `Error`; README:411-412 does not list this case.
- Reachability: needs the canister's liquid balance under the call cost or a full output
  queue. The known finding "Cycles reserved by in-flight calls and fetches have no global
  cap" shows a token holder can push the canister into that band.
- Refutation tried: (1) does `reserve` record the slot anywhere durable? No, `slots` is a
  `Cell` on the bridge. (2) Does the error reach `violations`? Only `policy:` errors are
  routed there (`lib.rs:139`), and `deny` is called only from `reserve` and the budget check.
  (3) Is `fetch_errors` enough to force an entry? No, it only selects the status inside the
  `if`. Not reproduced: needs a low-cycles canister (a settings change outside this phase)
  and `IcBridge` has no native harness (register #58).
- Root: the same condition as L2-6 (entry keyed to messages sent or policy refusals, not to
  attempts); the new part is that this outcome mutates shared state. A verifier may merge it
  into L2-6 as a further symptom.
- Fix: write the search's closing entry whenever a slot was taken (`slots > 0`) or a
  fetch error occurred, as `run_script` does unconditionally; or simply always write it in
  the update path.

<a id="grid-sweep-r3-1"></a>

### grid-sweep-r3-1

#### Variant sweep r3-1

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 3. Pattern (seed, known, not re-reported: the
query-path search ignores `DID_FAILED`, upgrades, and the update path then sends nothing and
writes no entry):

**"Two equivalent paths (query and update) judge the same state differently. One escalates
to paid work, and the other then does nothing and records nothing."**

Question asked of every inventory row: is there a pair of paths that should reach the same
verdict on the same state (query `http_request` vs `http_request_update`, `inspect_message`
vs the method, `search_cached` vs `run_search`, `IcBridge::candid` vs `IcBridge::service`,
script vs search), where the cheap/first path ignores or misjudges some state, escalates
(upgrade to a paid update, a call-cap slot, a fetch), and the second path, honouring that
state, refuses or no-ops without an audit entry?

Evidence: reading the code at `295d64b` (`src/mcp.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/search.rs`,
`src/bridge.rs`, `src/policy.rs`, `src/candid_bridge.rs`, `src/runtimes/mod.rs`). Nothing
compiled, deployed or sent: every hit below is unambiguous from the code path. C = code path.

##### New candidates

| Id | Sev | Title | Ev |
|---|---|---|---|
| SW3-1-1 | Low (may merge with L5-1 / L5-2) | The query path upgrades every `execute_icp_script` without looking at `ACTIVE_RUNS`; when 8 scripts are running, the paid update then answers "busy ... retry shortly" and writes no audit entry. The query could have refused it for free, and the error text invites the client/AI to retry, each retry another paid, unaudited update | C |

###### SW3-1-1 (busy refusal is judged only after a paid upgrade)

- Query: `http_query` (`src/mcp.rs:366`) returns `HttpResponse::upgrade()` for any
  `ToolRequest::Execute`, consulting no state. `ACTIVE_RUNS` is a heap `thread_local`
  (`src/lib.rs:200`) that a query can read (`get_policy`, a query, already reads it at
  `src/lib.rs:341`).
- Update: the gateway sends `http_request_update`; `inspect_message` lets it in (valid token,
  `src/lib.rs:276-277`), so the canister pays induction and execution. `run_script`
  (`src/lib.rs:219-221`) finds `RunSlot::take()` is `None` and returns
  `busy: 8 scripts are already running; retry shortly` before creating an `IcBridge`; no
  `append_audit` runs on this branch.
- Scenario: a token holder keeps 8 runs in flight (any long or unbounded-wait script; the
  slot pinning itself is known). Every other `execute_icp_script` from any client is then
  upgraded, paid by the canister (cost class measured in L5-1: a few M cycles for a small
  body, up to ~4B for a 1.9 MB body, which `parse_body` accepts before the tool runs), and
  answered "busy" with no record. The message tells the AI model to "retry shortly", so an
  agent loop multiplies the paid, unrecorded updates.
- Same shape as the seed: query ignores state the update honours (`DID_FAILED` there,
  `ACTIVE_RUNS` here); update no-ops and records nothing. The "no entry" part is documented
  (README:411-412); the escalation is not, and the cost lands on the canister.
- Refute attempts: (1) Could the query not know? It reads the same committed heap; a run
  started after the query's state would only make the query optimistic, never wrongly
  pessimistic beyond a race. (2) Is it covered by L5-1? L5-1 is "authenticated update
  requests that run no tool" (ping/initialize/invalid bodies, mostly direct ingress); this one
  is the normal gateway flow for the main tool, and a tool call is made. Listed as a possible
  merge. (3) Is it free on the IC? No: upgraded calls are ordinary ingress updates paid by the
  receiving canister.
- Fix direction: in `http_query`, answer the `Execute` with the same busy tool result when
  `ACTIVE_RUNS >= MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS` (non-authoritative pre-check; the update keeps its own
  check), or record busy refusals.

<a id="grid-sweep-r3-2"></a>

### grid-sweep-r3-2

#### Variant sweep r3-2: limit checked after the work; limit on one dimension only

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 3. Pattern (seed, known, not re-reported: search
keyword count and length are unbounded while request bytes are capped by the platform):

> A limit checked after the work it is meant to prevent, and a limit on one dimension only:
> request bytes are capped by the platform, but the count derived from them is not.

Generalised for the sweep: (a) a check whose outcome does not depend on the work, placed
after that work; (b) an app limit on one dimension (bytes, elements, text units) that feeds a
platform or dependency limit on another dimension (encoded bytes, bindings, messages), with
nothing comparing the two before the work or the send.

Method: code reading at `295d64b`, plus live probes on the local network (port 8010) using
only `execute_icp_script` against allowlisted demo_store **queries** (`get_product`,
`search_products`) and scripts that call nothing; audit entries read with the controller
query `get_audit_logs`. Nothing was deployed, upgraded or reconfigured; no setting changed.
The bearer token was read from `.env` inside a helper script and never printed. Nothing was
compiled. Probe bodies lived in a private temp dir, deleted afterwards. R = reproduced live,
C = code path.

##### SW3-2-1 Call arguments are never checked against the inter-canister payload limit: a JS argument within the value limits traps the canister

- Lens L3/L9 (also L5 clean failure). Invariant 5 (clean failure), 3 (records).
- Where: `src/bridge.rs:514-528` (`encode_args` then `Call::...with_raw_args(&enc.bytes)`;
  no size check). Value limit `MAX_VALUE_BYTES` 4 MiB (`src/bridge.rs:48`), counted in
  UTF-16 units by JS.
- R1 (warm-up `get_product`, then): `let s='一'.repeat(1000); while (s.length*2 <= 4100000)
  s = s + s; await icp.call(demo_store,'search_products',[s])` (4,096,000 units, 12,288,000
  UTF-8 bytes). HTTP 503, gateway details: `Canister violated contract: Request to
  4fbx2-...:search_products has a payload size of 12288026, which exceeds the allowed limit of
  10485760`. Audit: `Started` 9855 for `get_product`, then `Trapped` 9856 "instruction or
  memory limit, or a bug".
- R2 same string as the first message, inside `try { ... } catch`: same 503; the catch does
  not run; `get_audit_log_len` unchanged (9,857 before and after): the run is not audited.
- R3 1,024,000 units (3,072,000 bytes) is sent and answered (`found: 0`): the local subnet
  takes up to 10 MiB. Cross-subnet (mainnet, 2 MiB) the same 2-4 MiB argument would fail in
  `call_perform` with an opaque error after the slot and the encode (not reproducible on the
  single-subnet local network; unverified).
- Scope: JS reaches it directly with text (3 bytes per UTF-16 unit). Python and Rhai text is
  held to 4 MiB of UTF-8, so they reach 10 MiB only through type expansion (each missing
  `opt` field encodes a byte), which needs a wide allowlisted interface (code path, not
  reproduced).

##### SW3-2-2 Rhai compiles before any budget check, and its 1,000-variable limit applies only at run time: a 100 KiB script spends 35.8 B instructions in compile

- Lens L3. Invariant 4 (bounded cost), 10 (budget documented as checked on every Rhai operation).
- Where: `src/runtimes/rhai_rt.rs:196` (`engine.compile(code)` before the replay loop;
  `on_progress` is the only budget check), `set_max_variables(1_000)` at `:130`.
- R: `if false{ let q; let z; ... }0` with N distinct names inside a block that never runs:
  N=250 25 M, 500 72 M, 1,000 249 M, 2,000 0.90 B, 4,000 3.55 B, 5,000 5.58 B (quadratic);
  10,233 `let qab=0;` 22.8 B; 12,792 `let qab;` 35.4 B; 12,944 densest names 35.8 B (102,393
  bytes, under `MAX_CODE_BYTES`). Each run reported `policy: instruction budget exceeded
  (35786363838 > 20000000000)` after the fact (audit id 9883). Executing the same `let`s
  stops at "Too many variables defined (line 1001)" only after compile (id 9860, 7.5 B).
  Shadowing one name is linear (12,700 lets 0.19 B), so the cost is the count of distinct
  bindings, which neither the 100 KiB byte cap nor `max_variables` bounds before compile.
- 35.8 B is 89% of the 40 B message limit; no trap was reached at default limits.
- Sibling of the known Boa compile finding (SW2-0-2); r2-0 measured Rhai statements and
  functions as linear but did not try distinct variable names.

##### SW3-2-3 composite_query refusal comes after the call-cap slot, a possible interface fetch and full argument encoding

- Lens L3/L4. C only (demo_store has no composite_query).
- `call()` runs `reserve` (slot), `service()` (on a miss: second slot, up to two messages),
  `encode_args` (cost known to reach the budget for wide types), then refuses on
  `FuncMode::CompositeQuery`, a fact known from the interface alone. Refusal is an `Error`,
  not a recorded violation.

##### Not tested

- Cross-subnet behaviour of 2-10 MiB arguments (single-subnet local network).
- Heap high-water from JS calls holding 4 MiB+ args (`args_json`, the parsed `Value` and
  `enc.bytes`) across awaits, x 25 calls x 8 runs: not probed live because Wasm memory never
  shrinks and the known wasm_memory_limit finding shows that growth blocks later updates.
- Whether a denser Rhai shape (other binding kinds) passes 40 B in compile.

### grid-sweep-r3-3

#### Variant sweep r3-3: a filter on one entry path, claimed for every path

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 3. Pattern (seed, known, not re-reported: L5-3,
the canister-caller variant of register #30, "Canisters without a token make icp_code_mode
pay for every call; the unpaid-call filter covers ingress only"):

> A filter enforced on one entry path and claimed for every path.

Question asked of every inventory row: is there a filter here (authentication, cost filter,
allowlist, cap, budget, size check, sandbox removal, canonicalisation, switch-off) that is
installed on one way in, while a sentence in the README, the `.did`, a code comment or a text
shown to the AI says it holds for all of them? Ways in considered: ingress through the
gateway (query, then upgraded update), direct ingress, inter-canister callers (update and
replicated query), self-calls, the cleanup callback, `init` / `post_upgrade` vs the admin
endpoints, the three runtimes and each SDK function, `icp.candid` vs `icp.call` vs search,
the two interface-fetch transports, the two demo-page request helpers, and the build paths
(default vs per-language worker).

Method: code reading at `295d64b` (`src/*.rs`, `src/runtimes/*.rs`, `src/demo.html`,
`demo_store/src/lib.rs`, both `.did` files, `icp.yaml`, `README.md:98-125, 360-500`), every
absolute comment in `src/` (`grep -i "every|always|never|cannot|only|all "`), and the Boa
0.22 / Monty 1.6 sources for the sandbox removals (`boa_engine-0.22.0/src/context/hooks.rs`,
`builtins/date/mod.rs`, `monty-types-1.6.0/src/os_policy.rs`, `monty-1.6.0/src/modules/time.rs`).
Nothing compiled, nothing run against the live network. Round-1 sweep r1-4 ("guardrail on one
path, resource open on another") and round-2 sweep r2-9 ("per-request limit in one of two
sibling handlers") already covered most rows from the guardrail side; this sweep starts from
the claims and re-checks the rows they did not name.

Evidence key: **CP** = the code path settles it; **known** = a listed finding already covers
it (named); **holds** = every path applies the filter, or no claim extends it.

##### Result

**No new candidate.** Every claimed-universal filter either runs on every way in, or its gap
is already a known finding.

### grid-sweep-r3-4

#### Variant sweep r3-4: unauthenticated, unbounded writes

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 3. Pattern (from the confirmed demo_store
findings, not re-reported):

> Unauthenticated writes with no per-item or total bound, so storage and reply size grow
> with cheap anonymous requests.

Method: code reading at `295d64b` (nothing compiled or run, no live instance touched). Every
inventory row was asked: (a) can a caller with no credential (A1, A2, A8, A10) cause a write
that outlives the request, (b) is that write bounded per item and in total, (c) does any
reply or iteration grow with it. Round 2 swept the broader "cheap or unauthenticated
growth" pattern in `grid-sweep-r2-6.md`; this round re-checked its load-bearing cells
independently instead of trusting them, and looked for anonymous paths that sweep did not
name (canister-to-canister callers, demo_store reply echoes, query-path side effects).

Evidence key: **CP** = the code path makes it unambiguous; **ref** = cell taken from the
cited grid after re-reading the code it names.

Result: **no new candidate.** The only anonymous write path in the repository is demo_store
`create_order` / `cancel_order` / `restock`, and its growth (`orders`) is the known finding.
icp_code_mode takes no write before `authenticate`.

<a id="grid-sweep-r3-5"></a>

### grid-sweep-r3-5

#### Variant sweep r3-5: per-item check against batch-changed state, plus unchecked counter arithmetic

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 3. Pattern (seed: demo_store oversells because
duplicate lines in one order are each checked against the same stock, and `reserved +=`
wraps in the release Wasm; both known, not re-reported):

> A check made per item against state that the batch itself changes, combined with
> unchecked arithmetic on a counter.

Searched in its two halves and their combination: (a) a loop or batch that validates each
item against a shared quantity (stock, slots, budget, bytes, count) that earlier items of the
same batch consume, without the batch's own consumption being counted; (b) `+`, `+=`, `-`,
`*` on a counter in non-test code where the release profile (overflow checks off) wraps
instead of trapping; (c) a consumer of such a counter that reports the wrapped value.

Method: `grep -n "+= \|+ 1\|-= \|saturating\|checked_\|wrapping\|MAX_"` over `src/`,
`src/runtimes/`, `demo_store/src/`, `shims/`, then reading every hit and every loop that
checks a limit per item. One native reproduction (R) in a private copy of the tree with the
shared target dir: `cargo test -p demo_store --release --lib` (release profile = the shipped
overflow semantics). The copy's only source change besides the added test was
`created_at: ic_cdk::api::time()` -> `0` in `create_order` (ic0 is unavailable natively).
The copy was deleted afterwards. No running instance was contacted.

C = code path, R = reproduced.

##### New candidates

###### SW3-5-1 demo_store `sales_summary` wraps its u64 revenue sum after an oversell (Low)

- Where: `demo_store/src/lib.rs:246-257` (`revenue += line`, `e.2 += line`, u64), release
  profile without overflow checks (`Cargo.toml:44-49`).
- Scenario (R): `restock(p, 4294967295)` for products 11, 10, 1, 2, 9, then one
  `create_order` per product with 160,000 identical lines, each asking for the full
  available quantity (~4,294,967,29x); every order is accepted (the seed oversell). Exact
  revenue 19,378,892,426,896,652,550; `sales_summary().revenue_cents` = 932,148,353,187,100,934.
  Each order's own `total_cents` is correct. Wrong data returned as if right.
- Root cause: same class as the known release-profile finding (overflow checks off, the
  sum is `u64` while the output type is `Nat`); reachable only through the known oversell.
  Proposed handling: merge into the release-profile overflow finding as another site.
- Fix: accumulate in `u128` or `Nat` (the reply type is already `Nat`), and fix the oversell
  by summing quantities per product before the check.

###### SW3-5-2 Per-tool-call instruction budgets share one 40e9 message execution (Medium)

- Where: `src/mcp.rs:386-404` (items run in sequence), `src/lib.rs:121-154` (search checks
  its own budget only after render), `src/bridge.rs:318, 351-354` (each `IcBridge` measures
  from its own start), `src/runtimes/rhai_rt.rs:143-152` (Rhai stops at its own deadline).
- Scenario (C): one HTTP request with up to five `search_icp_canisters` calls answered from
  cache and one `execute_icp_script`. None of them awaits, so all run in one message
  execution. Each item is checked against `max_instructions` (20e9) from its own start; the
  sum is never checked against the 40e9 per-message limit. A Rhai script that loops to its
  20e9 stop, plus searches whose renders together exceed 20e9 while each stays under 20e9,
  traps the message: the client gets a gateway error instead of the script's clean
  "instruction budget exceeded", and nothing is recorded. When the script ran earlier in the
  request after awaits, the trap lands in its last callback (the known batch-trap record
  consequence). Reachability: search render costs about 240 instructions per keyword x
  allowed method (L3-7: 2.4e9 for 1M keywords x 10 methods), and the HTTP body caps the
  keywords for the whole request at about 1M, so the searches' sum exceeds 20e9 once about
  85 methods are allowed. That is far more than the test deployment's 8, but realistic for a
  deployment that allowlists a ledger, index and governance with `"*"`. Splitting the keywords
  over five searches gets past each search's own check, which refuses the same work done as
  one search.
- Distinct from the known "search rendering cost is not bounded by max_instructions": if each
  search were stopped at its own budget, five searches and a script could still use
  6 x 20e9 in one execution.
- Fix: measure one budget per HTTP request (base taken in `http_update`), or give later items
  only what is left of the message's headroom, and check search render cost while it runs.

<a id="grid-sweep-r3-6"></a>

### grid-sweep-r3-6

#### Variant sweep r3-6: in-engine limits that are per frame, per turn or per item

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 3. Pattern (seed, known, not re-reported: JS checks
the instruction budget only between host round-trips, and Boa's 1M loop limit is per call
frame):

> A limit enforced inside the engine in sibling runtimes (Rhai `on_progress`, Monty clock)
> but only at host boundaries in this one. A per-frame or per-item counter that multiplies
> with call depth or iteration count.

Question asked of every inventory row: does a counter or cap here reset per frame, per turn,
per replay, per round, per value or per item, so that the real total is that cap times a
count the caller controls; and is any budget enforced only at a boundary in one variant while
its siblings enforce it inside the engine?

Evidence: **R** = reproduced, **C** = code path. One native probe was built in a private copy
(no `target/`, `.icp/`, `design/`, `video/`, `.env`, `docs/per-customer-canisters-plan.md`)
with the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`; the copy was deleted afterwards. No live canister was
touched.

##### Candidate

**SW3-6-1 (Medium).** Python's `MAX_TURN_INSTRUCTIONS` cap is per turn, not per message, so
with `max_instructions` above about 40e9 Python reaches the IC's 40B trap as JS and Rhai do.
L14-2 says Python is unaffected.

- `src/runtimes/python.rs:29-31`: "Longest single stretch between suspensions ... below the
  IC's 40B limit per message, whatever the policy budget is". `python.rs:223-224`:
  `max_feed_duration(budget)`, `max_turn_duration(budget.min(30e9))`, where
  `budget = deadline - now`. With the default 20e9 the turn cap equals the feed cap and has no
  effect. It only matters when `max_instructions` > 30e9, the case it was written for.
- Monty resets the turn clock at every host resume (`monty-types-1.6.0/src/resource.rs:110-113,
  757-763`; `monty-1.6.0/src/repl.rs:1368-1375`). Turns are not message executions. The driver
  answers `icp.principal()` (`python.rs:133`), `import icp` (OsCall, `:266-270`), name lookups
  (`:265`), a policy-refused `icp.call` (`reserve` errors before any await) and a cached
  `icp.candid` without awaiting. So `rebased(host(..)).await` completes on its first poll and
  the next turn runs in the same IC message execution. Up to 256 turns chain this way, and
  each may use the full 30e9.
- R (native probe, Monty 1.6.0 driven like `python.rs`, wall clock): one 2M-iteration loop
  took 354 ms. With turn cap = 532 ms (1.5x) and a large feed cap, three such loops with no
  host call failed with `TimeoutError: turn time limit exceeded`. Six loops separated by
  `icp.principal()`, each answered synchronously in the same poll, finished `Ok` in 2.14 s:
  4.0x the turn cap, 7 turns, all inside one synchronous drive.
- C (on wasm): with `max_instructions = 60e9` (accepted unvalidated, L14-2), the script
  `import icp` / 29e9-instruction loop / `icp.principal()` / 29e9-instruction loop exceeds
  40e9 in one execution. That traps the canister. No message was sent, so there is no audit
  entry (K8).
- Fix: cap the turn at what is left of the current message, not per turn. Either have the
  driver call `budget_error` against `min(deadline, message_start + 30e9)` and force an
  `await` (yield) between turns, or validate `max_instructions` <= ~30e9 in `set_limits` /
  `apply` (L14-2's fix). Also fix the `MAX_TURN_INSTRUCTIONS` comment and L14-2's "Python
  unaffected".
- Regression test: needs the instruction-counter seam (register #58). Natively, a test can
  assert that a Python run with turn cap T and k synchronous host answers stops at T in
  total, not at k x T.

<a id="grid-sweep-r3-7"></a>

### grid-sweep-r3-7

#### Variant sweep r3-7: budget checked between interpreter steps, not inside one native operation

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 3. Pattern under test:

> A budget enforced between interpreter steps but not inside one uninterruptible native
> operation inside a dependency.

"Budget" covers every per-run limit the app relies on: the policy instruction budget
(`max_instructions`), engine step limits (Rhai operations, Boa loop limit, Monty VM budget),
and engine size limits (Rhai string/array/map size, Monty 64 MiB). The question for each row:
is there a single call into a dependency, reachable from script input or a target's reply,
whose cost or allocation is decided before the next check runs?

Known and not repeated (from the task's list): Boa built-ins and sync JS (register #23 and the
reported Boa items: repeat/pad/join capacity overflow, sort, `String.at`, compile quadratic,
parser depth, `Symbol.for`, console formatting), every Monty native operation in grid-L3-r3
(`**`, gcd/lcm, isqrt, `*`, `//`, 3-arg pow, decimal sqrt, regex, NFKC, zfill, replace, hex,
list search), Monty `eval`/`exec` compile, `json.dumps(indent)`, `re.compile`, Python
`to_json`/`py_repr`, candid_parser, `json_to_idl`, candid encode depth^2 and `from_radix`,
candid decode gamma clone, search rendering, Rhai sort/sleep/size-limit gaps.

##### How it was tested

- **Native.** Private copy of the tree at
  `/private/tmp/claude-501/sweep-r3-7.LvFO/repo` (no `target/`, no `design/`), build dir
  `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/audit-target`, release profile, one feature at a
  time. Throwaway examples (not in the repository): `examples/sweep_r3_7.rs` (Rhai engine
  configured exactly as `rhai_rt::build_engine`), `sweep_r3_7_js.rs` (Boa `JsValue::from_json`),
  `sweep_r3_7_py.rs` (Monty `MontyRun::new` compile), `sweep_r3_7_nat.rs`
  (`candid_bridge::Service::decode_reply` on large LEB128 `nat` replies).
- **Live.** The project's local network (port 8010), canister `icp_code_mode`
  (`4caro-hl777-77775-aaaba-cai`), default limits, nothing deployed or changed. Each probe is
  one `execute_icp_script`; the cost is the `instructions` field of its audit entry, matched by
  `script_sha256`. Helper `scratchpad/r37/probe.py` (token read from `.env`, never printed).
  Traps happen before any outbound message, so they roll back and write no entry
  (register #11). Canister memory after the probes: 380,391,208 bytes, status Running.

##### Results

###### Rhai compile (`engine.compile` in `rhai_rt::run`, `src/runtimes/rhai_rt.rs:187`)

Runs once per run, before the first `on_progress` callback. Native cost of 102 KB sources
(under `MAX_CODE_BYTES` = 102,400):

| Source shape | Optimizer on (as shipped) | `OptimizationLevel::None` | Cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| `let a = 1;{}{}{}...` (empty blocks) | 0.11 s / 0.45 s / 1.76 s / 7.45 s at 12.5 / 25 / 50 / 102 KB | 6.8 ms at 102 KB | optimizer: pure statements removed one at a time with `Vec::remove(index)` (`rhai optimizer.rs:245-268`) |
| `x;x;x;...` / `1;1;1;...` | 0.31 s at 102 KB | 12 ms | same loop |
| `let f = \|\| { b0;b1;...;bN }; 1` (distinct captured names) | 1.69 s at 102 KB | 1.74 s | parser: each new name scans `external_vars` (`rhai parser.rs:548-549`) |
| `let v0=1;let v1=1;...` | 0.43 s | 0.46 s | parser variable stack |

Live (wasm, audit `instructions`; no outbound call, so this is compile plus a trivial run):

| Script | Bytes | Instructions | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| empty blocks | 12,500 | 2,805,398,460 (entry 9878) | Ok |
| empty blocks | 25,000 | 11,111,435,992 (9879) | Ok |
| empty blocks | 37,000 | 24,267,157,933 (9880) | `policy: instruction budget exceeded (24267157933 > 20000000000)`, reported after the fact |
| empty blocks | 60,000 | | HTTP 503 `Canister exceeded the limit of 40000000000 instructions for single message execution`, no entry |
| closure with captured names | 50,000 | 27,905,427,073 (9881) | budget exceeded, after the fact |
| closure with captured names | 100,028 | | HTTP 503, 40e9 limit, no entry |
| `let v0=1;...` | 102,000 | 16,407,038,034 (9882) | `Too many variables defined` raised at run time, after compile was paid |

Cost is quadratic: twice the source, about 4x the instructions (2.81e9 to 11.1e9).

###### Rhai `parse_json` (`rhai packages/lang_core.rs:180-186` -> `Engine::parse_json`, `api/json.rs:68-131`)

A script-callable native function that runs the Rhai parser on a runtime string of up to
1 MiB (the string limit), with closures allowed, in one call. Same parser cost as above, but
the source is built at run time, so it is not bounded by `MAX_CODE_BYTES`:

| Script (9 lines, builds `[|| [[b0,b1,...]]]` in a loop) | Text | Rhai operations | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4,000 names | 22,900 B | ~24k | 5,997,200,229 instructions (entry 9896), error `Variable not found: b0` |
| 12,000 names | ~75 KB | ~72k | HTTP 503, 40e9 limit, no entry |
| 30,000 names | ~200 KB | ~180k | HTTP 503, 40e9 limit |

###### Rhai string `replace` (`rhai packages/string_more.rs:1172-1239`, four overloads)

`*string = string.replace(find, sub).into()` has no size check; the 1 MiB `max_string_size`
is applied by `check_data_size` after the native call returns (`func/call.rs`,
`func/func_call.rs`). The result can be `len(s) / len(find) * len(sub)`, up to 1 MiB x 1 MiB.

- Native (`sweep_r3_7 replace <sub>`; `s` = 1 MiB of `a`, `t` = `sub` bytes): sub 64 / 256 /
  1024 -> max RSS 171 MB / 574 MB / 2.69 GB, then `Length of string too large`.
- Live, sub 64 (64 MiB result): 1,314,442,794 instructions (entry 9884), then the size error.
- Live, sub 2048 (2 GiB result), script
  `let s = ""; s.pad(1048576, "a"); let t = ""; t.pad(2048, "b"); s.replace("a", t); s.len()`:
  HTTP 503 `Canister called ic0.trap with message: 'Panicked at 'capacity overflow',
  .../alloc/src/raw_vec/mod.rs:29:5'`, no entry. On wasm32 a `String` over `isize::MAX`
  (2 GiB) panics, so the trap does not depend on the memory limit.
- Python for comparison: `('a'*1048576).replace('a', 'b'*4096)` -> `MemoryError: memory limit
  exceeded: 4294967295 bytes > 67108864 bytes` in 0.2 s (Monty prechecks). Holds.

###### Checked and holding

##### Candidates

###### SW37-1 (High) Rhai compile and `parse_json` cost is quadratic and outside every budget

- **Where.** `src/runtimes/rhai_rt.rs:187` (`engine.compile(code)` before any `on_progress`),
  `build_engine` registers `StandardPackage`, which includes `parse_json`
  (`rhai-1.27.0/src/packages/lang_core.rs:180`). Quadratic loops: optimizer
  `optimizer.rs:245-268` (`statements.remove(index)` per pure statement), parser
  `parser.rs:548-549` (linear `external_vars` scan per captured name), parser variable stack.
- **Repro (live).** Rhai script `"let a = 1;" + "{}" * 13495` (37,000 B): `policy: instruction
  budget exceeded (24267157933 > 20000000000)`. 60,000 B: HTTP 503, 40e9 limit, no audit entry.
  `let f = || { b0;b1;...; }; 1` at 100,028 B: HTTP 503. At run time, 9 lines that build
  `[|| [[b0,...,b11999]]]` and call `parse_json`: HTTP 503 after ~72k operations.
- **Fix.** Compile with `OptimizationLevel::None` (102 KB `{}` script: 7.45 s -> 6.8 ms
  native), replace `parse_json` with a host function that parses with `serde_json` under the
  value budget, and bound the parser's remaining quadratic cases (a lower Rhai source limit or
  a pre-scan of distinct identifiers). Regression: a wasm-level test (PocketIC) that runs the
  three scripts and asserts a clean error under `max_instructions`.

###### SW37-2 (High) Rhai string `replace` builds its result before the 1 MiB size check; one call traps

- **Where.** `rhai-1.27.0/src/packages/string_more.rs:1172-1239` (four `replace` overloads,
  no size check); the engine's `check_data_size` runs only after the call returns.
- **Repro (live).** `let s = ""; s.pad(1048576, "a"); let t = ""; t.pad(2048, "b");
  s.replace("a", t); s.len()` -> HTTP 503 `Panicked at 'capacity overflow'`, no entry. With a
  64-byte `t`: 1.31e9 instructions and a 64 MiB string before `Length of string too large`.
  Native: 2.69 GB resident for a 1 KiB `t` before the same error. Python's `str.replace` with
  the same sizes raises `MemoryError` (precheck).
- **Not tested.** The same call in a replay after an outbound call (a callback, where the Wasm
  memory limit is not applied to responses per the known JS heap finding): code path only;
  not run, because it could leave the shared canister above its memory limit.
- **Fix.** Register replacement `replace` overloads (they take precedence over the package)
  that compute `matches x (sub_len - find_len) + len` with checked arithmetic and refuse above
  `max_string_size` before allocating. Regression: a native Rhai test asserting the size error
  for 1 MiB x 2 KiB, plus a counting-allocator assertion that peak allocation stays near 2 MiB.

##### Not tested

- Every Rhai parser shape. Four were measured; the fix above (optimizer off) removes the
  worst, the parser cases remain.
- JS `String.prototype.replaceAll` blow-up: Boa capacity-overflow family, already reported.
- Exact native-to-wasm instruction ratio (about 25e9 instructions per native second for the
  Rhai optimizer, from 12.5 KB: 0.11 s vs 2.81e9).
- Mainnet cycle cost of each 40e9 trap.

<a id="grid-sweep-r3-8"></a>

### grid-sweep-r3-8

#### Variant sweep r3-8: one limit, measured in different units by sibling implementations

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 3. Pattern:

> The same limit measured in different units by sibling implementations.

Seeds (known, not re-reported): JS counts value text in UTF-16 units while Python and Rhai
count UTF-8 bytes; Boa's 1M loop limit counts per call frame; Rhai's size limits are summed
over the whole nested value; the log cap counts line bytes and not lines; the call cap counts
slots, not messages; `DECODING_QUOTA` is scaled by 50 for untyped values; Python's clock is in
seconds while JS uses milliseconds.

Method: for every inventory row that holds or applies a limit, find each place that enforces
or depends on it and compare the unit each one counts: bytes or UTF-16 units, raw or
JSON-escaped bytes, JSON levels or Candid levels, per call frame, per replay, per Monty turn or
per IC message, slots or messages, elements or bytes. Reproductions were native
(`cargo test --lib`) in a private copy with the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. The copy was deleted
afterwards. Nothing was deployed and no live setting was changed.

Evidence keys: **R** = reproduced natively; **C** = the code path produces it unambiguously.

##### New candidates

| Id | Severity | Candidate | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| SW3-8-1 | Medium | `MAX_DEPTH` (128) counts Candid levels in `candid_bridge` and JSON levels in the runtimes. `opt` adds a Candid level but no JSON level (`json_to_idl` `src/candid_bridge.rs:231-233`, `idl_to_json` `:336`). So a recursive list (`type List = opt record { head; tail : List }`, or Motoko's `List` = `opt record { T; List }`) is refused from 65 elements (JSON depth 65), in both directions. The runtimes accept 128 levels, and README:369 promises 128. A reply is refused only after the call has run, with the misleading `reply nested deeper than 128 levels` | **R**: for n = 63 and 64, encode and decode succeed. For n = 65, 66 and 100, encode fails with `value nested too deeply` and decode fails with `reply nested deeper than 128 levels`. Same for the record list and the Motoko tuple list. JS returns a 100-node list as its result without error |
| SW3-8-2 | Medium (operator setting; merge candidate with L14-2) | The Python turn cap (`MAX_TURN_INSTRUCTIONS` 30e9, "below the IC's 40B limit per message, whatever the policy budget is", `src/runtimes/python.rs:29-31, 224`) counts per Monty turn. Monty resets the turn clock on every resume (`monty-1.6.0 run_progress.rs:444, 859`; `repl.rs:1368`). `drive` resumes without an IC await after `icp.principal()`, a `NameLookup`, an `OsCall` (`import icp`), a refused or cached request, and every queued `call_async` (`python.rs:248-273`). So one message can hold any number of turns. With `max_instructions` >= ~40e9 the feed budget no longer stops the run either, and `chunk; icp.principal(); chunk`, with each chunk 25e9, reaches the 40B trap with no audit entry. L14-2 recorded "Python unaffected (turn capped at 30e9)", and that is wrong | **R** (mechanism, wall-clock natively): turn limit 400 ms, 10 chunks of 133 ms. With no separator: `TimeoutError: turn time limit exceeded`. With `icp.principal()` or a caught `NameError` between chunks: `Ok` after 1.33 s / 1.29 s in one drive (9 synchronous host events). The on-chain trap was not run: it needs `set_limits` above 40e9, which only the Live phase may set |
| SW3-8-3 | Low | The log cap is 64 KiB of raw bytes in the runtimes (`js.rs:237`, `rhai_rt.rs:51`, Monty `io.rs:133`). `tool_result` cuts the same log text again, to 250,000 JSON-escaped bytes (`src/mcp.rs:165-166`). A control character costs 6 escaped bytes, so a log well inside the documented "Captured logs <= 64 KiB" is cut further, with `isError:false` | **R**: JS `console.log('\x01'.repeat(60000))` captures 60,000 bytes and the client gets 41,666 of them, followed by `…[truncated]` |

  resume path as `drive`.
- SW3-8-1 against a live Motoko canister that returns a `List` of 65 or more elements. The
  decode path was reproduced natively with candid's own encoder building the reply bytes.

<a id="grid-sweep-r3-9"></a>

### grid-sweep-r3-9

#### Variant sweep r3-9: a sibling runtime delegates a shared concern to its engine

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 3. Pattern (seed, known and not re-reported: Python
`print` caps through Monty's `CollectString` and raises MemoryError; Rhai refuses replies
through its engine size limits):

> A sibling runtime routes a shared concern (log cap, value limits) through its dependency's
> own mechanism instead of the shared host path, so the semantics differ.

Question asked of every row: is there a concern the host implements once (`bridge.rs`:
`ValueBudget`, `MAX_DEPTH`, `MAX_LOG_BYTES`/`LogBuf`, `budget_error`, `now_ms`,
`normalize_numbers`; `candid_bridge`; `policy`), and does one sibling (runtime, route, fetch
path, check site) hand that concern, or part of it, to a dependency's own mechanism whose
rules differ?

Evidence: **R** = reproduced, **C** = code path. One native probe was built in a private copy
(no `target/`, `.git`, `design/`, `video/`, `.env`) with the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, as a
`#[cfg(test)]` module appended to `src/runtimes/python.rs` in the copy only; the copy was
deleted afterwards. No live canister was touched.

##### Candidate

**SW3-9-1 (Medium).** Python call arguments are exported through Monty's object bridge, whose
depth guard shares the interpreter's recursion counter with the Python call stack. The
arguments of an `icp.call` made from deep recursion are cut at `200 - call depth` levels, and
every cut value, leaf strings included, becomes the text `Repr('<deeply nested>')`. Cyclic
values become `"[...]"`. The host's 128-level check only sees the cut graph, so the call is
sent with replaced data and the run is Ok. JS and Rhai send the same argument intact.

- `src/runtimes/python.rs:59-61` relies on the dependency: "Monty itself cuts exported values
  at the recursion limit and substitutes a `<deeply nested>` marker; the depth check here is
  lower, so deep data is an error instead of silently truncated." Not true when the script is
  more than about 72 frames deep.
- Monty `object_bridge.rs:182-186`: `push` takes `vm.recursion_guard()` before it looks at the
  value and on failure pushes `MontyNode::Repr("<deeply nested>")`. `bytecode/vm/recursion.rs:1-8`:
  the same counter charges "non-frozen call frames". `push_ref` turns a reference that is
  still being exported into `MontyNode::Cycle("[...]")` (`object_bridge.rs:226-236`).
- `type_name()` of these nodes is `"repr"` / `"cycle"` (`monty-types graph.rs:580`), so
  `to_json` takes the `_ => Value::String(o.py_repr())` arm (`python.rs:98`). One node and its
  repr length are charged, then the string is sent.
- R (native probe, Mock bridge records the args as sent):
  `def f(n, x): return icp.call(L, 'icrc1_balance_of', x) if n == 0 else f(n-1, x)` with
  `x = {'owner': 'aaaaa-aa', 'name': 'alice', 'deep': [[['leaf']]]}`:
  - n = 0 to 190: sent intact.
  - n = 195: `deep: [[["Repr('<deeply nested>')"]]]`. n = 197: `deep: ["Repr('<deeply nested>')"]`.
    All Ok.
  - n = 198: sent `{"Repr('<deeply nested>')": "Repr('<deeply nested>')"}`. All three keys were
    cut, collided, and only one survived. Ok.
  - `candid_bridge::Service::parse("service : { greet : (record { name : text; deep : vec vec vec text }) -> (text) }")`
    then `encode_args` of the marker strings: `Ok` (62 bytes). Text slots accept the
    replacement, so the message goes out. Slots of other types fail at encode with a
    type-mismatch error that names the marker.
  - Cycle: `a = ['x']; a.append(a); icp.call(L, m, {'owner': ..., 'path': a})` sent
    `"path": ["x", "[...]"]`, Ok. Returning `a` as the result gives `["x", "[...]"]`, Ok.
  - Same arguments, same recursion: JS `f(240, x)` and Rhai `f(30, x)` sent them intact. A JS
    cycle fails at the snapshot's 128-level check, Rhai has no cycles, and a Rhai cut never
    happens because `to_json_value` is a Rust walk.
- Related, loud: JS's snapshot is JavaScript code, so its depth also shares Boa's 256-frame
  recursion limit. At call depth 240 a 10-deep argument fails with `RuntimeLimitError:
  reached the maximum number of recursive calls`, whose stack trace shows the snapshot's own
  `put`/`walk` frames. `console.log(x)` there prints `<unprintable value>`, which is known and
  part of the README:369 finding. At depth 200 a 30-deep value passes. The message is wrong,
  but no data is replaced.
- Refuted alternatives: the result path is exported at frame depth 0 (`RunProgress::Complete`),
  so only cycles reach results, not depth cuts. Canister id and method are exported one level
  below the call's frame, so cutting them gives a loud `invalid canister id` error.
- Overlap: the last step goes through the same `_ =>` repr fallback as L7-6 (unsupported types
  become repr strings). This trigger is a supported type (list, dict, str) cut by the engine,
  and the depth at which it happens depends on the call stack. A fix that only converts known
  unsupported types (`range`, functions) would not fix it. The verifier may merge it into L7-6
  if it prefers.
- Fix: in `to_json`, treat `"repr"` nodes whose text is the marker, and every `"cycle"` node,
  as errors. Better, refuse every `repr`/`cycle` node, which is the L7-6 fix. Also export
  call arguments with a guard that does not share the call-stack counter, or check
  `depth + current frame depth`. Correct the `python.rs:59-61` comment. Regression test:
  `icp.call` from recursion depth 195 with a 4-deep argument must be an error, not a sent
  call.

<a id="grid-sweep-r3-10"></a>

### grid-sweep-r3-10

#### Variant sweep r3-10: engine limits applied to host-supplied data in one runtime only

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 3. Source finding (known, not re-reported): Rhai
applies its engine size limits (`set_max_string_size(1 << 20)`, `set_max_array_size(10_000)`,
`set_max_map_size(10_000)`, summed over the whole value) to replies the host hands it, after
the call has executed, while JS and Python bound only data the script produces.

Pattern, stated generally: **a sibling runtime applies its own engine limits to host-supplied
data, while the other runtimes bound only script-produced data.**

For each row the question is: does host-supplied data (replies, interface text, error
strings, principal, time) enter a script engine here, and does that engine apply a limit of
its own that the sibling engines do not apply to the same data?

Evidence key: **R** = reproduced here (native differential test, below); **CP** = code path
unambiguous; **known** = already reported, not re-reported.

##### Result

**No new candidate.** Every host-to-engine path was enumerated (JS `JsValue::from_json` and
`JsNativeError` messages; Python `from_json` → `MontyObject` and `MontyException` messages;
Rhai `rhai::serde::to_dynamic` and `ErrorRuntime` strings; `icp.candid` text; principal;
block time). The only engine limits that bite host data are the Rhai size limits already
reported. Engine limits that could in principle apply to host data were tested and hold:

| Probe (same mock reply, all three runtimes) | JS | Python | Rhai |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nested arrays / objects of depth 100, 120, 126, 127, 128, returned as-is | Ok | Ok | Ok |
| Same, only bound to a variable | Ok | Ok | Ok |
| Same, printed (`console.log` / `print`) | Ok | Ok | Ok |
| Same, received inside script recursion (JS/Py depth 150, Rhai 25 of 32 levels) | Ok | Ok | Ok |
| Reply string of 1.2 MB UTF-8 (600k UTF-16 units) | Ok | Ok | refused: "Length of string too large" (**known**) |
| `icp.candid` text of 500,000 bytes | Ok | Ok | Ok |
| Reply record with `__proto__` / `constructor` labels | own keys kept | kept | kept |

So Boa's recursion (256), stack-size (10,240) and loop (1M) limits are not charged by
`JsValue::from_json` or by the snapshot walk of a reply at the 128-level value depth, and
Monty's recursion limit (200) is not charged when it imports a reply, even with 150 script
frames already on the stack.

Repro: test module `src/runtimes/sweep.rs` in a private copy (a `DataBridge` whose `call`
returns a fixed JSON value and whose `candid` returns 500,000 bytes), run with
`cargo test --lib sweep -- --nocapture` against the shared target dir. The copy was deleted
afterwards.

### grid-sweep-r3-11

#### Variant sweep r3-11: build-time configuration honoured by the executor, not by the interface description

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6. Pattern under test:

> A build-time configuration honoured by the executor but not by the interface description.

Already known and not re-reported: per-language builds advertise all three languages and
`default: javascript` in `tools/list` (a Rhai-only worker fails every call that omits
`language`); `EXECUTION_BUDGET` / README:367 Python 10B (wasm32 vs native cfg); release
profile without overflow checks (demo_store `reserved`); the getrandom custom backend vs
"no randomness"; `icp.yaml` copying from a hard-coded `./target` path (breaks the README
worker recipe); no CI for feature subsets; .did/artifact drift has no guard.

Method: listed every build-time switch (`Cargo.toml [features]`, every `cfg(...)`/`cfg!` outside
tests via `grep -rn 'cfg\|feature' src demo_store/src shims`, `.cargo/config.toml` rustflags,
`[profile.release]`, dependency feature flags, `icp.yaml` build steps, `env!`), then every
surface that describes the canister to a client, an AI model or an operator (`tools/list`,
`initialize`, the input validator `parse_tool_call`/`Language::from_str`, error texts, the
demo page compiled in with `include_str!`, the `.did` and `candid:service` metadata,
`get_policy`, README), and asked for each pair whether the description follows the switch.

Evidence: R = reproduced; CP = code path. Reproduction: private copy (no `target/`), one
added `#[cfg(all(test, not(feature = "js")))]` test in `src/mcp.rs`,
`CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/audit-target cargo test --lib --no-default-features --features rhai sweep_r3_11 -- --nocapture`.
Output:

```
validator accepts uncompiled javascript: true
unknown language error: unsupported language `cobol` (expected javascript, python or rhai)
executor: Err("language `javascript` is not compiled into this canister")
demo offers js/python select: true true
demo comparison hard-codes javascript: 4
```

Copy deleted afterwards.

##### Cells

| Row | Build-time switch / surface | Cell | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|

Unknown names (`cobol`) get a free `-32602` (query path, `mcp.rs:354`), but an uncompiled one passes validation, upgrades to an update (`mcp.rs:359`), takes a run slot, sets `ran_script` (so the batch's next script is refused), and is refused only inside `LanguageRouter::execute` (`mod.rs:63-64`) with an `Error` audit entry written by `run_script` (`lib.rs:218-262`). ##### Candidates

- **SW3-11a** (R): the input validator accepts languages the build does not contain, so a
  worker refuses them only after a paid update, a run slot and an audit entry, and its
  error text lists languages it cannot run. Medium/Low (cost and misleading contract;
  likely merges with the known tools/list finding under one root cause: the `Language` set
  is not derived from the compiled features).
- **SW3-11b** (R): the demo page compiled into every build offers all three languages and
  its comparison runner is JavaScript-only, so on a Rhai- or Python-only worker it fails
  and leaves `Error` audit entries. Low/Medium (same root cause).

<a id="grid-sweep-r4-0"></a>

### grid-sweep-r4-0

#### Variant sweep r4-0: two paths answering one request from different subsets of one cache

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 4. Pattern under test:

> Two paths answering the same request from different subsets of the same cache.

Generalised for the sweep: a piece of shared state is layered (D5 overrides, V5 parsed
overrides, V2 `DID_CACHE` with TTL, V4 `DID_FAILED` with TTL, the allowlist, the limits,
heap counters, the durable log), and two paths that answer the same question (query vs
update, `icp.candid` vs `icp.call` vs search, admin view vs runtime view, Classic vs Code
Mode on the demo page) each consult a different subset of the layers, so the answers differ
for the same state.

Method: code reading at `295d64b` (working-tree changes under `src/` and `demo_store/` were
checked with `git diff 295d64b` and are test-module additions only, so non-test line numbers
match the commit). One computation: the demo page's own `classicDefsChars` code, copied
verbatim into a Node script in the scratchpad, run on `demo_store/demo_store.did` (the file
`icp.yaml` embeds as the `candid:service` metadata that `icp.candid` returns). Nothing was
built, deployed or sent.

Known and not re-reported: query search ignores `DID_FAILED`; query search skips
`MAX_SEARCHES` and the instruction budget; `icp.candid` serves overrides/cache without an
allowlist check; overrides outlive `remove_allowlist`; overrides consulted first (README says
third); eviction race; no single-flight; expired entry discarded on a failed re-fetch;
query-path override re-parse under the 5B limit; search trims `canister_id`, scripts do not;
`active_runs` excludes searches while `pending_run_ids` includes them; snapshot vs live
limits; latent override-parse divergence between `cached_service` and `IcBridge::candid`
(r3-1).

##### New candidates

| Id | Sev | Title | Ev |
|---|---|---|---|
| SW4-0-1 | Medium | Demo comparison (and README benchmark table) builds Classic tool definitions from `icp.candid` (all 10 store methods) but Code Mode's side from search (the 8 allowlisted ones). With the same 8-method surface, "What needs restocking?" flips from README's "1.2x fewer" to 0.96x (Code Mode uses more input tokens); Top 3 2.6x -> 2.38x, Tea 1.4x -> 1.31x | R (computed with the page's own code; base figure matches L16-r4's live 1,203 tok exactly) |
| SW4-0-2 | Low (may merge into the overrides findings) | `get_policy` answers "what governs this canister" from limits, allowlist and tokens only; `CANDID_OVERRIDES` (D5) has no read or list path at all, yet every serving path consults it first. A controller cannot discover a forgotten override that shadows a target's real interface (with the known stale-interface `opt` -> null effect) | C |

###### SW4-0-1 detail

- Classic side: `classicDefsChars` (`src/demo.html:401-417`) runs
  `icp.candid(S)` and makes one tool per service line: 10 tools, including `cancel_order`
  and `restock`, which `scripts/demo-setup.sh:2-3` keeps blocked "so the demo can show the
  guardrail".
- Code Mode side: `search_icp_canisters({canister_id: S})` (`src/demo.html:455`) renders
  only `e.allowed` methods (`src/search.rs:103-109`): 8 methods and their types.
- Same interface, two subsets. Computation (scratchpad `defs.mjs`, the page's regexes and
  object shape verbatim): all methods 4,810 chars (1,203 tok, matching L16-r4's live
  "10 classic tools ≈1,203 tok"); the 8 allowlisted methods 3,733 chars (933 tok). The page
  counts definitions once per Classic LLM turn (`simulate`, `src/demo.html:425-430`); Classic
  turns are 3 / 3 / 2. Re-scoring L16-r4's live inputs with 270 tok less per turn:
  Top 3 9,954/3,838 = 2.594 -> 2.383; Restocking 4,515/3,863 = 1.169 -> 0.960; Tea
  5,609/3,884 = 1.444 -> 1.305.
- README.md:194-203 presents the ratios as Code Mode's advantage. The page discloses
  "10 tools" in its "How the numbers are counted" note, but neither it nor the README says
  that 2 of the 10 are methods Code Mode refuses, and the restocking claim depends on them.
- Refute attempts: (a) a Classic server "one tool per store method" is the stated model
  (README:185); but the Code Mode side is held to the allowlist while Classic is not, so the
  two sides are not answering the same policy. (b) Checked that no scenario calls
  `cancel_order`/`restock` (`src/demo.html:289-327`), so those definitions only add input.
- Fix: build Classic definitions from the search reply's `allowed_methods` (or filter
  `icp.candid` output by them), re-measure, and update README.md:194-203.

###### SW4-0-2 detail

- `src/policy.rs:131` declares `CANDID_OVERRIDES`; the only accessors are
  `set_candid_override` (`:233`) and `candid_override(key)` (`:240`, single-key lookup).
  `PolicyView` (`src/lib.rs:27-36`) and `get_policy` (`src/lib.rs:335-343`) carry limits,
  allowlist, tokens, `active_runs`, `pending_run_ids`: no overrides. `icp_code_mode.did:105`
  has only the setter.
- Serving paths read D5 first: `IcBridge::candid` (`src/bridge.rs:475`), `service`
  (`:441`), `cached_service` (`:207-213`, query and update search).
- Consequence: the controller's view of policy and the runtime's view differ by exactly
  the layer that takes precedence. The only way to learn an override exists is to run a
  script calling `icp.candid` and compare its text with the target's own metadata.
- Fix: add overrides (principal, byte length, hash) to `PolicyView`, or a
  `list_candid_overrides` query.

### grid-sweep-r4-1

#### Variant sweep r4-1: a limit enforced in one route and missing in its sibling route

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 4. Pattern under test:

> A limit enforced in one route and missing in its sibling route.

Routes compared: query vs update HTTP handlers, `inspect_message` vs the method, admin
endpoints vs `InitArgs`, script vs search tools, `icp.call` vs `icp.candid`, the two
interface-fetch messages, the three runtimes, and inside each runtime the **exit routes for
script-produced data**: the result, call arguments, printed values and the **thrown value /
error**. Round 2 (`grid-sweep-r2-9.md`) swept the same pattern for per-request limits and
SDK arguments; this round covers what it did not: the error exit route, demo_store's
sibling updates, and a re-check of every r2-9 row against the known-finding list.

Method: read `src/mcp.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/bridge.rs`, `src/policy.rs`,
`src/runtimes/{mod,js,python,rhai_rt}.rs`, `demo_store/src/lib.rs` at `295d64b`
(`git archive 295d64b`, because the working tree's `src/` has someone else's uncommitted
edits), plus `boa_engine-0.22.0/src/error/mod.rs:557-650, 929-944` and
`rhai-1.27.0/src/types/error.rs:180-188`, `src/serde/serialize.rs:55-86`. Native
reproductions in a private copy (`/private/tmp/claude-501/sweep-r4-1`, deleted afterwards)
with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/audit-target`; one test module appended to the
copy's `src/runtimes/mod.rs` (text below). The test binary was copied out of the shared target
dir right after linking, because another agent's copy of the same package overwrote it twice.

Evidence key: R = reproduced natively (MockBridge, default features, debug build);
CP = code path; known = covered by a finding in the task's known list (not re-reported).

##### Grid

##### Candidates

###### 1. Thrown error text leaves the JS and Python sandboxes without the value limits; results and thrown plain values are held to 4 MiB

- **Where:** `src/runtimes/js.rs:325-333` (`error_string`, native branch); `src/runtimes/python.rs:211, 232-235, 275` (`MontyException::to_string`).
- **Sibling routes:** result (`js.rs:378` `to_json_safe`; `python.rs:241` `to_json` with
  `ValueBudget`) and thrown plain values (`js.rs:335-338`), which are bounded; the thrown
  `Error` / raised exception, which is not.
- **Reproduced (native, MockBridge):**
  - JS `let t='x'; for (let i=0;i<24;i++) t=t+t; return t;` -> `RangeError: value holds more than 4194304 bytes of text`.
  - Same `throw t;` -> `Uncaught <unserializable value>` (bounded).
  - Same `throw new Error(t);` -> error text of **16,777,223 bytes** handed to the host.
  - Python `s='x'*(1<<20)` then `[s]*64` -> `value holds more than 4194304 bytes of text`;
    `raise ValueError(s*16)` -> error text of **16,777,330 bytes**.
  - Rhai: the thrown value is refused by Rhai's own size checks (holds).
- **Effect (CP):** the host builds the message by `to_std_string` (Boa `try_native`), then
  `Display`, then `msg[..i].to_string()`: about three host copies of a string of any size
  (JS has no memory cap, register #24). It is cut to 1 MB in `tool_result` and 4 KiB in the
  audit, so nothing oversized reaches the wire. No N-fold amplification was found (`Display`
  ignores `cause`; Monty exceptions take one argument and collapse repeated traceback frames).
- **Severity:** Low. The limit is inconsistent between exit routes, but the bypass is a
  constant-factor copy of a string the script already holds, and CL10 does not name thrown
  values.
- **Fix:** bound error text at the source: truncate the native message to
  `MAX_VALUE_BYTES` (or to `MAX_RESULT_BYTES`) before copying it out of the engine, and do
  the same for `MontyException` messages; add a test that throws a 16 MiB `Error` and raises
  a 16 MiB `ValueError`.

###### 2. A thrown `AggregateError` with a huge sparse `errors` array makes `error_string` reserve and walk `errors.length` entries outside every limit; at `2**32-1` this traps on wasm32

- **Where:** `src/runtimes/js.rs:326` (`err.try_native(ctx)` on a script-thrown value) ->
  `boa_engine-0.22.0/src/error/mod.rs:604-631`: `length_of_array_like` (script-controlled),
  `error_list.reserve(length as usize)`, then `for i in 0..length { errors.get(i) }`.
- **Sibling route:** the result route snapshots the same object under the 200,000-node limit
  and the instruction budget checks; the thrown-`Error` route calls into Boa's conversion,
  which has neither. The run's budget is not checked again before `error_string` runs.
- **Script:** `const e = new AggregateError([]); e.errors.length = N; throw e;` (one line,
  no allocation in the engine: the array is sparse).
- **Reproduced (native, debug build):** N = 2^20: 0.73 s; 2^22: 2.89 s; 2^24: 11.46 s, then
  `AggregateError` (the conversion is linear in N; the same setup ending in `return 1` takes
  4 ms). N = 2^32-1: still running after 60 s (the 64-bit host reserved 171 GB lazily);
  killed.
- **On wasm32 (CP, unambiguous):** `usize` is 32 bits, so `reserve(4294967295)` needs more
  than `isize::MAX` bytes for any element size and Rust's `Vec` panics with "capacity
  overflow"; `panic = "abort"` makes that a trap. Smaller N spend instructions in host code
  with no budget check (not measured on-chain: no deploy in this phase).
- **Outcome:** the request traps instead of returning a clean error. If the script sent no
  message first, the whole run leaves no audit entry (register #11); otherwise a `Trapped`
  entry replaces the closing one.
- **Severity:** Medium (clean-failure invariant broken from a one-line script; same outcome
  class as the known Boa capacity-overflow findings, but the call into the unbounded
  conversion is app code, so it is fixed here, not in Boa). May merge with "Further Boa
  capacity-overflow sites" if the verifier treats it as the same root cause.
- **Fix:** do not call `try_native` on script-thrown values. Pass every opaque error through
  the bounded snapshot (or read `name` and `message` with a length cap), and check the
  budget before converting the final error.

##### Test used (appended to the private copy's `src/runtimes/mod.rs`; abridged)

```rust
// thrown_vs_returned_sizes: JS "let t='x'; for (let i=0;i<24;i++) t=t+t;" + "return t;" /
//   "throw new Error(t);" / "throw t;"; Python "s='x'*(1<<20)" + "[s]*64" /
//   "raise ValueError(s*16)"; Rhai "let s=\"\"; s.pad(1000000,'x'); throw [s, s];"
// js_aggregate_sparse_errors: for n in [1<<20, 1<<22, 1<<24]:
//   "const e = new AggregateError([]); e.errors.length = {n}; throw e;"
// js_aggregate_max_length (ignored): same with 4294967295
// rhai_debug_curry: debug(f) / print(f) for f curried 10/100/400 times with a 1 MB string
```

##### Not tested

- The on-chain instruction cost of candidate 2 for N below 2^32-1, and the wasm32 trap
  itself: both need a deployment (Live phase).
- Rhai thrown values nested about 10,000 deep (the `Display` recursion is the same one the
  known "Rhai print deeply nested values unchecked" finding covers).

### grid-sweep-r4-2

#### Variant sweep r4-2: one unrepresentable value, three rules across sibling converters

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 4. Pattern under test (from confirmed L6-9):

> An unrepresentable value handled by three different rules (drop, stringify, error) across
> sibling converters.

Method: code reading at `295d64b` plus native probes. The probes ran in a private copy of the
tree (no `target/`) with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/audit-target`, as a
throw-away test module `runtimes::sweep_r4_2` that drives `LanguageRouter::execute` with
`MockBridge` and prints result, logs and the JSON each call sent (`cargo test --lib
sweep_r4_2 -- --nocapture`). The copy was deleted afterwards. Nothing was deployed or
changed on the live network.

For each row the question was: is there a set of converters that should treat a value the
same way (the three runtimes, two directions, or two output paths of one runtime), and does
a value one of them cannot represent get dropped by one, turned into text by another and
refused by a third?

Known and not re-reported: L6-9 (results/args: function dropped in JS, repr in Python,
refused in Rhai), L7-2, L7-4 (NaN/inf to null), L7-6 (Python repr fallback), L7-7 (Python
non-str keys), L7-10 and SW11-3 (JS lone surrogates as literal `\uD800`), L7-11, L7-16,
L7-17, the README:369 depth-placeholder finding for printing, the Rhai reply-limit finding.
