##### Candidates

###### SW4-2-1 JS console.log/print and uncaught-error text pass values through the JSON snapshot: errors print `{}`, NaN/functions `null`, Symbols nothing (Low, reproduced)

- Where: `src/runtimes/js.rs:217-225` (`display`), `:325-340` (`error_string`).
- Repro (native, MockBridge): `try { await icp.call('nope-bad','m',null) } catch (e) { console.log('failed', e) }`
  logs `failed {}`. Python `print('failed', e)` and Rhai `print("failed " + e)` log
  `failed policy: canister nope-bad is not allowlisted`.
  `console.log(NaN, Infinity, -0)` -> `null null 0`; `console.log(() => 1)` -> `null`;
  `console.log(Symbol('s'))` -> empty line; `console.log(1n)` -> `1` but `console.log([1n])`
  -> `<unprintable value>`; `console.log(new Error('boom'))` -> `{}`. Python prints
  `nan inf -0.0`, `<built-in function len>`, `boom`; Rhai prints `NaN`, `inf`, `Fn(f)`.
  Thrown values: `throw undefined|() => 1|Symbol('s')|NaN` -> `Uncaught null`;
  `throw 1n` -> `Uncaught <unserializable value>`; `throw new Map([[1,2]])` -> `Uncaught {}`.
- Three rules inside one JS display path: drop (Error, Map -> `{}`, function/NaN -> `null`,
  Symbol -> empty because `to_string` throws and `unwrap_or_default` hides it), stringify
  (top-level BigInt, undefined), error placeholder (nested BigInt, deep values). The two
  sibling runtimes stringify every case.
- Impact: the catch-and-log idiom, the usual way an AI-written script reports a policy
  refusal, hands the model `{}` instead of the reason, against "identical semantics in
  every language" in the tool description (`mcp.rs:79`). No effect on calls or the audit.
- Refutation tried: is this just JSON.stringify semantics like the result path (where the
  L7 grid accepted Map -> `{}`)? For results, yes; but a console has no JSON contract, JS's
  own console prints errors and NaN as text, and the sibling runtimes print text. Does
  `error_string` catch native errors first? Yes (`try_native`), so `throw new Error(..)` is
  fine; only non-Error throws are affected.
- Fix: in `display`, print strings, numbers (`Number.prototype.toString`, so NaN stays
  `NaN`), bigints, symbols (`description`) and Error objects (`name: message`) directly and
  use the snapshot only for plain objects and arrays; in `error_string`, fall back to
  `JsValue::display()` for primitives before the snapshot.

###### SW4-2-2 A caught host error returned in a result is `{}` in JS, a repr string in Python and the message in Rhai (Low, reproduced; merge candidate into L6-9)

- Where: `src/runtimes/js.rs:45-94, 207-215` (snapshot: Error has no enumerable own keys),
  `src/runtimes/python.rs:98` (`_ => py_repr`), `src/runtimes/rhai_rt.rs:111-114` (catch
  binds the message string).
- Repro: JS `const r = await Promise.allSettled([icp.call('nope-bad','m',null)]); return r`
  -> `[{"reason":{},"status":"rejected"}]`, run Ok. JS `catch (e) { return {err: e} }` ->
  `{"err":{}}`. Python `except Exception as e: {'err': e}` ->
  `{"err":"RuntimeError('policy: canister nope-bad is not allowlisted')"}`. Rhai
  `catch (e) { #{err: e} }` -> `{"err":"policy: canister nope-bad is not allowlisted"}`.
- Same converters and root as L6-9 (no shared rule for non-JSON values); the new part is the
  value class: every rejected `icp.call` produces one, and `Promise.allSettled`, the batch
  idiom for partial failure, returns all reasons as `{}` while the run reports Ok.
- Fix: as L6-9 (one shared rule). For JS, convert Error objects to `{name, message}` (or
  their message) in the snapshot before the type rules.

###### SW4-2-3 A lone-surrogate escape is exported as literal text in JS, silently replaced by U+FFFD in Python, and refused in Rhai (Low, reproduced; cross-runtime extension of L7-10)

- Where: script source parsing in the engines (Monty's string-literal decoding, `monty
  =1.6.0`; Rhai's lexer; Boa strings + `to_std_string_escaped`, `js.rs:197`).
- Repro: Python `x = '\ud800'; [x, len(x)]` -> `["�", 1]`; `'\udc00x' == '�x'`
  -> `True`; `icp.call(L, 'icrc1_balance_of', {'owner': '\ud800'})` sends
  `{"owner":"�"}`, run Ok. Python `chr(0xd800)` -> `ValueError: chr() arg not in
  range(0x110000)` (the argument is in range; the message is wrong). Rhai `"\ud800"` ->
  `syntax error: Invalid escape sequence`. JS `'\ud800'` -> sent as the six characters
  `\uD800` (known L7-10).
- Three rules for one value: stringify (JS), drop/replace (Python literal), error (Python
  `chr`, Rhai). Python's substitution makes two distinct literals equal inside the script.
- Reachability: Python literals with surrogate escapes are rare (Python slicing never
  produces them, unlike JS); the practical impact is small. Graded Low.
- Fix: one documented rule. Refuse lone surrogates when a string leaves the sandbox in JS
  (L7-10's fix), and report them as an error in Python too (a compile-time check or an
  upstream Monty issue), so all three refuse.

<a id="grid-sweep-r4-3"></a>

### grid-sweep-r4-3

#### Variant sweep r4-3: one limit, different operators or different check positions

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 4. Pattern:

> The same limit compared with different operators, or counted at different positions.

Seeds (known, not re-reported): the depth limit is off by one between runtimes (JS
`d >= 128` on containers, Python/Rhai `depth > 128` on every value); `MAX_DEPTH` counts Candid
levels in `candid_bridge` and JSON levels in the runtimes (SW3-8-1); the log cap is 64 KiB raw
in the runtimes and 250,000 escaped bytes in `tool_result` (SW3-8-3). Round 3's units sweep
(r3-8) covered "different units". This sweep looks only at the operator (`>` / `>=` / `<`,
inclusive or exclusive) and at **where** the count is added versus where it is compared.

Method: for every limit row, `grep` every comparison against it in `src/`, `demo_store/` and
`src/demo.html`, then compare each comparison's operator and position. Also check that every
place that adds to a running total is followed by a comparison. Reproductions were native
(`cargo test --lib`) in a private copy (no `target/`, `design/`, `.env`), with the shared
`CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/audit-target`. The copy was deleted afterwards.
Nothing was deployed and no live setting was changed.

Evidence keys: **R** = reproduced natively; **C** = the code path produces it unambiguously.

##### New candidate

| Id | Severity | Candidate | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| SW4-3-1 | High | **JS object-key text is added to the 4 MiB value budget but never compared against it.** In `SNAPSHOT_JS` (`src/runtimes/js.rs:58-66`), `bytes > MAXB` is tested only in the string-value branch (`:58-60`). The key loop (`:64-66`) runs `bytes += k.length` and never checks. Python (`python.rs:91`) and Rhai (`rhai_rt.rs:105`) charge keys through `ValueBudget::bytes`, which compares on every add. So in JS, an object whose values are numbers, booleans, null or nested objects can carry any amount of key text, as long as no string value follows. One large string used as the key of many objects leaves the sandbox as one host copy per object. This brings back register #21 (fixed, High) for JS keys. It affects every path that uses the snapshot: the script result, `icp.call` arguments (`request_fn` -> `to_json_safe`), `console.log` of objects (`display`), and the `JSON.stringify` wrapper. CL10 (README:369, "4 MiB of text, in all three languages") and CL11 ("JSON.stringify is held to the value limits too") are false for JS | **R**: `let k='a'; for (let i=0;i<20;i++) k+=k; return Array.from({length:40},()=>({[k]:1}))` returns `Ok` with 41,943,040 bytes of key text (limit 4,194,304). With `{[k]:'x'}` it fails with `RangeError: value holds more than 4194304 bytes of text`. Python `[{k: 1} for _ in range(40)]` and the Rhai equivalent both fail with the same limit error. `icp.call(L, 'icrc1_balance_of', o)` with 8 keys of 1 MiB: the host received 8,388,629 bytes of key text, and the call was sent. `JSON.stringify(a).length` = 41,943,321. With length 200, the result is `Ok` with about 200 MiB of key text. That took 8.8 s natively, with a peak RSS of 675 MB for the test process. **Inferred, not run**: at about 1,000 x 1 MiB, the host copies pass the 3 GiB Wasm memory limit or the 40e9 instruction limit. The canister traps, and when the trap comes before the first send, no audit entry is written (K8) |

### grid-sweep-r4-4

#### Variant sweep r4-4

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6. Pattern: **"A limit applied to new writes but not to
data already stored (L13). A page bounded by count, not bytes."** Seeds (known, not
re-reported): legacy audit entry id 60 (8.39 MB) is unreadable; `get_audit_logs` page capped
at 100 entries, not bytes; `get_policy` returns admin inputs whole; demo_store
`list_orders(null)`.

Method: for the first half, every write-time check in the code was listed and its history
traced with `git log -S` / `git log -L` (when was it added, did the store already hold data
written without it, is it re-applied on read or in `post_upgrade`). For the second half,
every reply or in-memory list that is capped was checked for a count-only cap, skipping rows
already settled by sweeps r2-1 (search 40-method cap) and r2-6 (growing stores and reads).
One native probe was run in a private copy (`cargo test --lib`, shared
`CARGO_TARGET_DIR`); the copy was deleted afterwards. Evidence: R = reproduced, C = code path.

Result: **one new candidate (S4-4-1).**

endpoint made after parsing) and `bridge::cached_service(&p)` returns the parsed service
(8,552 methods), and `IcBridge::candid("RYJL3-…")` returns all 624,310 bytes. Output:

<a id="grid-sweep-r4-5"></a>

### grid-sweep-r4-5

#### Variant sweep r4-5: altered data returned as success; a smaller limit applied downstream by truncation

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 4. Pattern:

> Partial or altered data returned as success; a second, smaller limit applied downstream by
> truncation instead of refusal (same class as register #2/#33).

Generalised for the sweep: (a) a stage downstream of a limit that admitted a value cuts,
clamps or replaces it instead of refusing; (b) a conversion that substitutes a default
(`""`, `false`, `[]`, `null`, a placeholder) for data it could not read, and the run still
reports success.

Method: `grep` for `truncate`, `truncate_escaped`, `.take(`, `min(`, `saturating_`,
`unwrap_or_default`, `unwrap_or(`, `filter_map`, `slice(` over `src/`, `demo_store/src/`,
`src/demo.html`, `video/`, `scripts/`; read every hit and every conversion in B1-B17.
Native probes in a private copy (`/private/tmp/claude-501/sweep-r4-5.*`, repo copied
without `target/`, `design/`, the uncommitted plan doc and `.env`; shared
`CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/audit-target`; `cargo test --lib` /
`cargo test -p demo_store` with probe tests added to the copy only). Nothing was deployed;
the local network was not touched. Copy deleted afterwards.

Evidence: R = reproduced (native test), C = code path. "known" = in the do-not-re-report
list given to this sweep.

##### New candidates

| Id | Severity | Candidate | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| SW4-5-1 | Low | Python `to_json` dispatches on `ObjectRef::type_name()`, which for a script-defined class instance is the class's own name (`monty-types graph.rs:572-575`). An instance of a class named `str`, `bool`, `float`, `list`, `tuple`, `set`, `frozenset` or `NoneType` takes that builtin's arm, whose accessor returns `None`, and `unwrap_or_default()` / `map_or(Null)` substitutes `""`, `false`, `[]` or `null` (`src/runtimes/python.rs:67-88`). The attributes are dropped, the run is `Ok`, and the same substitution is sent as `icp.call` arguments | R: `class str:` ... `{'v': str(), 'n': 1}` -> `{"v":"","n":1}`; `bool` -> `false`; `float` -> `null`; `list`/`tuple`/`set` -> `[]`; `NoneType` -> `null`; `@dataclass class float: amount: int` -> `null`. As call args: `{'flag': bool()}` sent as `"flag": false`, `str()` as `""`, `list()` as `[]`, `float()` as `null`, result `Ok("done")`. Control: `class Point` -> repr string (that is known L7-6) |
| SW4-5-2 | Low | demo_store `restock(product_id, quantity)` adds with `on_hand.saturating_add(quantity)` (`demo_store/src/lib.rs:334`) and returns `Ok(Inventory)`: once `on_hand + quantity` passes `u32::MAX` the extra units are dropped silently, and every later restock of that product is a no-op that still reports success. A clamp in place of the `Err(String)` the method already has | R: `restock(1, u32::MAX)` -> `on_hand 4294967295`; then `restock(1, 1000)` -> `Ok`, `on_hand 4294967295` (unchanged) |
| SW4-5-3 | Low | JS `display` (console.log/info/warn/error/debug, `print`) formats Symbols with `v.to_string(ctx)...unwrap_or_default()` (`src/runtimes/js.rs:218-219`). `ToString(Symbol)` throws per spec, so the argument prints as an empty string with no error: printed output is altered while the run succeeds | R: `console.log("a", Symbol("x"), "b"); print(Symbol.iterator)` -> logs `["a  b", ""]`, result `Ok(1)` |

<a id="grid-sweep-r4-6"></a>

### grid-sweep-r4-6

#### Variant sweep r4-6: serialised, re-parsed under different limits, parse error defaulted

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 4. Pattern (seed, known, not re-reported: L7-2, JS
call arguments are written with `Value::to_string` and re-read with
`serde_json::from_str(..).unwrap_or(Value::Null)` at `src/runtimes/js.rs:395`, so arguments
128 containers deep become `null` and the call is still sent):

> A value serialised and re-parsed between components with different limits, with the parse
> error defaulted instead of reported.

Question asked of every inventory row: does a value leave one component in a serialised
form (text, Candid bytes, JSON, an agent's structured output) and get read back by another
component whose rules differ (depth, type, schema, version), and if the reader fails, is the
failure turned into a default (`null`, `None`, empty, "nothing found") instead of an error?

Method: grep of every `unwrap_or*`, `.ok()`, `if let Ok`, `from_str`, `from_slice`,
`Decode!`, `decode_one`, `to_dynamic`/`from_dynamic`, `from_json`/`to_json` site in
`src/`, `demo_store/src/`, `shims/`; reading `src/demo.html`, `scripts/`, `video/*.mjs`,
`.claude/workflows/audit.js`; dependency source for the readers (Boa `from_json`, Monty
`object_bridge`/`MontyGraph::type_name`, ic-stable-structures `StableCell::init`, Monty
execution clock). One native probe in a private copy (no `target/`, `.icp/`, `.git`,
`design/`, `video/`, `.env`, `docs/per-customer-canisters-plan.md`), shared
`CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, `cargo test --lib sw_probe`; copy deleted afterwards. Two read-only
queries to the local `demo_store` (port 8010) with icp-cli. Nothing deployed, upgraded or
reconfigured; no `icp_code_mode` method was called. **R** = reproduced, **C** = code path.

##### Candidates

###### SW4-6-1 Install, upgrade and admin arguments under `opt` that do not fit their type are decoded as `null`, and the setting is silently not applied (Medium)

- **Where:** `src/lib.rs:62-72` (`init(args: Option<InitArgs>)`, `post_upgrade(..)`),
  `src/lib.rs:38-49` (`apply`: `None` returns, `limits: None` keeps the old limits),
  `src/lib.rs:19-24` (`InitArgs.limits: Option<Limits>`), `src/policy.rs:33, 38`
  (`Limits.call_timeout_seconds: opt nat32`, `certified_reads: opt bool`),
  `src/lib.rs:324` (`set_candid_override(.., did: Option<String>)`, `None` = clear).
- **Mechanism:** the operator's tool serialises the arguments as Candid with its own types;
  the canister re-reads them with ic-cdk's typed decoder. Candid's `opt` rule turns any
  value under `opt` that does not fit the declared type into `None` instead of a decoding
  error. The app then treats `None` as "not given". Outside `opt` the same mistakes are a
  loud error (control P2c).
- **Evidence (R, native, candid 0.10.40 as locked; untyped encoding = `candid_parser::parse_idl_args(..).to_bytes()`):**
  - P1 `(opt record { token_sha256 = vec {"a"x64}; allowlist = vec {}; limits = opt record { max_calls_per_script = 5; max_instructions = 1_000_000_000 } })`
    -> `token_sha256` applied, `limits = None` (plain integer literals are `int`, not
    `nat32`/`nat64`). Install/upgrade succeeds with the default 25 / 20e9 limits.
  - P2 same with `allow_list` misspelled -> the whole `InitArgs` is `None`: no token, no
    allowlist, no limits; `apply(None)` returns; install/upgrade succeeds.
  - P2c control: `set_limits(record { ..; max_instruction = 1 : nat64 })` (not under `opt`)
    -> decode error.
  - P3 `set_limits(record { max_calls_per_script = 25 : nat32; max_instructions = 20_000_000_000 : nat64; call_timeout_seconds = opt 60; certified_reads = opt true })`
    -> `call_timeout_seconds: None` (unbounded wait, register #44's protection off) while
    the operator asked for 60 s; `certified_reads: Some(true)`.
  - P3b `certified_reads = opt 1` -> `None` (uncertified queries).
  - P4 `set_candid_override(principal "aaaaa-aa", opt blob "service : {}")` -> `did = None`,
    i.e. "clear the override"; same with ic-cdk-style quotas
    (`decode_args_with_config`).
  - Live, read-only (R): the same rule in a deployed ic-cdk canister. `demo_store
    list_products` with hex `4449444c016e7c01000105` (`opt int 5`, untyped) returns all 12
    products, exactly like `(null)`; typed `(opt "tea")` returns 4.
- **Who triggers it:** any encoder that does not type the arguments against the canister's
  `.did`: `--args-format hex`/`bin`, another canister (the factory idea in C14, an
  orchestrator, a governance proposal payload), agents with a hand-written or stale IDL.
  icp-cli 1.7.0 `canister call` types arguments against the fetched interface and refuses
  P1-style mistakes client-side (R: `list_products '(opt 5)'` -> "type mismatch: 5 can not
  be of type text"), so the README's documented admin calls are protected. For `init_args`
  / `upgrade_args` / `icp canister install --args`, the icp-cli binary's error strings for
  that path are only "failed to parse Candid args" / "failed to encode Candid args to
  bytes" (no "with specific types" variant, unlike `call`), which suggests inferred types;
  **not executed** (installing is a deploy). If install args are untyped, P1 is the
  ordinary way to write limits in `icp.yaml`, and they are dropped on every deploy.
- **Distinct from known findings:** "A terse or old-shape set_limits (or InitArgs.limits)
  silently turns certified_reads and call_timeout_seconds off" is about *omitted* fields
  under whole-record replacement; here the operator *supplied* the value and it is
  discarded by the decoder. "post_upgrade re-applies InitArgs additively" is about what
  `apply` does with arguments it received; here `apply` never receives them.
- **Invariant:** Honest interface / Fidelity (data crossing a boundary arrives intact or
  fails loudly); Configuration (an operator is misled: success reply, setting not applied).
- **Fix (proposed, not applied):** make the admin and install arguments non-`opt` where
  absence is not meaningful (`InitArgs.limits` as a record with defaults supplied by the
  operator, or a separate `set_limits` call), or decode them untyped first and compare the
  wire type with the expected type (`candid::types::subtype::subtype_with_config` with
  `OptReport::Error`) and trap on mismatch; at minimum, echo the applied `Limits` and
  override state in the reply / a log line so the operator can see what was stored.
- **Regression test:** P1, P2, P3 and P4 as unit tests on the decoder: each must be an
  error, never `None`.

###### SW4-6-2 The audit workflow turns an agent output it could not obtain into "nothing found", and that counts toward the stopping rule (Medium)

- **Where:** `.claude/workflows/audit.js:192-194` (`verify`: `if (!found) return null`),
  `:208-221` (`absorb` filters out `null` results), `:230-247` (review and sweep results go
  through `verify`/`absorb`; `fresh` 0 -> `dry + 1`), `:268-269` (`work = critic ? .. : []`
  then logs "the critic found no further gaps"), `:287-291` (live verdicts matched by exact
  `title`; an unmatched refutation is ignored).
- **Mechanism:** each agent's answer is serialised by the agent, schema-checked by the
  harness and read back by the script; the script already knows the read can fail (it
  handles `null` for the inventory, live and report agents). For reviewers, verifiers,
  sweepers and the critic the failure is defaulted instead:
  1. A reviewer or sweeper that does not finish: `verify(null)` returns `null`, `absorb`
     drops it, nothing is added to `notTested`, nothing is logged; the round can count as
     dry.
  2. A verifier that does not finish for a non-empty candidate list: the candidates are
     neither confirmed nor refuted nor listed anywhere; they vanish from the report.
  3. A critic that does not finish: `work = []` and the log says "the critic found no
     further gaps"; the loop ends.
  4. A live agent that rewrites a title: its refutation (`real: false`) matches nothing
     and is dropped, so the finding stays confirmed without its live refutation.
- **Evidence (C):** unambiguous from the script; not executed (running the workflow is out
  of scope for a sweep agent).
- **Effect:** the run report, the register and `complete_by_stopping_rule` are records the
  plan relies on. Agent failures can make a round look dry (two of them satisfy the
  plan's stopping rule), drop candidate findings without trace, and print a false
  "critic found no further gaps".
- **Invariant:** Records match reality (the audit report is the record); plan section 1
  ("an empty cell is unfinished work, not an assumption of safety").
- **Fix (proposed, not applied):** treat a `null` agent result as an error everywhere:
  log it, add the lens/pattern to `notTested` and back to `work`, never count that round
  as dry, carry unverified candidates into the report as "unverified"; log "the critic did
  not finish" separately; match live verdicts by a stable id passed in the prompt, not by
  title.
- **Regression test:** a dry-run harness for the workflow with an `agent()` stub that
  returns `null` for one reviewer, one verifier and the critic; assert the round is not
  dry, the candidates appear as unverified and the log names each failure.

<a id="grid-sweep-r4-7"></a>

### grid-sweep-r4-7

#### Variant sweep r4-7: lossy input accepted as exact; precision rule enforced on output only

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 4. Pattern under test:

> A lossy input accepted as exact; a precision rule enforced on output only.

Seed finding: L7-3 / L5r2-4 (integral JS floats above 2^53 accepted by `num_text` as exact
integers, while `idl_to_json` applies `MAX_SAFE_INT` to replies only). For each inventory row
the question is: does a value enter the app (from a script, a client, an operator or a
target) through a conversion that can silently lose precision or change the value, while
the app reports or treats it as the exact value?

Known and not repeated: L7-2 (JS args 128 deep -> null), L7-3 (integral floats > 2^53),
L7-4 (NaN/Infinity -> null), L7-5 (`f64 as f32` saturation/underflow, float text overflow),
L7-9 (JSON-RPC ids), L7-12 (lenient numeric/hex text), L7-16/L7-16b (raw strings, Python
time in seconds), L7-17 (Python/Rhai ints 2^53..2^63 as numbers), Python repr fallbacks.

##### How it was tested

Private copy `/private/tmp/claude-501/sweep-r4-7.5flQ/repo` (no `target/`, `design/`,
`.env`, the uncommitted plan doc), `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/audit-target`.
Throwaway code (deleted with the copy):

- `examples/rt.rs`, `examples/rt2.rs`: serde_json 1.0.154 (the locked version; features
  `default`+`std` only per `cargo tree -e features -i serde_json`, so no `float_roundtrip`)
  `Value::from(f).to_string()` then `from_str`, bit comparison.
- `src/runtimes/mod.rs` test `sweep_r4_7::float_args_round_trip`: the same literal in JS,
  Python and Rhai, passed to `icp.call` through `LanguageRouter::execute` with
  `MockBridge`, then the recorded argument encoded with `candid_bridge::Service::encode_args`
  against `service : { f : (float64) -> (); n : (nat) -> () }`.

##### Results

###### New candidate S4-7-1: JS call arguments lose up to 1 ulp in a text round trip (reproduced)

`js.rs:262` stores the snapshot of the args as text (`a.to_string()`), and `js.rs:395`
parses it back with `serde_json::from_str`. serde_json is built without
`float_roundtrip`, so its default float parser is best-effort and differs from the
written value by 1 ulp for a large share of floats: 5,927,545 of 19,990,233 random finite
bit patterns; 10-30% of values per decade from 1e-30 to 1e40; 210,722 of 2,000,000 values
in [0,1). The result path (`to_json_safe` -> `Value`) has no text step and stays exact,
as do Python (`to_json` builds `Value` directly) and Rhai (`to_json_value`).

Same literal, three runtimes (native, `cargo test --lib sweep_r4_7 -- --nocapture`):

| literal | JS sent | Python / Rhai sent | Candid sent by JS |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0.36040155707569876` | `0.3604015570756987` | exact | `(0.3604015570756987 : float64)` |
| `1841021037.9102077` | `1841021037.9102075` | exact | `(1841021037.9102075 : float64)` |
| `1.1022301835603701e-10` | `1.10223018356037e-10` | exact | float64 1 ulp lower |
| `1.1296295699452381e18` | `1.129629569945238e18` | exact | `nat 1_129_629_569_945_238_016` (Py/Rhai `..._144`) |

The JS script's own `return {v: x}` shows the unaltered value, so the result and the
message disagree; the run reports Ok. Same site as L7-2 (both are the args text round
trip); distinct symptom: L7-2's depth fix would not fix this. Evidence: reproduced natively;
the wasm build runs the same pure-Rust parser (code path; not run on the local network).

###### Cells

| Row | Verdict | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| B1 HTTP body -> JSON | holds (beyond L7-9) | Only numeric field used is `id` (L7-9). Tool arguments `code`, `query`, `canister_id`, `language` are strings |
| B2 Candid ingress -> HttpUpdateRequest | holds | Candid decode is exact or fails |
| B3 token -> SHA-256 | n/a | not numeric; trim/case-fold is documented |
| B4 principal text | holds | `Principal::from_text` checks the CRC; no lossy form accepted (whitespace in search is a known finding) |
| B5 `json_to_idl` ints | holds beyond L7-3/L7-12 | Non-integral floats refused; `|f| >= 1e19` falls to `n.to_string()` (`1e19`) and fails loudly; strings exact; Python ints > i64 arrive as exact decimal `py_repr` |
| B5 float64 | holds in `json_to_idl` | `n.as_f64()` exact; string via Rust `str::parse` (correctly rounded) |
| B5 float32 | known L7-5 | `as f32` rounding/saturation/underflow; no new symptom |

Refute attempts: checked `cargo tree` for any crate enabling `float_roundtrip` or
`arbitrary_precision` through feature unification (none); checked that integral values
<= 2^53 are unaffected (normalised to i64 before the text step); checked that the result
path is exact (it is, so the defect is confined to args).

<a id="grid-sweep-r4-8"></a>

### grid-sweep-r4-8

#### Variant sweep r4-8: a value with no JSON form becomes a substitute

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 4. Pattern (shared root with L7-6 and L7-10):

> A value with no JSON form is mapped to a substitute instead of an error or the string form
> used elsewhere (runtime -> JSON conversion substitutes unrepresentable values).

Known and not re-reported: L7-2 (128-deep JS args -> `null`), L7-4 (NaN/Infinity -> `null` in
results and args, all three runtimes), L7-6 (Python repr fallback), L7-7 (non-str dict keys),
L7-10 (JS lone surrogates -> literal `\uD800`), L6-9 (JS drops functions/undefined in results),
SW1-3 (boxed primitives), SW3-9-1 (Monty `<deeply nested>` / `[...]` markers), `<unprintable
value>` (README:369 finding), Rhai `from_dynamic` refusals (holds).

Question asked of every row: where does a value with no JSON (or no UTF-8) form cross a
boundary, and does it come out as an error, as the string form the rest of the system uses
for it, or as a silent substitute?

Evidence: **R** = reproduced, **C** = code path. Probes ran natively as a `#[cfg(test)]`
module (`src/sweep_probe.rs`) in a private copy made with `git archive 295d64b` (no
`target/`, no uncommitted files), built with the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. The copy's
package version was changed to `0.1.0-sweepr48`, because with the shared target directory
another copy's test binary was otherwise reused without compiling this one. The copy was
deleted afterwards. No live canister was touched.

##### Candidates

###### SW4-8-1 (Medium). JS console output and uncaught thrown values are formatted through the JSON snapshot, so Errors print as `{}`, NaN/Infinity/functions as `null`, Symbols as an empty string and BigInts as `<unserializable value>`

`display` (`src/runtimes/js.rs:217-225`) formats every non-string argument of
`console.log/info/warn/error/debug` and `print` with `to_json_safe`, the JSON snapshot
used for results. `error_string` (`js.rs:335-339`) does the same for uncaught non-Error
thrown values and rejection reasons. JSON has no form for an Error's message, NaN, Infinity,
functions or undefined, so these print as JSON substitutes. JavaScript's own string form
(`String(e)` prints `Error: policy: ...`) is not used. For Symbols, the special case calls
`to_string`, which throws for a Symbol, and `unwrap_or_default()` turns that into `""`.

R (native, MockBridge):

| Script | JS output | Python / Rhai for the same thing |
|---|---|---|
| `try { await icp.call('aaaaa-aa','raw_rand',null) } catch (e) { console.log('failed:', e) }` | log `failed: {}` | Python `print('failed:', e)`: `failed: policy: canister aaaaa-aa is not allowlisted`; Rhai the same |
| same, `console.log({err: e})` | `{"err":{}}` | Python `{'err': RuntimeError('policy: ...')}`; Rhai `#{"err": "policy: ..."}` |
| `try { null.x } catch (e) { console.log(e); console.error(e) }` | `{}`, `[error] {}` | |
| `console.log(NaN); console.log(Infinity, -Infinity)` | `null`, `null null` | Python `nan inf`; Rhai `NaN`, `inf` |
| `console.log('x', NaN, 'y')` | `x null y` (but `String(NaN)` prints `NaN`) | |
| `console.log(() => 1)` / `console.log(Symbol('s'))` / `console.log(10n)` | `null` / `""` (empty line) / `10` | Python `print(len)`: `<built-in function len>` |
| `console.log([NaN, undefined, () => 1])` | `[null,null,null]` | Python `[nan]`; Rhai `[NaN, ()]` |
| `console.log(new Date(NaN))` | `null` | |
| `throw undefined` / `throw NaN` / `throw Infinity` / `throw Symbol('s')` / `throw () => 1` / `await Promise.reject(undefined)` | run error `Uncaught null` | Rhai `throw 0.0/0.0` -> `Runtime error: NaN`; `throw ()` -> `Runtime error` |
| `throw 10n` / `await Promise.reject(10n)` | `Uncaught <unserializable value>` (while `console.log(10n)` prints `10`) | Rhai `throw 10` -> `Runtime error: 10` |
| `throw [NaN, undefined]` / `throw new Map([[1,2]])` | `Uncaught [null,null]` / `Uncaught {}` | |

- Impact: the most common JS error idiom, `catch (e) { console.log(e) }`, hides the reason
  for every policy refusal, call rejection and runtime error. The captured output is what
  the AI model reads to debug its script, and it gets `{}`. The same script in Python or
  Rhai shows the message. The tool description promises "identical semantics in every
  language" (`src/mcp.rs:79`, shown to the AI). Thrown substitutes reach the tool result
  text and the closing audit entry's `error` field (`lib.rs` run_script, C): `throw NaN`
  and `throw undefined` are both recorded as `Uncaught null`, and `throw 10n` loses its
  value.
- Not covered by known findings: L7-4 / L6-9 are about values that leave as results or
  call arguments, where JSON is the contract. Here the target is human-readable text, and
  the JavaScript string form exists. `<unprintable value>` (README:369 finding) is the
  snapshot error path. This finding is the snapshot success path returning substitutes.
- Refuted alternatives: strings, `undefined` at top level and BigInt in `console.log` are
  special-cased and print correctly. Thrown `Error` objects go through `try_native` and
  keep their message. Only non-Error throws and console arguments are affected.
- Fix: format console arguments and thrown values with a bounded ToString-style formatter,
  not the JSON snapshot. For example, use `String(x)` for primitives, symbols, functions
  and Error objects (`name: message`), and the snapshot only for plain objects and arrays,
  with NaN/Infinity printed as `NaN`/`Infinity`. Remove the dead `is_symbol()` branch, or
  use `Symbol.prototype.toString`. Regression test: in JS, `catch (e) { console.log(e) }`
  after a policy refusal must log text that contains `not allowlisted`, as Python and Rhai
  do.

###### SW4-8-2 (Low). Python string literals with a lone-surrogate escape are silently replaced by U+FFFD and sent

Monty's parser, `ruff_python_parser` 0.0.14 (`src/string.rs:179`, in `Cargo.lock`), maps
`\uD800`-`\uDFFF` escapes to `std::char::REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER`. A Monty `str` is strict
UTF-8, so the script never sees the surrogate it wrote, and nothing reports the change.
CPython keeps the surrogate in the `str` and raises `UnicodeEncodeError` when it is
encoded. JS has the same input and sends the six literal characters `\uD800` (L7-10).
Rhai refuses the literal at compile time (`syntax error: Invalid escape sequence`). The
same value thus has three outcomes, and only Rhai's is an error.

R (native, MockBridge):
- `icp.call(L, 'icrc1_balance_of', {'owner': 'aaaaa-aa', 's': 'x\ud800y'})`: the call is
  sent with `s: "x\u{FFFD}y"` and returns Ok. JS sends `"x\\uD800y"`, also Ok.
- `s = 'x\ud800y'; [len(s), s == 'x�y', ord(s[1])]` -> `[3, true, 65533]`.
- `'a\udc00b'.encode('utf-8')` -> bytes `97, 239, 191, 189, 98` (CPython raises).
- `print('x\ud800y')` logs `x\u{FFFD}y`.
- Loud siblings (hold): `chr(0xD800)` raises `ValueError: chr() arg not in range(0x110000)`,
  and Monty's codecs raise `NotImplementedError` for `surrogateescape`/`surrogatepass`
  (`monty-1.6.0 src/codecs.rs:230-262`). So Monty treats lone surrogates as errors
  everywhere except in the parser.
- Overlap: the same class as L7-10 (lone surrogates do not survive and the run is still Ok),
  through a different mechanism, in a dependency's lexer. The verifier may merge it into
  L7-10 as the Python half of a cross-runtime finding.
- Fix: before `MontyRun::new`, refuse sources that contain `\uD8xx`-`\uDFxx` escapes in
  string literals. A conservative check: scan the source for `\\u[dD][89a-fA-F]` and
  `\\U0000[dD][89a-fA-F]`. Otherwise document the substitution. Better, fix L7-10 and this
  together, so that a lone surrogate is an error in every runtime. Regression test: the
  Python `icp.call` above must fail and send nothing.

### grid-sweep-r4-9

#### Variant sweep r4-9: narrowing cast or parse that saturates instead of failing

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 4. Pattern (seed L7-5, with its siblings L7-11/12/13,
all known and not re-reported):

> A narrowing cast or parse that saturates (or otherwise coerces leniently) instead of
> failing, so a value that does not fit arrives changed and the operation reports success.

Method: `grep -nE "\bas (u8|u16|u32|u64|u128|usize|i8|i16|i32|i64|i128|isize|f32|f64)\b|parse::<|\.parse\(\)|from_str|unwrap_or|try_from|saturating|as_u64|as_i64|as_f64|clamp|\.min\(|\.max\("`
over `src/`, `demo_store/src/`, `shims/web-time/src/`; read every hit; read the four
value converters (B5, B8, B9, B10) and the demo_store write paths; grep `src/demo.html`,
`video/*.mjs`, `scripts/*.sh` for JS numeric coercions. Checked that no dependency turns on
serde_json `arbitrary_precision` (`cargo tree -e features -i serde_json`: `default`, `std`
only), so every `as_f64`/`as_i64` result below is the plain i64/u64/f64 form.
Evidence: R = reproduced (native test in a private copy, shared target dir), C = code path.

##### Probes (private copy, deleted afterwards)

- P1 `demo_store` `restock(1, u32::MAX)` on seed stock 21 -> `Ok(Inventory { on_hand: 4294967295 })`;
  21 units silently lost. Then `restock(1, 1000)` -> `Ok`, `on_hand` unchanged (R).
- P2 `json_to_idl` against `record { 5 : nat8; b : nat; c : float64; d : float32; e : int64 }`:
  keys `"+5"` and `"_+5_"` match field 5; `"+7"`, `"+12"`, `"+3"` accepted; `"1e-400"` -> `0.0`,
  `1e-50` (float32) -> `0.0`, `"-1e400"` -> `-inf`, `"infinity"` -> `inf`; `9.2e18` (int64) ->
  exact `9_200_000_000_000_000_000`; `1e19` (int64) -> error `` `1e+19` is not a valid int64 `` (R).

| LIM5 `policy.rs:265` `limit.min(MAX_AUDIT_PAGE)` | audit page | holds | Documented clamp (CL32); offset arithmetic is `checked_*` (C) |

| `lib.rs:445` `as u8` | getrandom bytes | holds | Intended byte extraction (C) |
| `mcp.rs:179` `c as u32` | escaping | holds | Widening (C) |
| U4 JSON-RPC ids | | **known** (L7-9) | |
| AD1-AD5 admin Candid args | nat32/nat64 | holds | Candid decoding rejects out-of-range values; no app-side narrowing (C) |
| E23 demo_store `restock` `on_hand.saturating_add(quantity)` (`demo_store/src/lib.rs:334`) | stock count | **finding SW4-9-1** (R, P1) | Excess quantity is discarded and the call returns `Ok`. Earlier sweeps r3-4/r3-5 marked this "holds" for growth and wrap patterns; for this pattern it is the hit |
| E22 demo_store `cancel_order` `reserved.saturating_sub` (`:324`) | stock | **known** root cause | Only reachable when `reserved < quantity`, i.e. after the known oversell / `reserved` wrap; sweep r3-5 already ties it there |
| E21 demo_store `create_order` `available = on_hand.saturating_sub(reserved)` (`:290`) | stock | holds | Saturating to 0 available is the correct reading of an oversold product (C) |
| E21 demo_store `create_order` `total += cents * quantity` (`:294`) | order total | **known** root cause | Wraps (not saturates) only with release overflow checks off plus unbounded duplicate lines: the known oversell and overflow-checks findings |

| C12 video scripts (`render.mjs:10`, `tts.mjs:27, 62, 68`) | dev tooling | not applicable | Local CLI parsing of the developer's own arguments and ffprobe output |

##### New candidate

**SW4-9-1 (Low).** `demo_store.restock(product_id, quantity)` adds with
`on_hand.saturating_add(quantity)` (`demo_store/src/lib.rs:334`) and returns `Ok`. When the
sum passes `u32::MAX`, the excess units are silently dropped instead of the call failing.
P1: `restock(1, 4294967295)` on seed stock 21 returns `Ok` with `on_hand = 4294967295` (21 units
lost); a further `restock(1, 1000)` returns `Ok` and changes nothing. Anyone can call it
(demo_store has no access control, known). The returned `Inventory` shows the capped value, so the
caller can see it only by comparing. Fix: `checked_add(quantity).ok_or("stock would exceed u32::MAX")?`.

##### Merged, not new

`+` signs in numeric text and in record id keys, and float64 text underflow to 0 / `"infinity"`,
are further spellings of the known L7-12, L7-13 and L7-5 (P2). They share one root cause:
`json_to_idl` delegates to Rust's `FromStr`, which accepts these spellings, and casts without
range checks.

<a id="grid-sweep-r4-10"></a>

### grid-sweep-r4-10

#### Variant sweep r4-10: fallback that reinterprets an unsupported value as text

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 4. Source pattern (shared root of L7-4 / L7-10,
not re-reported): **a conversion meets a value it cannot represent and, instead of failing,
substitutes text (or null / an empty default) that then travels on as if it were the data.**

For every inventory row the question is: does a conversion here have a fallback branch
(`_ =>`, `unwrap_or*`, `py_repr`, `to_string`, a sentinel string) that is reachable with a
value the target format cannot hold, and does the run then continue as if the value were
valid?

Evidence key: **R** = reproduced in a private copy (native test `sweep_r4_10`, appended to
`src/runtimes/mod.rs` in a temp copy, shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, copy deleted afterwards);
**CP** = code path unambiguous; **known** = already reported, not re-reported.

##### Result

Two new candidates (S10-1, S10-2). Everything else holds or is a known finding.

| Id | Candidate | Evidence | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| S10-1 | Python `to_json` dispatches on `type_name()`, which for a class instance is the script-chosen class name; the builtin branches then fall back with `unwrap_or_default` / `map_or(Null)`. An instance of a class named `str`, `bool`, `list`, `dict`, `float`, `NoneType` leaves the sandbox as `""`, `false`, `[]`, `{}`, `null`, `null` (data and attributes discarded), also inside `icp.call` args, and the call is sent | R | Low |
| S10-2 | Non-finite Candid `float32`/`float64` reply values become the strings `"NaN"`, `"inf"`, `"-inf"` (`candid_bridge::f64_json`). The tool description and README document strings only for nat/int, so scripts treat them as numbers: JS `x > 1e308` is `false` and `x + 1` is `"inf1"`; Python `y * 2` is `"NaNNaN"`; Rhai `r[0] + 1` is `"inf1"`; all three runs report Ok | R | Medium |

###### S10-1 reproduction (Python, MockBridge)

| Script | Result |
|---|---|
| `class str:\n    pass\nstr()` | `Ok("")` |
| `class bool:\n    pass\nbool()` | `Ok(false)` |
| `class list: ...` / `class dict: ...` | `Ok([])` / `Ok({})` |
| `class float: ...` / `class NoneType: ...` | `Ok(null)` / `Ok(null)` |
| `class bool:` with `self.v = True`; `{'approved': bool(), 'amount': 5}` | `Ok({"amount":5,"approved":false})` |
| `class str:` holding `self.s = s`; `icp.call(L, 'icrc1_balance_of', {'owner': str('bob')})` | call **sent** with `{"owner": ""}`; run Ok |
| `class str: pass`; `icp.call(L, str())` | call sent with method `""` (the `host()` TypeError signature check is bypassed) |
| Control: `class Thing: pass; Thing()` | `Ok("Thing()")` (the known L7-6 repr path) |

Root: `src/runtimes/python.rs:67-99` matches on `o.type_name()`; monty-types
`graph.rs:546-580` returns `class.name` for `MontyNode::ClassInstance`. The `"str"`
(`as_str().unwrap_or_default()`), `"bool"` (`as_bool().unwrap_or_default()`), `"float"`
(`map_or(Value::Null, ..)`), list/tuple/set/frozenset (`items().unwrap_or_default()`) and
`"dict"` (`pairs().unwrap_or_default()`) branches assume the node kind matches the name.
`"bytes"`/`"bytearray"` fall to `py_repr` (no MontyNode for bytearray exists, so the
`bytearray` arm is reachable only through a class of that name). Fix: dispatch on
`monty_types::unstable::node(o)` (the node kind), and make every non-matching case an error.

###### S10-2 reproduction

`Service::parse("service : { f : () -> (float64, float32) query }")`, reply bytes
`(inf, NaN)` encoded with `IDLArgs::to_bytes_with_types`, decoded by `decode_reply` to
`["inf","NaN"]`, then fed to each runtime by a bridge that returns it:

| Runtime | Script | Result |
|---|---|---|
| JS | `const [x, y] = await icp.call(...); return {gt: x > 1e308, sum: x + 1, typ: typeof x, nan: Number.isNaN(y), y2: y * 2}` | `Ok({"gt":false,"sum":"inf1","typ":"string","nan":false,"y2":null})` |
| Python | `x, y = icp.call(...)`; `{'typ': type(x).__name__, 'sum': x + '1', 'rep': y * 2}` | `Ok({"typ":"str","sum":"inf1","rep":"NaNNaN"})`; `x > 0` raises TypeError (loud) |
| Rhai | `#{typ: type_of(r[0]), sum: r[0] + 1}` | `Ok({"typ":"string","sum":"inf1"})` |

The strings were chosen deliberately (register #39: so the value can be sent back, and
`float()` parses them), but nothing tells the script or the AI model: TOOL_DESCRIPTION
(`src/mcp.rs:81`) and README.md:358-359 list only nat/int as possibly-string numbers. A
typed float field changes JSON type depending on its value. Fix: document it in both
places (or return a tagged value), and add the case to the tool description's value list.

##### Grid (every inventory row against the pattern)

### grid-sweep-r4-11

#### Variant sweep r4-11

Pattern: "Map conversion where distinct keys collapse to one without error (same pattern as
L7-14, different code)." Stated both ways: (a) two distinct source keys map to one target key
and one value is lost; (b) one source key is taken by two distinct target keys, so the
script cannot address them separately.

Method: code reading at `295d64b` of every place a keyed structure crosses a boundary
(`grep` for `Map`, `BTreeMap`, `BTreeSet`, `insert`, `from_iter`, `field_value`,
`key_matches` over `src/` and `demo_store/src/`), plus scratch tests in a private copy
(`cargo test --lib sweep_r4_11`, shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/audit-target`,
copy deleted afterwards). R = reproduced, C = code path.

Result: three new candidates (SW11-1, SW11-2, SW11-3). Known hits: L7-14 (record decode),
L7-7 (Python non-str dict keys), L7-13 (aliases for one id field).

| Row | Keyed conversion | Can distinct keys collapse? | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| B6 `idl_to_json` record (`candid_bridge.rs:344-349`) | `label_name` -> `Map::insert` | yes: `"1"` (Named) and `1` (Id) | **known** L7-14 |
| B6 `idl_to_json` variant (`candid_bridge.rs:352`) | `label_name(&f.id)` as the single key | yes: `variant { "1" : text; 1 : text }`, reply `"1" = "named"` -> `{"1":"named"}`, reply `1 = "id"` -> `{"1":"id"}` (R) | **SW11-2** |
| B5 `json_to_idl` variant tag lookup (`candid_bridge.rs:283-287`) | `label_name == tag` first match in field order | yes: tag `"1"` always selects the Id arm; the named reply above, passed back, is sent as `variant { 1 = "named" }` (R) | **SW11-2** (encode half) |
| B5 `json_to_idl` record object (`candid_bridge.rs:255-265`, `key_matches`/`field_value` `:136-149`) | each field scans the JSON keys; matching is not exclusive | yes, direction (b): `record { "1" : text; 1 : text }` given `{"1":"x"}` sends both fields `"x"`; `record { "01" : nat; 1 : nat }` given `{"01":7}` sends both `7`, and given `{"01":7,"1":9}` sends both `7` and drops `9` with no error; same for `"_1_"` (R). The unknown-key check passes because every key matches some field | **SW11-1** (distinct from L7-13: one key filling several fields, not several keys for one field; shares its root `key_matches`) |
| B5 `json_to_idl` tuple / `is_tuple` (`candid_bridge.rs:130-132, 247-254`) | positional | no: requires ids 0..n-1, no Named | holds |
| B5 `json_to_idl` func object (`candid_bridge.rs:221-230`) | `get("principal")`, `get("method")` | no collapse (extra keys are ignored, a different pattern) | holds for this pattern |
| B5 variant object with several keys | `o.len() == 1` guard | refused | holds |
| B8 JS -> JSON (Boa `JsValue::to_json`, `boa_engine-0.22.0 src/value/conversions/serde_json.rs` keys via `to_std_string_escaped`, `map.insert`) | JS property key -> Rust `String` | yes: keys `"\uD800"` (lone surrogate) and `"\\uD800"` (six characters) are two properties in JS (`Object.keys(o).length` = 4 for two such pairs) and one key after conversion; result `{"\\uD800":2,"a\\uDC00":4}`; the same object as an `icp.call` argument is sent as `{"\\uD800":"text"}`, run Ok (R) | **SW11-3** (symptom of L7-10's root cause; merge candidate) |
| B8 JSON -> JS (`JsValue::from_json`, `js.rs:403`) | JSON key -> JS property key | no: string keys map one-to-one | holds |
| B9 Python -> JSON dict (`python.rs:89-96`) | non-str keys `py_repr`'d | yes: `{True:1,'True':2}`, `{None:1,'None':2}`, `{b'a':1,"b'a'":2}`, `{(1,2):1,'(1, 2)':2}` each leave as one key (R) | **known** L7-7 (same root, wider key types than its `{1,'1'}` example) |
| B9 Python str keys with surrogates | `'\ud800'`, `'\ud801'` | they become one key, but inside Monty already: `len({'\ud800':1,'\ud801':2})` = 1 and `'\ud800' == '\ud801'` is True (R); the conversion itself is one-to-one | holds for this pattern (Monty lexer, not a boundary conversion) |
| B9 JSON -> Python (`python.rs:115`) | JSON key -> `str` | no | holds |
| B10 Rhai -> JSON map (`rhai_rt.rs:102-109`) | `rhai::Map` key (Rust string) -> `String` | no: keys are already UTF-8 strings, one-to-one (R: `#{"a":1,"b":2}` round trip) | holds |
| B10 JSON -> Rhai (`rhai::serde::to_dynamic`, `rhai_rt.rs:76`) | JSON key -> `rhai::Map` key | no | holds |
| B1 / U3 `parse_body` (serde_json `Value`) | JSON object with repeated identical keys: last wins | identical keys, not distinct ones; RFC 8259 leaves duplicates undefined; body is from a token holder only (C) | out of pattern, holds |
| U2 `authenticate` headers (`mcp.rs:274-279`) | first `Authorization` header (case-insensitive name) | list scan, not a map conversion (C) | holds |
| B16 search `types` map (`search.rs:135-138`) | type names from `TypeEnv` (unique) | no | holds |
| B16 search `methods` (`search.rs:103-110`) | service method names (candid_parser rejects duplicates) | no | holds |
| B4 principal keys: D2 `ALLOWLIST` (`Principal`), D5 overrides, V2/V4/V5 caches, `touched` (`to_text()` of a parsed principal) | canonical text | different spellings of one principal collapse by design (CL23) (C) | holds |
| B3 / D3 token hash keys (`policy.rs:211-232`) | trim + lowercase of hex | different spellings of one hash collapse by design; caller id = first 16 hex (64-bit prefix) collides only by chance among controller-registered tokens (C) | holds |
| B13 language names | case-insensitive, aliases | by design | holds |
| B12 stable Candid records | typed decode | no keyed collapse | holds |
| C2 demo_store | vectors only, no maps (grep) | duplicates in one order are the known oversell finding, not a key collapse | holds (known elsewhere) |
| W11 Rhai `answers` / JS `pending` / Python `queued` | sequence numbers | no | holds |

##### Candidates

- **SW11-1** `json_to_idl` record matching is not exclusive: one JSON key fills every field
  whose label it matches (`"1"` matches both `"1"` and `1`; `"01"`, `"_1_"` likewise), and a
  second key meant for the id field is dropped. R (scratch test in a copy).
- **SW11-2** Variant arms with a quoted numeric label and an id label print the same tag:
  the reply's arm is lost, and the tag always encodes as the id arm. R.
- **SW11-3** JS object keys that differ only by a lone surrogate versus its escaped spelling
  collapse to one key when the value leaves the sandbox (result or call argument). R.
  Root cause is L7-10's.

### grid-sweep-r5-0

#### Variant sweep r5-0: a limit enforced with different semantics in one runtime than its siblings

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 5. Pattern (register class L6):

> A limit enforced in one runtime (or route, build, SDK function, output channel) with
> different semantics from its siblings, or missing there.

Method: read `src/runtimes/{mod,js,python,rhai_rt}.rs`, `src/bridge.rs`, `src/lib.rs`,
`src/policy.rs`, `src/search.rs`, `src/mcp.rs:140-200, 330-410`, `demo_store/src/lib.rs` at
`295d64b` (`git archive 295d64b` into `/private/tmp/claude-501/sweep-r5-0`, deleted
afterwards, because the working tree's `src/` has someone else's uncommitted edits). I also
read `monty-types-1.6.0/src/io.rs:100-170, 279-292` and `monty-1.6.0/src/builtins/print.rs:21-84`
for Python's second output stream. For every limit row I listed each sibling that enforces
it and compared the unit counted, when the check runs, what is counted against it, and what
happens at the limit. I then checked each difference against the task's known list and
the earlier sweep and lens grids (r1-r4, L3/L6/L14/L16). Nothing was compiled or run. Every
verdict below comes from the code path (C) or cites an earlier reproduction.

Result: **no new candidate.** Each difference that fits the pattern is already a known
finding or was given a reasoned "holds" in an earlier grid that this sweep re-checked.

##### Cells

| Row | Siblings compared | Verdict | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| LIM2 instruction budget | JS (rounds, 256 jobs, console, request), Python (Monty feed/turn clock), Rhai (`on_progress` every op), bridge `reserve`, post-run check | known | Sync JS unchecked; Python soft, relative and turn-reset; snapshot vs live limits; compile and `parse_json` outside the budget; search query path unbudgeted |
| LIM2 catchability | JS budget refusal thrown from `console`/`icp.*` (`js.rs:202-205, 230, 253`) is a catchable RangeError; Rhai's is the uncatchable terminate marker (`rhai_rt.rs:148-151`) | holds | Catching it in JS lets only synchronous code continue, which is already the known "sync JS never checks the budget" finding. The run still ends at the next `check_budget` (`js.rs:376`) or job tick. Host-side `reserve` refusals are catchable in all three by design |
| LIM15 log cap | JS (skips formatting at cap, `[level] ` prefix counted), Rhai (formats, then drops; `[debug pos]` counted), Python (Monty `CollectString`, newline bytes counted, MemoryError), `LogBuf`, `tool_result` 250 KB | known | Python MemoryError; JS formats every argument; marker overshoot; empty lines; 250 KB escaped re-cut |
| LIM15, Python second stream | `print(..., file=sys.stderr)` vs stdout | holds (C) | `PrintWriter::write`/`push` send both streams through the same `CollectString` buffer and `check_print_collect_limit` (`monty-types io.rs:132-136, 159-163`), so stderr cannot get around the 64 KiB cap. JS has `console.error`/`warn` on the same counter; Rhai has `debug` on the same counter |
| LIM16 nodes / bytes / depth | JS `SNAPSHOT_JS`, Python `to_json`, Rhai `to_json_value` | known | UTF-16 vs UTF-8; JS keys unchecked; py_repr uncharged; bytes/blobs as text not elements; depth off by one; Rhai engine limits summed (SW2-3-1) |
| LIM16, scope of the budget per call | JS budgets `args` only; Python one `ValueBudget` across canister, method and args (`python.rs:243-244`); Rhai `args` only (`rhai_rt.rs:160`) | known | JS canister and method strings unbounded (known). Python's wider scope is the stricter one. Rhai strings are capped at 1 MiB by the engine |
| LIM23 code size | `LanguageRouter::execute` once for all (`mod.rs:52`) | holds | The same byte count for every language; compile costs past it are known (Boa, Rhai, Python eval/exec; Monty top-level compile is linear, r2-0 / r3-2 / r3-7) |
| LIM24 / LIM26 / LIM27 recursion | JS 256 frames, Python 200, Rhai 32 call levels | holds | Each is documented with its own number (README:370-372). The Python counter shared with export is known |
| LIM25 / LIM26 / LIM27 request counts | JS 64 per round x 64 rounds, Python 256 progress events, Rhai 64 requests | known / holds | No per-batch cap in Python (T2-1); last round dropped (SW5-1). ### grid-sweep-r5-1

#### Variant sweep r5-1: identifier re-serialised from a lossy parse instead of echoed verbatim

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 5. Pattern under test. The seed is known and not
re-reported: L7-9. serde_json reads JSON-RPC ids as f64, and the server echoes the altered
id.

> An identifier is re-serialised from a lossy parse instead of being echoed verbatim.

Generalised for the sweep: an identifier (request id, token id, principal, method name, field
or variant label, language or tool name, finding key) is parsed, normalised, truncated or
converted into a lossy form. It is then shown to a party, or used as a key, in place of the
original. As a result the shown form no longer round-trips, two identifiers collapse into
one, or one identifier appears as another.

Method: I read the code at `295d64b` (sources exported with `git show`) for every inventory
row. The library code I read: ic_principal 0.1.5 `from_text`, and Boa 0.22
`JsValue::from_json` plus `PropertyKey::from(JsString)`. There were two probes:

- **P1 (native):** a test added to `policy::tests` in a private `git archive` copy. Every
  file was touched so cargo could not reuse stale output. The run was
  `cargo test --lib sw5_probe` with the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. The copy was deleted
  afterwards.
- **P2 (node):** the audit workflow's own `keyOf`, copied verbatim into a scratch script.

Nothing was deployed, called or reconfigured. **R** = reproduced, **C** = code path.

These findings are known and not re-reported:

- L7-9 (JSON-RPC ids)
- L7-10 (lone surrogates become literal `\uXXXX`, including in method and canister strings)
- L7-14 and the json_to_idl label and variant-tag collisions
- `_n_` alias resolving to a different case
- Search labels printed in a form the converter refuses (`1_000`, `true`/`false`)
- Search `script_sha256` taken from raw spelling
- Search trims `canister_id`
- Search echoes the "not allowlisted" id in full
- Python dict keys as `py_repr`
- Python class named `str` and similar type-name dispatch
- L7-16 and L7-17, and their demo-page `pretty()` rounding (noted in L7-r1 and r4-2)
- Demo page splices the canister id into code
- `demo-setup.sh` parses human-readable output
- Audit `canister.method` labels unescaped
- Interface fetches recorded as `aaaaa-aa`
- Live refutation matched by exact title

##### New candidates

| Id | Sev | Title | Ev |
|---|---|---|---|
| SW5-1-1 | Medium | The controller sees each token only as a 16-hex hash prefix, in `get_policy` and in every audit `caller`, but `revoke_api_token_hash` accepts only the full 64-hex hash. The identifier the operator can see does not revoke anything (returns `false`). A token whose full hash was not saved outside the canister cannot be revoked without a reinstall or new code | R (P1) |
| SW5-1-2 | Medium | The audit workflow keys findings by `(location + '|' + root_cause).toLowerCase().slice(0, 160)`. Two different confirmed findings that share a long location, or a 160-character prefix, collapse into one key. The second is dropped without being listed as confirmed or refuted, and the round counts as dry | R (P2) |

###### SW5-1-1 detail

- **Where:**
  - `src/policy.rs:221-223`. `list_tokens` returns `e.key()[..16]` and the label.
  - `src/lib.rs:336-345`. `get_policy` exposes that list as `PolicyView.tokens`, and
    `icp_code_mode.did` documents it as "(token hash prefix, label)".
  - `src/lib.rs:122, 222`. The audit `caller` is `caller_hash.get(..16)`.
  - `src/policy.rs:217-219` and `src/lib.rs:317`. `revoke_token_hash` removes only an exact,
    trimmed, lowercased 64-hex key.
  - The full hash is returned nowhere: the .did shows no other method that reads `TOKENS`.
- **Repro (P1):** `add_token_hash(sha256("leaked-token"), "laptop")`, then take
  `list_tokens()`. The output was
  `SW5 shown=d1737c1fb291d3a7 len=16 label=laptop` and then
  `SW5 revoke(shown)=false still_valid=true`.
- **Why it matters:**
  - README.md:459-462 tells operators to treat tokens as revocable credentials and to revoke
    them "when in doubt".
  - The natural trigger for doubt is an audit entry or a `get_policy` row, and both name the
    token only by this prefix.
  - The README's setup flow (README.md:53-54, 144-148) computes the hash inline in a shell
    command and never stores it. The operator therefore has the full hash only while the
    plaintext token is still at hand.
  - For a lost client or a leaked token, nothing the canister returns can be used to revoke
    it. A reinstall would also wipe D1-D5, including the audit log, and `post_upgrade` args
    cannot remove a token (only add one).
  - The canister never shows the prefix anywhere a non-controller can see it, and a hash of
    a 256-bit random token is not sensitive. The truncation therefore protects nothing that
    a controller-only view needs to hide.
- **Refute attempts:**
  - (a) Collision safety of the 64-bit prefix was assessed by L10-r1 and holds. That is a
    different question: it concerns telling tokens apart, not using the id as input.
  - (b) An operator who still has every plaintext can recompute hashes. That fails exactly in
    the leak or loss case the README cites.
  - (c) No prefix-match path exists: `revoke_token_hash` uses `remove(&key)` on a
    `StableBTreeMap`, exact match only.
- **Fix:** one of:
  - return the full 64-hex hash in `PolicyView.tokens` (and optionally in the audit
    `caller`);
  - accept a unique prefix of 16 or more hex characters in `revoke_api_token_hash`, refusing
    an ambiguous prefix;
  - add a `revoke_api_token_label`.

  Then document the chosen form in the .did. Add a test that revokes using exactly what
  `get_policy` lists.

###### SW5-1-2 detail

- **Where:** `.claude/workflows/audit.js:177` (`keyOf`), used for deduplication at `:213-216`
  (`absorb`) and at `:291` (Live). In `absorb`, a confirmed verdict whose key is already in
  `seen` takes `continue`. It is not added to `confirmed` or to `refuted`, and nothing is
  logged.
- **Repro (P2):** I copied `keyOf` and the `absorb` loop verbatim and ran four confirmed
  verdicts through them:
  - A and B: same 172-character location (`src/bridge.rs:470-506 (IcBridge::candid), ...
    README.md:441`), different root causes;
  - C and D: same short location, and root causes that share their first 151 characters.

  The output was `confirmed: A,C`. B and D vanish.
- **Effect:**
  - Once the location string alone is 159 characters or more, the root cause is ignored
    entirely. Every later finding at that location (one multi-site location or a long list
    of `file:line`) is dropped.
  - `fresh` is computed from the same check, so a round whose only new finding collapsed
    counts toward the two-dry-rounds stopping rule (PLAN.md section 9).
  - The `seen` keys handed to later reviewers ("Already reported") are the same truncated
    strings, so the dropped finding is also hidden from the people who might find it again.
  - This is the same family as known SW4-6-2: the report silently loses a finding and the
    stopping rule is advanced. The root is different: SW4-6-2 is a missing agent output,
    while this is a lossy key derived from free text instead of a stable identifier.
- **Refute attempts:**
  - (a) Verifiers merge duplicates. However, two verifiers in different lenses or sweeps never
    see each other's output, so cross-agent duplicates are exactly what `keyOf` must
    separate, and it cannot tell them apart from distinct findings.
  - (b) Lower-casing is harmless; the truncation is the cause.
  - (c) r4-6 noted this site "for the critic" but returned no candidate.
- **Fix:**
  - Key on a stable identifier: the verifier's own id, or a hash of the full untruncated
    `location|root_cause`.
  - Log, rather than drop, a verdict whose key matches. Record it as "merged into <title>"
    so a near-duplicate stays visible in the report.

### grid-sweep-r5-2

#### Variant sweep r5-2: unrepresentable value replaced by a look-alike

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 5. Pattern (shared root of L7-4 / L7-6, not
re-reported):

> A value the target format cannot hold is replaced by an escaped or substitute look-alike
> (null, a repr string, literal escape text, an empty or index-keyed object) instead of an
> error.

Prior sweeps r4-2, r4-8 and r4-10 covered this root. This round looked for value classes and
rows they did not name. Known and not re-reported: L7-1, L7-2, L7-4, L7-5, L7-6, L7-7, L7-9,
L7-10, L7-11, L7-12, L7-14, L7-16, L7-16b, L7-17, L6-9, S10-1, S10-2, SW4-8-1, SW4-8-2,
SW4-2-1/2/3, SW3-9-1, the boxed-primitive and README:369 placeholder findings, demo_store
`restock` saturation, and the `reserved` wrap.

Evidence: **R** = reproduced natively. The copy was a `git archive 295d64b` with no
`target/` and none of the uncommitted test additions in the working tree. Its package
version was set to `0.1.0-sweepr52`. It was built with the shared
`CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/audit-target`, the probe ran as a throw-away test
module `runtimes::sweep_r5_2` with MockBridge, and the copy was deleted afterwards. **C** =
the code path is unambiguous. No live canister was touched.

Note on the tree: the working tree has uncommitted test-only additions in `src/` and
`demo_store/` (insertions inside `mod tests` / `mod mock`, no deletions). Non-test line
numbers match `295d64b`, so every reference below is valid for the audited commit.

##### Candidate

###### SW5-2-1 (Low). JS byte containers have no blob form: Uint8Array leaves as an index-keyed object, ArrayBuffer/DataView as `{}`, and the run reports Ok

**Where.** `SNAPSHOT_JS` (`src/runtimes/js.rs:68-82`) recognises only `Array.isArray` values
as arrays. A typed array passes `typeof x === "object"`, fails `isArray`, and is walked as a
plain object. Its own enumerable keys are its indices, so `Uint8Array [1,2]` becomes
`{"0":1,"1":2}`. `ArrayBuffer` and `DataView` have no own enumerable keys, so they become
`{}` and their bytes are dropped. The blob rule elsewhere in the system is "array of
numbers": Candid blob replies come back as arrays (`candid_bridge.rs:338`), Python `bytes`
and Rhai blobs are exported as arrays (`python.rs:79-83`, `rhai_rt.rs:93-96`), and the tool
description says "blobs are byte arrays or hex strings" (`src/mcp.rs:75`).

**R (native, MockBridge):**

| Script | Result |
|---|---|
| JS `return new Uint8Array([1,2,255])` | `Ok({"0":1,"1":2,"2":255})` |
| JS `return new Uint8Array([1,2]).buffer` | `Ok({})`: the bytes are gone |
| JS `return new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(4))` | `Ok({})` |
| JS `return {hash: new Uint8Array([7,8])}` | `Ok({"hash":{"0":7,"1":8}})` |
| JS `return Array.from(new Uint8Array([7,8]))` (control) | `Ok([7,8])` |
| JS `icp.call(L,'icrc1_balance_of',{owner:'aaaaa-aa', subaccount: new Uint8Array(2)})` | the mock records `{"subaccount":{"0":0,"1":0}}`; `encode_args` against `record { owner : principal; subaccount : opt blob }` gives `argument 0: .subaccount: expected array, got object` (loud) |
| same with `new Uint8Array(2).buffer` | the mock records `{"subaccount":{}}`; encode gives the same error (loud) |
| Python `icp.call(..., {'owner':'aaaaa-aa','subaccount':bytes(2)})` | sends `[0,0]`, encodes Ok |
| Rhai `let b = blob(3, 1); b` | `Ok([1,1,1])` |

**Impact.** Results are where the substitution is silent. A JS script that returns bytes it
built (a typed array, or its `.buffer`) hands the model an index-keyed object, or `{}` with
the data lost, while the run is audited Ok. The same script in Python or Rhai returns an
array, against "identical semantics in every language" (`src/mcp.rs:79`, shown to the AI).
In call arguments the result is a loud refusal, but its text, "expected array, got object",
contradicts the description the AI was given ("blobs are byte arrays"), because
`Uint8Array` is JavaScript's byte array.

**Refutation tried.** Is this just `JSON.stringify` semantics, already accepted for `Map ->
{}` and grouped under L6-9? For `ArrayBuffer`/`DataView` -> `{}`, yes: it is the same drop
as `Map`, and the verifier may merge it into L6-9. The Uint8Array case is a different value
class from L6-9's examples (functions, undefined, Map). The system has its own
representation for exactly this value (the blob array), and the sibling runtimes use it.
No known finding names byte containers. Args are not silent, so this is graded Low.

**Fix.** In the snapshot, convert `ArrayBuffer.isView(x)` (typed arrays; DataView by its
bytes) and `ArrayBuffer` values to plain arrays of their bytes before the object rule,
counting each element against `MAXN`. Alternatively, refuse them with a TypeError that says
to use `Array.from`. Mention typed arrays in the tool description's blob sentence.
Regression test: JS `return new Uint8Array([1,2])` returns `[1,2]` (or fails), and the
same value as an `opt blob` argument encodes.

### grid-sweep-r5-3

#### Variant sweep r5-3: supplied data silently discarded by a permissive type

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 5. Pattern (seed: lenient coercion in `json_to_idl`,
with L7-5 / L7-12 / L7-13, all known and not re-reported):

> Supplied data is silently discarded because the receiving type or signature is
> permissive: an extra argument, key, field or entry is accepted and dropped, and the
> operation reports success.

Method: code reading at `295d64b` of every place an input from a script, a client, an
operator or a target is mapped onto a fixed shape (function arity, record/func object, map
entry, Candid record): `src/candid_bridge.rs` (B5/B6), `src/runtimes/{js,python,rhai_rt}.rs`
host functions and converters (E16-E19, B8-B10), `src/mcp.rs` (U3-U5, B1, B11, B13),
`src/search.rs`, `src/lib.rs` `apply` and admin methods (E1/E2, E6-E14), `src/policy.rs`
setters, `demo_store/src/lib.rs`. The working tree has uncommitted test-only additions
(`git diff -U0 HEAD` hunks are all inside `mod tests`/`mod mock`); production code equals
`295d64b`. Probes ran in a private `git archive HEAD` copy
(`/private/tmp/claude-501/sweep-r5-3.xLJ4`, deleted afterwards) with
`CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/audit-target`,
`cargo test --lib sweep_r5_3 -- --nocapture`. R = reproduced, C = code path.

##### Probes

- P1 (`runtimes::sweep_r5_3::extra_call_args`, `MockBridge`, R):
  - JS `icp.call(L, 'icrc1_balance_of', {owner:'aaaaa-aa'}, {subaccount:[1,2]}, 'memo')`:
    one call recorded with args `{"owner":"aaaaa-aa"}`, run `Ok`.
  - JS `icp.call(L, 'icrc1_balance_of', undefined, {owner:'aaaaa-aa'})`: call recorded with
    args `null`, run `Ok`.
  - Python, same four arguments: `TypeError: icp.call(canister_id: str, method: str, args=None)`,
    no call.
  - Rhai, same four arguments: `Function not found: icp::call_canister (.., map, map)`, no call.
  - JS `icp.candid(L, 'extra')`: accepted (harmless: no data in the extra argument).
- P2 (`candid_bridge::sweep_r5_3::func_object_extra_keys`, R): against `func (nat) -> (text)`,
  `{"principal":"aaaaa-aa","method":"m","args":[1,2,3],"n":5}` and
  `{"principal":"aaaaa-aa","method":"m","cycles":1000000}` both encode as
  `func "aaaaa-aa".m`. The same extra key on a record (`{"cb":..,"x":1}`) is refused with
  `unknown record field `x``; a func object nested in that record accepts `"n":7` and drops it.
- P3 (`sweep_r5_3::init_args_duplicate_allowlist`, R): `apply(InitArgs { allowlist:
  [(ledger, ["icrc1_balance_of"]), (ledger, ["icrc1_symbol"])] })` leaves the allowlist as
  `[(ledger, ["icrc1_symbol"])]`; no error, install would succeed.

##### New candidates

###### SW5-3-1 (Medium): JS `icp.call` silently drops arguments after the third and sends the call

`request_fn` (`src/runtimes/js.rs:250-273`) takes `args.get(2)` as the call arguments and
ignores the rest. `icp.call(L, 'icrc1_balance_of', {owner}, {subaccount})` sends
`{owner}` alone (for an ICRC ledger: the default-subaccount balance, reported Ok);
`icp.call(L, m, undefined, x)` sends `null`. Python raises `TypeError` and Rhai
"Function not found" for the same four-argument call, so the tool description's
"identical semantics in every language" (CL29, shown to the AI) does not hold. Reproduced
natively with `MockBridge` (P1). Fix: refuse `args.len() > 3` (and `> 1` for
`icp.candid`) with a `TypeError`, matching Python.

###### SW5-3-2 (Low): `json_to_idl` func objects accept and drop unknown keys

`candid_bridge.rs:223-226` reads only `principal` and `method` from an object; any other
key is discarded, while records refuse unknown keys. Reproduced (P2), including a func
nested inside a record. Fix: refuse an object whose keys are not exactly
`principal`/`method`.

###### SW5-3-3 (Low): duplicate principals in `InitArgs.allowlist` replace each other silently

`apply` (`src/lib.rs:43-45`) calls `policy::set_allowed` per entry, an overwriting insert,
so only the last method list for a principal survives install or upgrade. Reproduced (P3).
Fails closed. Fix: merge or refuse duplicates in `apply` (trap, like a bad token hash).

### grid-sweep-r5-4

#### Variant sweep r5-4: lenient parser accepting malformed input as a valid value

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 5. Pattern:

> A lenient parser accepts malformed input as a valid value.

Known and not repeated: L7-12 (stray `_`, repeated `0x`, plus the `+` spellings merged in
r4-9), L7-13 (aliased record id keys), L7-11 (null/reserved slots take any value), L7-5
(float text `inf`/`infinity`/underflow), L7-9 (JSON-RPC id forms), L7-15 (`[]` for one opt vec),
the inputSchema finding (unknown keys, `language: null`, aliases), whitespace-padded search
`canister_id`, opt-typed admin args decoded as null, duplicate JSON keys (last wins, noted under
L7-9), the `_n_` / quoted-number variant tag finding, Python repr fallbacks, JS dropping
unrepresentable values.

`parse_body`, `classify`, `parse_tool_call`, `opt_string`, `demo_page`), `runtimes/mod.rs`
(`Language::from_str`), `policy.rs` (`add_token_hash`, `revoke_token_hash`, `authorize`),
`lib.rs` (`apply`, `inspect_message`, admin endpoints, `run_search`), `search.rs` (`scope`,
`keywords`), `bridge.rs` (`parse_principal`, `fetch_did`, `candid`, `call`), `candid_bridge.rs`
(`Service::parse`, `encode_args`, `json_to_idl`, `decode_reply`), the three runtimes' host
functions, `demo_store` endpoints, `src/demo.html`, `scripts/demo-setup.sh`, `video/*.mjs`.
Dependency parsers read at source: `ic_principal-0.1.5` `Principal::from_text`,
`candid-0.10.40` `Nat/Int::parse`, `IDLArgs::from_bytes_with_types_with_config` + `done()`,
`candid_parser-0.4.1` `check_prog` / `check_meths` / `check_defs`.

Probes: native, private copy (no `target/`, `design/`, `.env`, uncommitted plan doc),
`CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/audit-target`, throwaway test modules in
`src/candid_bridge.rs`, `cargo test --lib sweep_r5_4`; copy deleted afterwards.

##### New candidate

**SW5-4-1 (Low): `set_candid_override` accepts `.did` text with `import` declarations and
silently ignores them, so imported methods disappear.** `Service::parse`
(`src/candid_bridge.rs:34-46`) uses `candid_parser::check_prog`, which skips
`Dec::ImportType` / `Dec::ImportServ` (`candid_parser-0.4.1/src/typing.rs:144`). Imports are
resolved only by the file-based `check_file` (`typing.rs:302-303`). A standalone text cannot
resolve them, so this text is incomplete, yet the parse succeeds. Reproduced natively:
`Service::parse("import service \"ledger.did\";\nservice : { local_m : () -> () }")` returns Ok
with methods `["local_m"]`, and `method("icrc1_transfer")` gives
`` method `icrc1_transfer` is not declared in the target's candid interface ``.
`import "/etc/passwd";\nservice : { m : () -> () }` also parses. Only when an imported *type*
is referenced does it fail (`Unbound type identifier Account`). `set_candid_override`
(`src/lib.rs:316-325`) uses this parse as its validation and returns `Ok(())`. The stored text
still shows the `import` line through `icp.candid`, while search lists only the local methods
and calls to imported methods are refused with a message saying they are not declared.
Effect: an operator is misled and the AI model sees an interface that does not match what
calls accept. No wrong value is sent. The failure is a refusal, so the grade is Low.
Fixed-interface fetches are unaffected in practice, because compiled `candid:service`
sections contain no imports. Fix: in `Service::parse`, refuse any `Dec::ImportType` /
`Dec::ImportServ` in `prog.decs` ("imports are not supported; inline the imported
definitions").

Refute attempts: checked `check_prog` for an error on unresolved imports (none: the arm is
`=> ()`); checked that `check_meths` and `check_defs` reject the other malformed forms
(duplicates: refused in the parser; trailing declarations after the service: parse error, R).

### grid-sweep-r5-5

#### Variant sweep r5-5: several input spellings mapped to one slot without a collision check

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 5. Pattern:

> Several input spellings mapped to one slot without a collision check (residual of
> register #35).

Generalised for the sweep: wherever two or more distinct inputs (aliases, case or
whitespace variants, escape forms, stringified keys, sentinel values) are normalised into
one key, label, map entry or meaning, check whether the code detects two of them meeting
(or a sentinel meeting a literal) and refuses, or silently keeps one.

Method: read at `HEAD` (`git show HEAD:`; the working tree carries uncommitted test
additions in `src/` and `demo_store/` that are not part of the audited commit) every
normalisation site: `key_matches`/`field_value`/variant tag lookup/`label_name`
(`src/candid_bridge.rs`), `num_text`, blob hex, `Principal::from_text` uses
(`src/bridge.rs`, `src/search.rs`, `src/policy.rs`), `authorize` (`src/policy.rs:170-190`),
`add_token_hash`/`revoke_token_hash`/`verify_token`, `InitArgs` `apply`, `authenticate`
(header, scheme, path), `parse_body`/`classify`/`parse_tool_call` (`src/mcp.rs`),
`Language::from_str`, `run_search` audit key, Python `to_json`/`from_json`/`host`, Rhai
`to_json_value`/`request` replay comparison, JS `arg_string`/`SNAPSHOT_JS`/Boa
`JsValue::from_json` (boa_engine 0.22 `value/conversions/serde_json.rs:68-79`,
`property/mod.rs:695-699`), `search::render` maps, demo_store lookups, demo page builders.
Native probes in a private `git archive HEAD` copy (`/private/tmp/claude-501/sweep-r5-5.*`,
shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/audit-target`, `cargo test --lib` with
probe tests added to the copy only; 57 HEAD tests + probe, so the HEAD tree was built).
Copy deleted. Nothing deployed; the local network was not touched.

Evidence: R = reproduced (native test), C = code path. "known" = in the do-not-re-report
list given to this sweep.
