### grid-sweep-r5-6

#### Variant sweep r5-6

Pattern: "Map conversion where distinct keys collapse to one without error (same pattern as
L7-7)". Read as: a keyed structure crosses a boundary (or is normalised into a store), and
two keys that are distinct on the source side become one key on the target side, so one
value is lost or overwritten with no error. Identical keys (same canonical text) are out of
pattern.

Builds on grid-sweep-r4-11 (same pattern via L7-14), which already found SW11-1, SW11-2 and
SW11-3; those are in the known list and are not re-reported.

Method: code reading at `295d64b` of every keyed conversion and keyed store (`grep` for
`insert`, `BTreeMap`, `BTreeSet`, `Map::new`, `to_lowercase`, `eq_ignore`, `trim` over `src/`,
`src/runtimes/`, `demo_store/src/`, plus `src/demo.html` object maps), Boa 0.22.0
`value/conversions/serde_json.rs` and monty-types 1.6.0 `object.rs` accessors, and one
scratch test in a private copy (`cargo test --lib sweep_r5_6`, shared
`CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/audit-target`, copy deleted afterwards).
R = reproduced, C = code path.

Result: no new candidate.

| Row | Keyed conversion / store | Can distinct keys collapse? | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| B8 JS -> JSON, canonical-index keys (`SNAPSHOT_JS` `put` via `defineProperty`, Boa `to_json` index keys then shape keys) | `"1"`, `"01"`, `"1.0"`, `" 1"`, `"1e0"`, `"-0"`, `"4294967294"`, `"4294967295"`, `"__proto__"`, `"constructor"` on one object | no: `Object.keys` = 10 and the result and the `icp.call` argument both carry 10 keys (R) | holds |
| B8 JS arrays with string-index props | `a["1"]` is the same element as `a[1]` inside JS; `a["01"]` dropped | not a collapse (non-index array props are dropped, a different pattern) (R) | out of pattern |
| B8 JS Unicode-equivalent keys | `"é"` (NFC) vs `"é"` (NFD) | no normalisation: 2 keys out (R) | holds |
| B8 JS lone-surrogate vs escaped spelling | Boa `to_std_string_escaped` | yes | known (SW11-3) |
| B8 JSON -> JS (`JsValue::from_json`, `js.rs:403`) | JSON keys are unique UTF-8 strings -> UTF-16 | no (C) | holds |
| B9 Python -> JSON, `str` keys (`python.rs:89-96`, `as_str` = `MontyNode::String` only) | `'1'`, `'01'`, `' 1'` | no: 3 keys out (R) | holds |
| B9 Python -> JSON, non-`str` keys | `py_repr`; also Monty prints a 1-tuple key `(1,)` as `"(1)"`, so `{(1,):..,'(1)':..}` collides | yes (R) | known (L7-7, same root) |
| B9 class instances / modules (`pairs()` returns attrs) | attribute names unique per instance | no; class-name dispatch is S10-1 | known elsewhere |
| B9 JSON -> Python (`from_json`) | JSON keys -> `str` | no (C) | holds |
| B10 Rhai -> JSON (`rhai_rt.rs:102-109`) | `rhai::Map` keys are Rust strings | no: `"1"`, `"01"`, `" 1"`, NFC/NFD `é` -> 5 keys out (R) | holds |
| B10 JSON -> Rhai (`to_dynamic`) | one-to-one | no (C) | holds |
| B5 `json_to_idl` record / variant | `key_matches` / tag lookup | yes | known (L7-13, SW11-1, SW11-2) |
| B6 `idl_to_json` record / variant | `label_name` | yes | known (L7-14, SW11-2) |

### grid-sweep-r5-7

#### Variant sweep r5-7: ambiguous input shape resolved differently from the documented rule

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 5. Pattern:

> An input whose shape admits more than one reading is resolved by the code (or by a
> documented recipe) in a way the documented rule does not say, so the same value means
> different things on different paths.

Seeds (known, not re-reported): L7-15 (`[]` for one `opt vec` argument), the single-argument
`[x]` heuristic, the `_n_` / quoted-number variant tag finding, L7-13 (aliased record keys),
L7-11 (null/reserved slots), L7-16 (raw string results), register #42 (opt opt; also opt
null / opt reserved, per grid-L7-r1), the inputSchema finding (non-object `arguments`,
`language: null`, aliases), whitespace-padded / invalid search `canister_id`.

Method. Code read at `295d64b` from a `git archive` copy (the working tree's `src/` carries
someone else's uncommitted test additions; non-test lines are unchanged). Every place a
caller, script, operator, target or developer supplies a value whose shape is open to more
than one reading was listed, and the reading the code takes was compared with the README,
the `.did`, the tool descriptions shown to the AI and the code comments. Probes were run
natively in `/private/tmp/claude-501/sweep-r5-7.*` (shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, every source
touched first so nothing stale was reused; `cargo test --lib`), and with `sh`/`node` for the
two tooling rows. The copy was deleted afterwards. No deployment, no live request.

Evidence: **R** reproduced here; **C** the code path produces it unambiguously; **known** in
the task's known list; **r5-N** found by another round-5 sweep (not repeated).

##### New candidates

| Id | Sev | Rows | Summary | Ev |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SW5-7-1 | Low | B6, B5, CL (README:354, `SEARCH_DESCRIPTION` `src/mcp.rs:75`) | A record whose labels are 0..n-1 (a Candid tuple, e.g. ICRC-1 `icrc1_metadata`'s `vec record { text; Value }`) leaves the bridge as a JSON **array**; a record with numeric labels that are not contiguous leaves as an **object** keyed `"0"`, `"2"`. README ("Records are objects") and the search description shown to the AI ("records are objects") state one rule; the code applies a second, undocumented one on output, while input accepts both forms | R |
| SW5-7-2 | Low | E1/E2, AD1, AD5, CL (`icp_code_mode.did:61`, `src/lib.rs:20`) | The token-hash recipe in the `.did` and `InitArgs` doc, `echo -n "$TOKEN" \| shasum -a 256`, depends on the shell. Under POSIX `sh` (macOS `/bin/sh`, every `make` recipe) `-n` is printed as text, so the digest is of `-n TOKEN\n`. The canister accepts it (it is 64 hex) and the token then gets 401. The README uses `printf %s` and gets the right digest. The recipe also omits `cut -d' ' -f1`, so pasting its output whole (`<hex>  -`) into `InitArgs` traps the install (F1) | R |
| SW5-7-3 | Low | C12, D10, U16, E28 | The two `.env` readers in `video/` resolve a quoted value differently. `tts.mjs:11` strips quotes from `GEMINI_API_KEY="…"`; `capture-demo.mjs:7` keeps them in `MCP_TOKEN="…"`, writes `"…"` (with quotes) into the page's localStorage, every MCP request is 401, and the script still writes screenshots and `demo-results.json` of the error state and exits 0. It also ignores `process.env.MCP_TOKEN`, which the README's quick start exports | R (parsers), C (401 path) |

###### SW5-7-1 details

- Where: `src/candid_bridge.rs:339-350` (`idl_to_json`: tuple test `Unnamed(n)|Id(n) if n == i`
  for every field, else an object keyed by `label_name`). Input side `:256-273` accepts an
  array (tuple only) or an object keyed `"0"`, `"_0_"`. Docs: README.md:353-354 ("How values
  are encoded: Records are objects"), `SEARCH_DESCRIPTION` (`src/mcp.rs:75`, shown to the AI:
  "records are objects"). `TOOL_DESCRIPTION` says nothing about records.
- Repro (native, copy of 295d64b): interface
  `type R = record { text; nat }; type S = record { 0 : text; 2 : nat }; service : { f : (R, S) -> () }`.
  `encode_args("f", [{"0":"a","1":1}, {"0":"b","2":2}])` is accepted (records given as
  objects, as documented). Decoding the same bytes as a reply gives `[["a",1],{"0":"b","2":2}]`.
  `S` given as an array is refused ("expected record object, got array").
- Effect: a script that follows the documented rule and reads a tuple record by key gets the
  wrong type. In Python, `m["0"]` on a reply element is a `TypeError` (it is a list); in Rhai,
  map access on an array is an error; JS `m["0"]` happens to work. Whether the same kind of
  value (a record with numeric labels) is an array or an object depends on whether the labels
  are contiguous from 0, which the AI cannot see from the rule it is given. Loud failure, no
  wrong data: Low (L16, honest interface). The README's own Python example (`m[0] for m in
  meta`) relies on the undocumented array form.
- Fix: document the rule ("records whose fields are 0..n-1 are arrays, both ways") in README
  and both tool descriptions; test with a `record { text; nat }` reply.

###### SW5-7-2 details

- Where: `icp_code_mode.did:61` and `src/lib.rs:20`. README.md:54 and :148 use
  `printf %s "$MCP_TOKEN" | shasum -a 256 | cut -d' ' -f1`.
- Repro (macOS, dummy token `dummy-token`, nothing sent anywhere):
  `sh -c 'echo -n "$1" | shasum -a 256' _ dummy-token` gives `1b9742e5…`;
  `sh -c 'printf %s "$1" | shasum -a 256'` and `zsh -c 'echo -n …'` give `fe0c8f2d…`.
  `sh -c 'echo -n abc' | od -c` prints `- n   a b c \n` (`/bin/sh` is bash 3.2 in POSIX mode).
- Effect: an operator who scripts `InitArgs` or `add_api_token_hash` from the interface's own
  comment in a `sh` script or Makefile registers a digest no token matches. `add_token_hash`
  accepts any 64-hex string (`src/policy.rs:208-213`), so nothing flags it until clients get
  401. Fails closed; the operator is misled about why. Low (L16).
- Fix: use the README's `printf %s … | cut -d' ' -f1` recipe in the `.did` and `lib.rs`.

###### SW5-7-3 details

- Where: `video/capture-demo.mjs:7` (`.match(/^MCP_TOKEN=(.*)$/m)[1].trim()`), `video/tts.mjs:11`
  (`.match(/^GEMINI_API_KEY=(.+)$/m)…trim().replace(/^["']|["']$/g, "")`).
- Repro: a scratch `.env` with dummy values `MCP_TOKEN="dummy"` and `GEMINI_API_KEY="dummykey"`, run
  through the two regexes copied from 295d64b: `{"capture_demo_token":"\"dummy\"","tts_key":"dummykey"}`.
  The real `.env` was not read.
- Effect (C): the page sends `Authorization: Bearer "dummy"`, `authenticate` hashes the quoted
  text (`src/mcp.rs:266-290`) and answers 401. `capture-demo.mjs:24-37` does not check the
  comparison status, so it overwrites `video/assets/*.png` and `demo-results.json` with the
  error state and exits 0. An `export MCP_TOKEN=…` line (the README's quick-start form) does
  not match at all and the script crashes with a `TypeError` (loud). Dev tooling only: Low.
- Fix: one shared `.env` reader that strips `export` and quotes, falling back to
  `process.env.MCP_TOKEN`; fail if the page shows an error.

### grid-sweep-r5-8

#### Variant sweep r5-8: "Type information dropped at a boundary"

Pattern: a value or a fact about it (its type, kind, name, provenance or class) is known
on one side of a conversion and missing on the other, so the receiver cannot tell apart
cases that the sender kept apart. Searched every inventory row. Known findings from the
task's list are marked "known" and not raised again.

Evidence: the probe was run natively in a private `git archive` copy of 295d64b. The
crate version was bumped in the copy so the shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR could not reuse
another copy's build. The copy was deleted afterwards. Everything else is from reading
the code path.

##### New candidates

| Id | Row(s) | Result |
|---|---|---|
| SW58-1 | B7, B16, E5b, CL3 | **finding (reproduced).** `Service::parse` -> `candid_parser::check_prog` turns `IDLArgType { name, typ }` into bare `Type`s (typing.rs:75-96), and `search::signature` / `type_text` re-print that `TypeEnv`. Argument names, result names and every `//` doc comment of the target's .did are dropped. Probe output: `transfer : (from : principal, to : principal, amount : nat) -> (ok : bool)` with a doc comment is shown as `"signature": "(principal, principal, nat) -> (bool)"`. For the project's own demo_store, the comments that explain `list_products` (the valid category values), `list_orders` and `Inventory."reserved"` never reach the model through search. `icp.candid` still returns the full text. |
| SW58-2 | O1, U8, U9, B5/B6 path, E16-E19, CL15 (README:397-398) | **finding (code path).** `HostBridge::call` returns `Result<Value, String>`. ic-cdk's typed `CallFailed` and its `is_clean_reject()` classification are turned into text, and the reply-decode step (`svc.decode_reply`, bridge.rs:532) adds another failure to the same channel. Only one marker is added back: " (outcome unknown…)", and only when `call_timeout` is set (bridge.rs:529). With the default unbounded wait, a `CanisterReject` or `CanisterError` (ic-cdk: not clean, so the callee may have committed state) carries no marker. A decode failure after the target ran ("candid decoding failed: …" or "reply nested deeper…") carries none either. Scripts get the same `Error` (JS), `RuntimeError` (Python) or runtime string (Rhai) as a policy refusal that sent nothing. README:397-398 says whether the target executed is in the error ("a reject, or 'outcome unknown'"). |

<a id="grid-sweep-r5-9"></a>

### grid-sweep-r5-9

#### Variant sweep r5-9: same value, different precision in sibling runtimes

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 5. Pattern (seed: L7-16b / L11-3, known and not
re-reported: Python sees block time truncated to whole seconds, JS milliseconds, Rhai no
clock):

> The same value handled at different precision by sibling runtimes.

Question asked of every inventory row: is one value (a time, a number, a count, a length,
an identifier, a text) converted, measured or truncated by two or more sibling
implementations (the JS/Python/Rhai runtimes, query/update routes, metadata/tmp_hack fetch
paths, script/search runs, native/wasm32 builds, server/demo page), and does one of them
keep less of it than the others?

Known and not repeated (from the task list): L7-16b / L11-3 (clock seconds vs ms, Rhai no
clock), S4-7-1 (JS args 1 ulp via serde_json text), L7-3 (integral floats > 2^53),
L7-4 (NaN/Inf), L7-5 (float32 saturation), L7-17 (Python/Rhai ints 2^53..2^63 as numbers),
JS -0.0, UTF-16 vs UTF-8 text counting, JS key bytes, lone surrogates (three behaviours),
depth off by one, MAX_DEPTH Candid vs JSON levels, log cap raw vs escaped, Python print
cap, blob element counting, register R1 refutation (numbers vs decimal strings by
magnitude is deliberate).

##### Method

- Read every conversion site in `src/` for the three runtimes (`js.rs` snapshot,
  `to_json_safe`, `display`, `from_json`; `python.rs` `to_json`/`from_json`, OsPolicy;
  `rhai_rt.rs` `to_json_value`, `to_dynamic`), `candid_bridge.rs` (`num_text`, `float`,
  `big`, `f64_json`, `key_matches`, variant tag match), `bridge.rs` (`now_ms`,
  `normalize_numbers`, `instruction_deadline`, `truncate`, TTL arithmetic), `lib.rs`
  (`run_search`/`run_script` audit values, `inspect_message`), `mcp.rs` (`authenticate`,
  `truncate_escaped`), `policy.rs` (`audit_page`, `verify_token`), `search.rs`,
  `demo_store/src/lib.rs`, `src/demo.html`.
- Dependency source: Boa 0.22 `JSON.parse` (serde_json only validates; values come from
  Boa's own parser), Monty 1.6 `time` module and `OsPolicy` defaults (`ProcessTime::Zero`,
  zone UTC), Monty `json.loads` via jiter 0.17 (`lexical-parse-float`, correctly rounded),
  Rhai 1.27 serializer (`serialize_u64` -> INT when it fits, else FLOAT; unreachable here).
- One native probe (R): private copy without `target/`, `.git`, `design/`, `.env`, `.icp`,
  `video/`, the uncommitted plan doc; `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/audit-target`;
  `cargo test --lib sweep_r5_9 -- --nocapture`; copy deleted afterwards. The test ran the same
  number literal in JS, Python and Rhai through `LanguageRouter::execute` with `MockBridge`
  (which echoes the `owner` argument back as the reply), and recorded the result, the sent
  argument and the printed line. Nothing deployed, nothing called on the local network.

Probe output (native):

| literal | JS result / sent / log | Python | Rhai |
|---|---|---|---|
| `5.0` | `5` / `5` / `5` | `5.0` everywhere | `5.0` everywhere |
| `0.1+0.2` | `0.30000000000000004` in all three, all channels | same | same |
| `9007199254740991` | exact everywhere | exact | exact |
| `2**53` | `9007199254740992.0` (result, sent, log) | `9007199254740992` | `9007199254740992` |
| `1e16`, `1e21`, `1e300` | `1e+16` etc. | `1e+16` etc. | result `1e+16`, log `1e16` |
| `0.000001` | `1e-6`, log `1e-6` | `1e-6`, log `1e-06` | `1e-6`, log `0.000001` |
| `0.10000000149011612` | exact everywhere | exact | exact |
| `123456.789`, `-5` | exact everywhere | exact | exact |

Every value round-tripped (script -> args -> reply -> script -> result) to the same f64 or
integer in all three runtimes; only the text spelling of the same value differs (JS prints
integral floats as integers below 2^53 and as `N.0` above; print formats differ per
language). No precision is lost outside the known S4-7-1 text round trip, which these
literals happen not to hit. Off-pattern observation from the same probe: Python's captured
output is split with `str::lines`, so `print('a\r\nb\rc')` is logged as `["a", "b\rc"]`
(the `\r` of the CRLF is dropped), where JS keeps `"a\r\nb\rc"`; text fidelity of a log line,
not precision, Low, not raised as a candidate.

##### Candidates

None new. Every hit of the pattern found in this sweep is one of the known findings listed
above.

##### Cells

R = reproduced (probe above), C = code path.

### grid-sweep-r5-10

#### Variant sweep r5-10: a precision rule applied on one path and not its sibling

Run `2026-11-17-295d64b`, Phase 6, round 5. Pattern:

> A precision rule applied on one path and not its sibling.

Question asked of every inventory row: where a value is converted with an exactness rule
(the JS-safe integer rule, a single correctly rounded conversion, a time resolution, a
canonical form), is the same rule applied on every sibling path that carries the same
kind of value: argument vs result, text vs number, one runtime vs another, one numeric
width vs another, query vs update?

Known and not repeated: L7-3 / L5r2-4 (integral floats > 2^53 accepted as exact ints),
S4-7-1 (JS args text round trip, 1 ulp), L7-4 (NaN/Infinity -> null), L7-5 (float32
saturation/underflow, float text overflow), L7-9 (JSON-RPC ids), L7-12 (lenient numeric
text), L7-16 / L7-16b (raw string results; Python clock in whole seconds), L7-17 (Python /
Rhai ints 2^53..2^63 as JSON numbers), -0.0 sign dropped by JS, S10-2 (non-finite float
replies as strings), UTF-16 vs UTF-8 text counting, log cap units.

Evidence: **R** = reproduced, **C** = code path. Probe: private copy
`/private/tmp/claude-501/sweep-r5-10.HQbD` (`git archive 295d64b`, no `target/`, no
uncommitted files), `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/audit-target`, throwaway test
module `candid_bridge::sweep_r5_10` (deleted with the copy). Dependency source read for
Boa 0.22 `JsValue::from_json`/`to_json`, Monty 1.6.0 `modules/time.rs`.

##### New candidate S5-10-1: float32 slots round twice; float64 slots round once (R)

`json_to_idl` turns every float input into an f64 first (`float()`, `candid_bridge.rs:170-176`:
`Number::as_f64` or `str::parse::<f64>`) and then narrows with `as f32`
(`candid_bridge.rs:216`). For a `float64` slot that is one correctly rounded conversion. For
a `float32` slot it is two roundings (decimal or integer -> f64 -> f32), so an input that
lies just off a float32 midpoint is first rounded onto the midpoint and then tie-broken to
the even neighbour: the sent float32 is not the nearest one. JS is not affected (its value is
already an f64); Python and Rhai integers and every decimal string are.

`cargo test --lib sweep_r5_10 -- --nocapture` (native, same pure-Rust code as the wasm):

| Input to `float32` | Sent | Correctly rounded |
|---|---|---|
| `"1.0000001788139343261718749"` (text) | `1.0000002` (bits `3f800002`) | `1.0000001` (bits `3f800001`) |
| `1152921573326323713` = 2^60+2^36+1 (Python or Rhai int, a JSON i64) | `1.1529215e18` (`5d800000`) = 2^60 | `1.1529216e18` (`5d800001`) |
| Same text to a `float64` slot | correctly rounded (equal) | |

Of 200,000 decimal texts within ~1e-40 relative of a float32 midpoint (`{:.40e}` of the
midpoint), 39,176 were sent as the other neighbour than `str::parse::<f32>` gives. The run
reports Ok; nothing tells the script. Impact: 1 float32 ulp, only for inputs near a
midpoint; float32 is rare in ICP interfaces. Severity Low. Fix: parse text with
`str::parse::<f32>` for float32, and convert integers (`as_i64`/`as_u64`, big-int strings)
straight to f32 instead of through f64; add the two rows above as a test. Merge candidate:
same line as L7-5 (`as f32`), different mechanism (double rounding, not overflow).

<a id="grid-sweep-r5-11"></a>

### grid-sweep-r5-11

#### Variant sweep r5-11

Pattern: "Per-run cost or limit accounting done on a process-wide resource (thread-local GC
heap, global GC threshold) that concurrent or earlier runs also occupy." Stated generally: a
number that is meant to describe one run (its instruction budget, memory limit, audit
`instructions`, call cap, log cap) is read from a counter or structure that other runs, or
process-wide one-time work, also move.

Method: code reading at `295d64b` (C = code path). For every place a per-run limit or audit
figure is computed, I traced which counter it reads and who else moves that counter:
`grep` for `instruction_counter`, `performance_counter`, `call_context`, `LIVE_MEMORY`,
`BASELINE`, `force_collect`, `thread_local!`, `static` over `src/`, `shims/`, `demo_store/src/`;
and for process-wide statics (`thread_local!`, `static` atomics/`LazyLock`/`OnceLock`/
`OnceCell`/`Mutex`) in the shipped engines and libraries: `boa_engine`/`boa_gc`/`boa_string`
0.22.0, `monty`/`monty-types` 1.6.0, `rhai` 1.27.0, `candid` 0.10.40, `candid_parser` 0.4.1,
`ic-cdk-executor` 2.0.0. Nothing was built or run (no step needed it).

Result: **no new candidate.** Known hits: the Boa GC finding (L8-1, threshold and
`force_collect`), the Python reply credit (L8-2), the shared 40B per-message limit for a batch,
the process-wide run-slot pool, the Symbol.for registry, the getrandom stream position, the
shared negative interface cache. Everything else either reads a per-run or per-call-context
counter that only this run moves, or is a one-time, bounded process-wide cost.

##### Counters behind per-run limits and audit figures

| Row | Per-run figure | Counter / structure it reads | Who else moves it | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LIM2 instruction budget, JS (`check_budget` `js.rs:388`, `BoundedJobs::tick` `js.rs:115`, `budget()` in host fns) | `deadline = base + max` | `call_context_instruction_counter` (`bridge.rs:128-130`) | Only this HTTP request's call context. Batch items run strictly in sequence (`mcp.rs:386-402`, `exec(..).await` per item), and `base_instructions` is taken when each item's `IcBridge` is created (`bridge.rs:318`) | holds for this pattern, except work done inside the run for other runs: Boa GC = **known** (L8-1) |
| LIM2, Rhai (`on_progress` -> `budget_error(deadline)` `rhai_rt.rs:146-155`) | same deadline | same counter | same | holds (C). No shared GC: Rhai values are refcounted per run; `Engine` and `StandardPackage` are built per run (`rhai_rt.rs:118-120`) |
| LIM2/LIM26, Python (`vm_budget` `python.rs:37-43`, Monty clock = web-time `Instant`) | feed/turn budget | web-time shim `Instant::now()` = `performance_counter(1)` (`shims/web-time/src/lib.rs:15-18`), i.e. the same call-context counter; Monty only measures its running windows | Nothing else runs inside a Monty running window (single thread, synchronous) | holds for this pattern; one-time budget capture and turn-cap resets are **known** |
| LIM2, search (`run_search` `lib.rs:153-156`) | `instructions_used()` vs `max_instructions` | call-context counter from the search's own `IcBridge` | Sequential with the other batch items | holds (C) |

| LIM26 Python 64 MiB (`probe_memory` = `LIVE_MEMORY - BASELINE_MEMORY`, `monty-types resource.rs:825-829`) | live bytes | process-wide `LIVE_MEMORY` fed by the counting allocator (`lib.rs:357-425`) | Every allocation of every run and of the host. `rebased` (`python.rs:151-157`) re-bases around every await; nothing else executes inside a Monty synchronous window; `allocate_into_baseline` is not called anywhere in monty 1.6.0 | holds for other runs' allocations (register #43 fix); own reply excluded = **known** (L8-2) |
| LIM1 call cap | `slots` per `IcBridge` | per-run `Cell` (`bridge.rs:311-360`) | none | holds (C); cache-state dependence = **known** (concurrent cache misses / fetch slot) |
| LIM12 run slots | `ACTIVE_RUNS` | process-wide by design | every caller | **known** (one token holder can fill the pool; slots held during unbounded waits) |
| LIM14, LIM15, LIM16, LIM25, LIM27, Rhai `MAX_REQUESTS` | violations, log bytes, value budgets, promise jobs, rounds, replays | per-run structs (`IcBridge`, JS `State`/`BoundedJobs`, Rhai `RunState`, `ValueBudget` per conversion, Monty `PrintWriter` limit) | none | holds (C) |
| LIM24 Boa loop/recursion/stack limits | per run | Boa `RuntimeLimits` and VM stack per `Context` | none; per-frame loop counting is **known** | holds for this pattern |
| LIM20/LIM21 decode quota/depth | per decode | candid `DecoderConfig` per call | none | holds (C) |
| LIM18 / V2 / V4 / V5 interface caches | cost of fetch + parse charged to whichever run misses | process-wide caches | earlier runs warm them | holds for this pattern: the run that misses really does the work (not work done for another run). Outcome depending on cache state is the known call-cap/no-single-flight finding; negative cache shared across callers is **known** |

##### Process-wide state in the engines and libraries (V7-V10)

| Row | Item | Can it charge one run for others, or carry a per-run limit over? | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| V8 | `boa_gc` `BOA_GC` heap and threshold (`boa_gc-0.22.0/src/lib.rs:44-45`) | yes | **known** (L8-1, L8-6) |
| V10 | Boa `GLOBAL_SYMBOL_REGISTRY` (`builtins/symbol/mod.rs:41`) | grows across runs | **known** (Symbol.for registry) |
| V10 | Boa `FutexWaiters` static (`builtins/atomics/futex.rs:253`) | would hold waiters across runs | holds: unreachable, `Atomics` and `SharedArrayBuffer` are deleted from the global (`js.rs:314`, test `js.rs:428`); no other path reaches `Atomics` |
| V10 | Boa `SYMBOL_HASH_COUNT` atomic, `CODEBLOCK_ID_COUNTER`, `CANNOT_BLOCK_COUNTER`, `RecursionLimiter::SEEN` (Debug fmt only) | ids/counters, no limit is computed from them | holds (no accounting reads them) |
| V10 | Boa `RAW_STATICS_CACHE` (`boa_string common.rs:231`), Monty `CORE_ENTRIES` (`intern.rs:2823`), `INT_MAX_STR_DIGITS_THRESHOLD` (`long_int.rs:60`), `DEFAULT_OS_POLICY`, `RESERVED_STRING_HASHES` (129 atomics), Rhai `HASHING_SEED`/`INDEXER_HASHES` | built lazily by the first run that needs them, so that run's instructions (and, for Monty, its 64 MiB count) include a one-time cost later runs skip | holds (low, no failure): fixed size, built from constants, once per install/upgrade; far below the 20B budget and 64 MiB. Not a candidate under the evidence rule |
| V10 | candid `ENV`/`ID`/`NAME` thread-locals (`types/internal.rs:747-752`) | used by typed `CandidType` encoding; the app decodes/encodes untyped `IDLArgs` against parsed `TypeEnv`s | holds (no per-run figure depends on them) |
| V9 | `ic-cdk-executor` `TASKS`/`PROTECTED_WAKEUPS`/`MIGRATORY_WAKEUPS` | could poll another task inside this run's execution | holds: the app spawns no tasks (`grep spawn` empty in `src/`); each HTTP request is one protected task, woken only by its own call futures, so the call-context counter of a run never includes another request's polling |
| V7 | getrandom `STATE` (`lib.rs:437`) | shared stream | **known** (position carries over between runs); no limit reads it |
| V6 | Monty `LIVE_MEMORY` / `BASELINE_MEMORY` | see LIM26 above | holds / **known** L8-2 |
| V1, V3 | `ACTIVE_RUNS`, `PENDING_RUNS` | process-wide by design | **known** findings only |
